- `<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch/` (outside the repository, a sibling of it): the host mutation scratch, where on a Windows host `run --mutants` puts cargo-mutants' temp copies and its `--output`; a guard refuses any other final component or a repository inside it, never a fallback to `%TEMP%` or the repo, and its path is never printed. Off Windows the harness arm is inert.
**Docker volumes, containers, service names:** none.

title: Infrastructure Patterns

body: Contracts: .andromeda/registries/architecture-contracts.toml — ask registry.py contracts; read one contracts/architecture/{key}.md; never whole.

title: Cross-cutting Patterns

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/cross-cutting-patterns.md — read whole.

- **Config management.** Precedence: CLI flags override `<viola home>/config.json`, which overrides built-in defaults. The viola home resolves `--home`, then the grandparent of `VIOLA_DIR`, then `<user home>/.viola/`; `config.json` is parsed tolerantly and carries `v`. There are no secrets in v1, and environment variables are not a configuration channel: a dependency or feature that reads one breaks this rule like a direct read does.
- **Development Style signal:** agent-driven.

- **Identity by instance, never by location.** Every hook, MCP call and CLI verb finds its instance through `VIOLA_NAME` (or an explicit `ViolaName` argument), never through the working directory. Two sessions in one folder never share records.

- **Fail open toward the human.** Any internal failure in `hook` produces exit 0 with no body, so the dialog renders for the human. Any failure to confirm delivery is reported as `not-delivered`, never retried blindly. The one exception is a local command on the ledger whose post-condition is "none" or not yet measured on this CLI version. It is reported as `ok` with `confirmed: false` and detail `unconfirmable`.

- **Mixed-version tolerance.** Every channel `params`, event, snapshot and config carries `v`, and channel `params` also carry the sender's `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. Readers skip unknown kinds and fields and surface the counts. A newer request than the wrapper supports gets a `-32602` naming the wrapper's version.

- **Capability ledger as the single gate for CLI-specific behaviour.** Any new dependence on an undocumented `claude` behaviour is added as a ledger row in `viola-agent-claude`, with a `viola verify` probe that has a post-condition check; it is never hard-coded as an unconditional assumption. One ruled limit: a CLI shape no `send` relies on needs no probe.

- **Tokio containment.** New code on the `run`, `hook`, `send` or channel-server paths uses std threads and blocking I/O. Only `viola-mcp` may build a runtime. CLI `wait` is a blocking read on `viola-channel`'s sync client.

- **Crash-safe disk writes.** Append-only logs use one `write` per line. Mutable files are replaced atomically. Every guarded file has its own `.lock` sibling. Readers always tolerate a torn last line.

- **Diagnostic output channels.** `hook` writes only its decision body to stdout and nothing to stderr; on the `hook statusline` pass-through stdout carries the user's status line output instead, and nothing else, and its `--capture` probe arm prints nothing (Hook Contract). While the child runs, `run` writes nothing to the terminal except the child's own output, because the terminal carries the child's screen. Every role's codes-only process log goes to its home-level role file under `diagnostics/`: `run-<name>`, `hook-<name>`, `mcp` or `cli-<name>` `.ndjson`. Content-bearing detail belongs only in the instance's `diagnostics/detail-<role>.ndjson`. `mcp` writes only MCP frames to stdout, and its log goes to `diagnostics/mcp.ndjson`; it writes JSON to stderr only when that file cannot be opened. Short-lived CLI verbs may use stderr for their human output. The logger and the format are owned by obs.

- **Cross-platform discipline.**
  - Every path written into plugin files uses forward slashes.
  - Nothing shells out through `sh`, `bash` or `cmd`, except `hook statusline` running the user's own statusline command (see Hook contract).
  - Child processes are spawned directly.
  - Endpoint names are hashed and short.
  - Every OS-specific branch compiles and is tested on its CI runner.
- **Untrusted upstream text.** A driven session's `Stop` text and dialog payloads are content, never commands to viola. viola forwards them as escaped strings and never interprets them (R1).

- **Bounded readers.** Every product reader of external bytes is bounded in its own statement (`take`) or named as an exception (the own-executable reads); the contract binary `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` enumerates the boundaries and censuses the product sources.

- **Local endpoint trust boundary.** Any process that can open an instance's endpoint can `send` prompts and `answer` dialogs, including PermissionRequest. v1 trusts every process of the same OS user and no other. Each endpoint, whether a named pipe or a Unix socket file, must not be connectable by another OS user. The security specialist owns how this is enforced per OS and any per-connection proof beyond it.

title: Project Intent

body: - **Core function.** Lets one interactive Claude Code session drive another on the user's own subscription. It wraps the unmodified `claude` CLI in a PTY, types at turn boundaries, answers dialogs through hooks, and holds a one-driver wheel the human can take at any moment.
- **Growth model.** Modular monolith: one binary with compiler-enforced internal crates (`pty · channel · state · agent-claude · mcp` around `core`), and no daemon.

- **How new functionality is added.**
  - New capabilities arrive as new subcommands or channel verbs, exposed consistently on the CLI (`--json`) and, where a driver needs them, as MCP tools.
  - New Claude behaviours arrive as capability-ledger rows in `viola-agent-claude`.
  - A second driven agent (for example Codex) arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.
- **Template patterns.** None. This is a single-product repository, not a fleet.

- **Scale path.**
  - v1 is personal (first live on the Linux dev host, by the founder's ruling R-L1; Windows, macOS and Linux CI-tested against the fake agent; Windows live awaits an interactive Windows host).
  - v1.x adds public distribution (dist 0.33.0 releases, signing, winget/Homebrew/Scoop, a marketplace entry, self_update 1.3.0).
  - A phone or remote view comes later, behind authentication.

title: Inherited Defaults

body: - Framework: Rust 1.98.1, pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml` (MSRV 1.96, edition 2024). A sync std-thread core; Tokio 1.53.3 only in `mcp`; rmcp 3.4.1 for MCP; clap 4.6.7 for the CLI.
- Database: none. ndjson append logs + atomic JSON snapshots (tempfile 3.27.0 `persist` through one shared helper) + std `File::lock`, serde_json 1.0.151.
- IPC: interprocess 2.4.4 local sockets, one endpoint per `viola run`, JSON-RPC 2.0 over ndjson with `v` + sender version in every `params`.
- API style: typed `RefusalReason` in `result.refusal`.

- Errors: thiserror 2.0.20, one enum per crate (except `viola-pty`'s hand-written `PtyError`; `viola-mcp`'s `ServeError` beside `McpError` and `viola-state`'s `StampsError` beside `StateError` are open divergences, with `PinError`, `StampsReadError` and `Refused` the three the census adds, [Error Handling]), anyhow 1.0.104 only in the root bin; typed CLI exit codes; `viola hook` always exits 0.
- Validation: tolerant serde for external payloads, versioned-tolerant own formats, nutype 0.8.0 newtypes.
- Timestamps: chrono 0.4.45, RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds and `Z`, field `ts` / `*_at`.
- Agent isolation: Claude-specific shapes only in `viola-agent-claude`, and every undocumented behaviour is a capability-ledger row.
- Deployment: local `cargo install --path .`, plugin embedded in the binary and loaded with `--plugin-dir`; no containers, no hosting.
- CI: GitHub Actions on windows-2025 / macos-latest / ubuntu-latest against the fake agent.
- Development Style: agent-driven.

- Publishability: every workspace crate, including the root `viola` bin, sets `publish = false` and inherits `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` from `[workspace.package]`. Nothing is published to crates.io in v1.

- **`RefusalReason` (serialised kebab-case):** `human-typing` · `budget-paused` · `unverified-cli` · `not-delivered` · `unknown`. `unknown` is `#[serde(other)]`, so an older client can still read a refusal from a newer wrapper. `detail` values are kebab-case strings from a closed set per reason, extended only in `viola-core`:
  - `human-typing`: `null` · `manual-pause`
  - `budget-paused`: `five-hour` · `seven-day`
  - `unverified-cli`: `null`
  - `not-delivered`: `input-not-ready` · `no-prompt-submitted` · `turn-running` · `unknown-dialog` · `control-character` · `empty-text`
  - `unknown`: a code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`) or `null`

  Readers treat an unrecognised code-word `detail` as opaque text, never as an error. When several refusals apply, the wrapper returns only the first in this order. For `send`: `not-delivered`/`control-character` first (`viola_core::validate_paste_text`: LF, CR and TAB pass; every other C0, DEL and C1 is refused, never stripped; the CLI checks before any frame and the wrapper checks again), then `not-delivered`/`empty-text` (the typed text, the text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters ([Delivery Confirmation]), is empty; the CLI checks before any frame and the wrapper checks again, before the first wheel read; a text that also holds a refused character is still `control-character`), then `human-typing`, `budget-paused`, `not-delivered`/`turn-running` (a turn running, or another `send` in flight), then the readiness gate (`input-not-ready`, also when no child has started), then `human-typing` and `not-delivered`/`turn-running` read a second time once the gate has returned ready, and then the confirmation (`no-prompt-submitted`) outcome. A paste that fails after `send-issued` is `input-not-ready` with that send's `cursor`. For `answer`: `not-delivered`/`control-character` first (`validate_paste_text` on the response's free text; the CLI checks before any frame and the wrapper checks again), then `human-typing`, `unverified-cli`, `not-delivered`/`unknown-dialog`. `unconfirmable` is not a refusal detail. It appears only in an `ok` payload (`{"confirmed":false,"detail":"unconfirmable"}`), for a ledger-listed local command whose post-condition is "none" or not yet measured on this CLI version.
- **Code word:** `viola_core::is_code_word(&str) -> bool`: 1 to 64 bytes of `[a-z0-9-]`, a lower-case letter first; `reply_of` and `of_reply` call it.
- **A peer's reply:** `reply_of` and `of_reply` read a `refusal` that is no code word as `unknown`, a string `detail` that is no code word as `null`, and a non-string `detail` as no known reply.

- **Unreachable cause:** `viola_core::UnreachableCause` (`StrictModes` · `InstanceDead` · `UnwrappedName` · `EndpointLost` · `ServerVerify` · `SocketDir`, each word through `as_str`, `SocketDir`'s `socket-dir-refused`) is exit 21's closed cause set.   - `2` usage error (clap, a second positional to `viola send` included; never produced by `viola hook`), and `viola send` text over `MAX_FRAME` or not UTF-8 (`error: the text must be readable UTF-8 of at most 16 MiB`)
  - `10` `human-typing`

  - `14` `unknown` refusal

The start's refusal (exit `1`, above) is a step with no span and one line.

- **MCP:** a success is a tool result with `isError: false` and the channel `ok` payload as `structuredContent` (for `list`, the caller-side `{items, budget, skipped}` payload, the `list` payload of Standard Contracts). A refusal is a tool result with `isError: true` and the same `refusal` + `detail` in `structuredContent`. An unreachable instance and a wrapper protocol fault are also `isError: true` tool results. Their `structuredContent` is `{"error":"instance-unreachable"|"wrapper-fault","detail":…}`, the same as CLI `--json` (`instance-unreachable` with `detail` its cause word, `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`; `wrapper-fault` with the JSON-RPC fault's `{code,message,data}` as `viola_channel::sanitised_fault` reads it: a fixed `message`, `data` a closed object or null). As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): each handler re-validates its raw argument object (`target` through `ViolaName::try_new`, `text` a string, `after` / `timeout_ms` absent, `null` or a `u64`, `dialog_id` a `u64`, `response` an object through `Response::parse`), and a failure is an `isError: true` result `{"error":"invalid-params","detail":"<field>"}` (the closed field words `target` · `text` · `after` · `timeout_ms` · `dialog_id` · `response`) with no frame written; every `isError` text is `refused: <code>`. JSON-RPC errors are the MCP connection's own faults, an unknown tool name (`-32602`) and an internal handler fault — any other channel error, a reply of no known shape, a `wait` / `last` refusal, a panicked call — which is `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null`. `tools/list`'s result carries `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private`: claude 2.1.287 negotiates protocol `2026-07-28` and drops every tool of a list result without them (as measured live at that chunk, `evidence/live-mcp.md` start 1).
 claude 2.1.302 on that protocol opens with `server/discover` (its JSON-RPC id a string) and then `tools/list`, each carrying `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`, `…/clientInfo`, `…/clientCapabilities`), and sends no `initialize` or `notifications/initialized`; viola's two results each carry `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private` (as measured live at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii/evidence/live-tap.md`, start 2). - **[Database / State Store] ndjson append logs + atomic JSON snapshots + std `File::lock` on separate `.lock` files (KEYSTONE).** Each event line is written with one `write` call. The next append heals a torn last line; readers count it and never rewrite the log. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state): every appender (`append_event`, `append_event_at`, `try_append_event`) reads the log's last byte under the lock it already holds and, when the log is not empty and that byte is not LF, writes one LF and its line in a single write. The line then starts on a fresh line, no earlier byte moves, and every offset handed out before still starts the same line; `append_event_at` hands its builder and returns the offset its line really starts at (L + 1 after a heal, L otherwise). The healing process logs one `state-recovered` line, and an append that did not heal logs none. The one reader (`viola_state::events::read_from`: the wrapper's `wait` scan and `last` rebuild, `replay::session_chain`, the pass `viola revive` reads the logged session ids from, and since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the wrapper's link-set restore at start, `LinkSet::restore`, one pass from offset 0, and since chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::log_pass`, one pass from offset 0 per scanned instance whose snapshot read or was absent) counts what it steps over, per read, as `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`: a line whose `kind` it does not know is not returned (`link` and `unlink` are known kinds since that chunk, returned and no longer counted); a known-kind line with a top-level key outside the six, or a `data` key outside its kind's list, is returned and counted once; an over-long line, a terminated line that is not one JSON object and the unterminated last line of the read count as torn, the last still neither returned nor rewritten.
 The counts are not logged. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. The wheel is decided in the wrapper's memory and mirrored to a snapshot. Budget readings are timestamped, last-writer-wins, under `File::lock`. Rationale: the audit trail stays human-readable and `tail`-able, there is no C in the build, and there is no daemon to serialise writers. SQLite (C build, binary format) and redb (multi-process mode hardened only 2026-09-06) were rejected. Lock files are separate from logs because append + exclusive lock fails on Windows (rust-lang/rust#54118). Upgrade path if a real query need appears: a derived, rebuildable SQLite index (rusqlite) beside the authoritative log. The log stays the source of truth.

- **[Snapshot writer] tempfile 3.27.0 `persist` and `persist_noclobber` through the shared helpers of `viola_state::fs`.** `viola_state::fs::replace_private` creates the temp file beside the target, sets its mode before any byte is written (0600), writes, `sync_all`s and `persist`s; a failure leaves the target as it was. On Windows a `persist` refused with raw OS error 5 (a reader holding the target open, as measured at chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events research.md M1 under every share mode) is retried every 10 ms, re-persisting the same temp file, at most `viola_state::fs::REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` = 100 attempts (an attempt count, never a time bound); any other error returns at once. The loop sits in the private `replace_private_retrying`, which takes the decision to retry a failed rename (from its raw OS error) from its caller; `replace_private_with` passes `retry_replace(_, HOST_IS_WINDOWS)`, so the product's behaviour is the one above and the loop's attempt bound is exercised by a unit case on every host (chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors). `replace_private_shared` is the variant for files every concurrent start of one version writes identically (the plugin files, the Windows x64 ConPTY companions under `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/`): a replace that fails counts as done when the target already holds exactly those bytes. The pinned copy's absent-copy write is never a replace: it is the no-clobber `place_private_new` (below). The companions' held open (`FILE_SHARE_READ` only) retries a Win32 error 32 (sharing violation) under the same `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` bound (`retry_open`, `open_held_waiting`), as measured at chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty: two concurrent first starts, the refusal lasting 5-11 ms after the other start's write, 0 of 6 pairs over companions already written. No call site carries its own temp + rename code.
 Rationale: atomic-write-file 0.3.1 was the first choice, but its licence is BSD-3-Clause, outside `deny.toml`'s allow list (operator ruling at the 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order plan); tempfile was already locked, MIT OR Apache-2.0.

- `viola_state::fs::place_private_new(path, bytes, mode) -> Result<Placed, StateError>` (public enum `Placed { Written, Present }`) is the no-clobber placement, the pinned copy's absent-copy write (`viola_state::pin::place_absent`): it creates a temp file beside the target (`NamedTempFile::new_in`), sets its mode before any byte (the pinned `viola` at `DIR_MODE`), writes the bytes, `sync_all`s, closes the write handle (`into_temp_path`) and calls `TempPath::persist_noclobber`. `AlreadyExists` is `Ok(Placed::Present)`, the target untouched and the temp path removed; any other failure is an error that leaves the target as it was. It has no retry and no error variant of its own.

- Its body, the private `place_private_new_with(path, bytes, mode, placed)`, runs its `placed` hook right after a `Written` placement: a forced-window test parameter, not a seam (no env read, no feature). `place_private_new_placed_copy_execs_at_once` execs the placed copy from it on Unix, and `place_private_new_placed_copy_runs_at_once` runs it on Windows.

- The write handle is closed before the placement because `NamedTempFile::persist` renames while that handle is still open, and a concurrent first start's agent exec of a copy still open for write fails `ETXTBSY` (raw errno 26): 4 of 24 two-instance boots failed so through the open-handle rename and 0 of 24 through `place_private_new` (as measured on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds/evidence/race-before.md` and `evidence/race-after.md`).

- **[Message Broker / IPC] interprocess 2.4.4 `local_socket`, one endpoint per `viola run`, behind viola's own `channel` seam.** `hook` blocks on the channel for a dialog answer. `wait` blocks until the next driver-relevant event (`turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end` or `dialog-expired`) and returns that event, so nothing polls and a driver parked in `wait` learns that a dialog is pending. If a dialog is already pending when `wait` is called without `after`, or with an `after` at or before that dialog's event line, it returns that dialog at once (as landed by 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id: `hook.dialog` is served, the dialog line is appended and signalled through `WaitFeed::appending_dialog` and cleared through `WaitFeed::dialog_settled`). With an `after` past that line the driver has already seen the dialog, so `wait` blocks for the next driver-relevant event, and a driver that leaves a dialog to the human never spins. Each dialog event carries a wrapper-assigned `dialog_id` (an integer, monotonic per instance, with the counter restored from `events.ndjson` on start so an id never repeats across wrapper restarts), and `answer` names its target by that id. At most one dialog is pending per instance. A `hook.dialog` that arrives while another is pending is answered `null` at once, so that dialog renders for the human. Its event is still logged with its own `dialog_id`, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` with detail `unknown-dialog`. Whether Claude Code can hold two dialog hooks open at once (for example on parallel tool calls) is a capability-ledger row. `wait` takes an optional `after` cursor and an optional `timeout_ms`. `after` is a byte offset into the instance's `events.ndjson`.
 `wait` returns the first driver-relevant event whose line starts at or after it, at once if that event is already logged, so a turn that ends before the driver calls `wait` is never missed. Every `send` `ok` payload and every `wait` event result carries `cursor`, the offset to pass as the next `after`. Without `after`, `wait` returns the next such event appended after the call. With no `timeout_ms` it blocks until an event arrives, and if the endpoint vanishes first the caller gets `instance-unreachable`, its `detail` `endpoint-lost`. On timeout it returns `ok` with `{"timed_out":true}`. `last` returns the `last_assistant_message` of the newest `turn-ended` event. The wrapper holds it in memory and rebuilds it from `events.ndjson` on start. Endpoint names are a short hash of the instance, never the raw `VIOLA_NAME` + path. On Windows the client connects only through the SQOS Identification open (windows-sys `CreateFileW` with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, adopted by `Stream::try_from`), never interprocess's default connect, so a squatted or rogue server cannot impersonate the client; a non-overlapped handle adopted this way hangs (as measured at chunk 2026-09-25-security-prerequisites). Rationale: one API over named pipes and Unix sockets, sync and Tokio flavours, and no daemon. macOS caps socket paths at about 104 bytes. Accepted risk: interprocess has one main maintainer, which the seam contains.

- No check sits inside `viola_channel::Client::connect`: `viola-channel` has no `viola-state` edge, and `channel_link_names_are_validated_by_the_wrapper` writes through that client past every check by design; the socket-directory check stands at the channel seam's callers.

- `viola_channel::Client::server_pid` and `tokio_client::TokioClient::server_pid` return the connected stream's peer pid through interprocess's `peer_creds().pid()`: Linux `SO_PEERCRED`, Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the client end the SQOS Identification open adopts, none on macOS, where `SERVER_PID_REPORTED` is false; they write and log nothing. Every frame-writing client compares that pid and the process's OS start time with the snapshot's before its first frame (§Standard Contracts, Channel methods), so on Linux and Windows a squatted or rogue server is never sent a frame either.

- `viola_channel` exports `peer_euid_admitted`, `peer_admitted` and `PEER_EUID_REPORTED`, the last `cfg!(unix)`: `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own, reported)` is `!reported || observed == Some(own)`, so a peer whose euid cannot be read is refused where it is reported, and on Windows the DACL and the pid comparison stay the controls. `Client::server_euid` and `TokioClient::server_euid` supply the observed euid, writing and logging nothing.

- The wrapper's `accept_loop` filters `incoming()` by `admitted(peer_euid_of(stream))`, so a refused stream is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and any frame, reading end-of-file, writing no line, nothing on the terminal and moving no wheel; `Server::serve` injects the decision, `peer_admitted`, as a `type Admission` through the private `serve_admitting`, with no env, flag or feature seam.

- On macOS no peer pid is reported, so `viola_state::liveness::server_verdict` returns `Matches` with no comparison: the recorded gap, named and owned by no route entry. The macOS client euid and socket-directory checks, and the 0755-directory exit-cause case, stand built, so on macOS `server-verify-failed` means an euid mismatch alone.

- `viola_state::strict::check_socket_dir` takes one `symlink_metadata`: an absent path passes, an unstattable one is `Refused::Unreadable`, then `socket_dir_verdict` reads a symlink as `Refused::Symlink`, a non-directory as the fixed-message `Refused::NotADirectory` and anything else by the read rule; it never chmods, a refused directory stays as found, and off Unix it returns `Ok(())`. `check_endpoint_dir` is that check on a recorded endpoint's parent.

- A verified client meets an unreadable or newer snapshot as an absent one, through `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` (§Standard Contracts, Snapshot envelope): a replayed snapshot holds no `endpoint`, so it gives no endpoint and no frame is written; no product reader under `src/` calls `read_snapshot`.

- `viola hook statusline`'s `serve` reads the snapshot through the replay too: a replayed snapshot holds no `statusline_command`, so nothing runs and nothing is printed. The replay's `state.snapshot_recover` span sits under `run.start` before `run.collision_check`, and under `hook.handle` on the hook path.

- **[MCP] rmcp 3.4.1, stdio, tools `send · wait · last · answer · list`. `release` is CLI-only.** Refusals are `isError: true` tool results mapped from `result.refusal`. Rationale: it is the official SDK, tracks spec 2026-07-28, and the pinned minor limits churn from its near-weekly releases. `answer` and `list` are how a driver answers dialogs under R7 and sees sessions, and the prototype driver uses both every session. `release` stays off the driver's tool surface, so a driver is never offered a way to hand the wheel back to automation. This is an affordance, not an enforcement: an agent's Bash tool can still run CLI `viola release` (for example through `VIOLA_BIN`), and the Local endpoint trust boundary accepts it because v1 trusts every process of the same OS user. The wrapper refuses a `release` whose `params` carry a string `from` (`-32602`, `data.reason` `release-from-driver`), so CLI `viola release` run inside a wrapped session (`VIOLA_NAME` set) is refused; `from` is self-reported (`from_trust:"self-reported"`), so this deters rather than enforces. `pause`, `link` and `unlink` are CLI-only for the same reason: they are human controls over the wheel and the link topology, and links made by drivers are already recorded from `from` on `send` and `answer`. Tool inputs:
  - `send {target, text}`
  - `wait {target, after?, timeout_ms?}`
  - `last {target}`

The event is lost rather than the turn delayed, and a driver recovers through `wait`'s `timeout_ms`.

- **[Budget Governor] Soft stop at the turn boundary.** Once a configured threshold is crossed (defaults `five_hour` ≥ 90 %, `seven_day` ≥ 85 %), automated `send` is refused with `budget-paused` through the same refusal path as `human-typing`. Human keys are never blocked, and a running turn finishes. The pause lifts when `resets_at` passes or on `viola release --budget`. `release --budget` leaves the wheel where it is, and a plain `release` returns the wheel to `driver` without lifting a budget pause. `release --budget` is sent to one instance's wrapper and lifts the pause for that instance only, until the crossed window's `resets_at` passes, so the next over-threshold reading does not re-pause it. The wrapper evaluates its gate from `budget.json`, read under `budget.json.lock`, at three points: at start, when a `send` arrives, and at each `turn-ended`. It never polls. A crossed threshold, a passed `resets_at` or an expired override takes effect at the next of these points, and only then is `budget-gate` appended. So a snapshot can still read `budget_paused: true` after the reset, until a `send` arrives or a turn ends, and every surface that shows the snapshot inherits that. The wrapper mirrors its budget-pause state, including any override, to the instance snapshot, where `list` reads it. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor; `src/run/budget.rs`, one `BudgetGate` per wrapper, no thread and no timer): a window is crossed only when its `used_percentage` is known and at or above its threshold and its `resets_at` is known, parses as RFC 3339 and is later than now, so a window whose `resets_at` is `"unknown"`, unparseable or passed never pauses. With both windows crossed the refusal names `five-hour`.
 The `send` point sits after the text refusals and the first `human-typing` read and before the running-turn read, so the order is `control-character` → `empty-text` → `human-typing` → `budget-paused` → `turn-running` → the readiness gate's wait; the gate is read once per `send`, never again after that wait. `answer`, `wait`, `last`, `pause` and `hook.dialog` do not read the gate (read in the diff: its five product call sites; since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the root case `path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone`, `tests/cli_budget.rs`, drives `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` under one closed gate, each giving the exit code and the document it gives under an open one; no case drives `hook.dialog` under a closed gate). An override covers both windows until its end and is dropped at the next point after that end. It does not outlive its wrapper: every start, a revived one included, evaluates from `budget.json` alone and restores none. `release --budget` with no pause standing records nothing. `budget-gate` is appended, and the snapshot's `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until` are rewritten, only when the triple (paused, window, override end) changes, both before the evaluation returns; a record that cannot land is an error and the recorded state stays as it was. The thresholds are read once, at the wrapper's start, and no value of either switches the gate off. The gate is fail-open: no reading, an `"unknown"` figure, a passed or unparseable `resets_at`, an unreadable or refused `budget.json` and a bad threshold each leave it open or at its default. The decision takes the wall-clock instant as an argument (no clock seam). With figures missing, viola uses the newest reading from any wrapped session and shows its age. Rationale: Git Bash rewrites `/skill` arguments into Windows paths (brief §6), and agents need machine-parseable refusals. `viola revive` takes `--json` on both arms (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): every refusal of its start, a refused strict-modes check and a preflight refusal among them, prints `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `batch-script-child` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`, a `claude` not on `PATH` or an anyhow error of the start being `internal-error`) in place of its `unable:` / `hint:` pair where it has one, exit 1, and `<name> --list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order; without `--json` the pairs and the `--list` rows are byte-identical. A `pump_child` error prints no document: the child has held the terminal.

- **Linux / macOS:** Unix domain socket file `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` in a per-user 0700 directory (security-plan arch amendment 2): `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` on Linux, `$TMPDIR/viola/` on macOS, and `/tmp/viola-<uid>/` only as a fallback; never the `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` root. `run` and `revive`'s start check that directory before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, creating it only when absent and checking it again, and the CLI frame verbs, `hook` and `mcp`'s frame tools check the recorded `endpoint`'s directory before they connect; a symlink, a non-directory, a foreign owner or any group or other bit is refused (`socket-dir-refused`) and left as found, the check never changing its mode. The socket is chmod 0600 after the bind. The start arbiter is the sibling `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.lock`: `run` holds an exclusive lock on it, and a held lock is the taken-name refusal. `run` resolves the path once and records it as `endpoint` in the instance snapshot. Every other process (`hook`, `mcp`, CLI verbs, and `run`'s collision check) connects to the recorded `endpoint`, because processes spawned inside the session may run with a different environment from the wrapper. Each reads the snapshot through `viola_state::replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, and only a snapshot read whole yields an `endpoint`, because one rebuilt from the log carries no `endpoint`, `pid` or `started_at`: on a replay, an absence or an error `live_endpoint` (the CLI frame verbs and `mcp`'s frame tools) returns none; on a replay or an absence hook `connect` is unreachable (fail open; SessionEnd appends directly); `run`'s collision check takes its caller's one read and decides a replay from the heartbeat alone (`already-live` within `STALE_AFTER`, else free) and an absence or an error as free. None rebuilds the path. Linux abstract-namespace names are never used, because they carry no filesystem permissions and any local user could connect (see Local endpoint trust boundary).

- A force-killed wrapper's socket file stays in the per-user directory until a next bind of that name takes it over; nothing removes it and no removal is owed, a choice: a harmless file in a 0700 directory.

- Before its first frame each process that connects to the recorded `endpoint`, but `run`'s collision check (`hook`'s event and dialog paths, the CLI frame verbs `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, and `mcp`'s four frame tools), checks that the process serving it is the snapshot's wrapper: the connected stream's peer pid (`viola_channel::Client::server_pid` / `TokioClient::server_pid`) and its OS start time against the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` (§Standard Contracts, Session liveness). Ahead of that comparison each checks the recorded `endpoint`'s directory (`viola_state::strict::check_endpoint_dir`) before it connects, a refusal reading `socket-dir-refused`, and then, on Unix, the connected peer's euid (`viola_channel::peer_admitted` over `Client::server_euid` / `TokioClient::server_euid`), a foreign euid or one it cannot read reading `server-verify-failed`. A mismatch or a check that cannot be made sends no frame: CLI exit 21 `instance-unreachable`, MCP `instance-unreachable`, the hook failing open. macOS reports no peer pid and stays on the recorded gap, owned by no route entry: there the pid and start-time comparison is absent and `server-verify-failed` means an euid mismatch alone.

 `verify` takes `[--record <DIR>] [-- <program> [args…]]` (program default `claude`). `list` takes `[--json]` and nothing else; it exits 0 with a board (one stdout write), 21 when its strict-modes check refuses the home, `instances/` or any one instance (the whole board refused), 1 for an internal error through the `cli` catch site and 2 for a clap usage error (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list). `plugin install` takes `[--json]` and nothing else (`viola plugin` alone is a clap usage error; clap's own `viola plugin help` is served); it exits 0 with its result (one stdout write), 21 when its strict-modes check refuses the home or any existing `marketplace/` tree dir (nothing created, no log opened), 1 for an internal error through the `cli` catch site and 2 for a clap usage error. `revive` takes `<name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [-- <child args>]`, or `<name> --list`, each with `[--json]`; under `--json` a refused strict-modes check and every refusal of its start is the exit-1 `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document (one of the eleven codes, §Standard Contracts) with stderr empty, and `--list --json` prints the `ok.sessions` document, or the `no-session` document with exit 1; it exits 0 when the revived child's wrapper ends as `run`'s does, 1 for a refused strict-modes check, a preflight refusal or a refusal of the start after a passed preflight and 2 for a clap usage error (a malformed `--id` included).

Neither arm writes the word `strict-modes-failed` on any line. `viola link` / `viola unlink` run `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>` before `client::start`, so before any role file or log opens and before any snapshot value is read; a refusal is exit 21 (`--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` document on stdout, stderr empty; human the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr), no line written and the mode left as found. That a refused check leaves no trace on the statusline arm is the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13). `check_instance` has these three product call sites (`src/cmd/hook.rs` `trusted`, shared by the statusline, event and dialog paths; `src/cmd/revive.rs`; and `src/cmd/client.rs` `refuse_untrusted`, shared by `link` / `unlink` and the six frame verbs; the rule: `check_instance(` under `src/`). Outside that rule `viola-mcp`'s `tools.rs` `frame` calls it, and `run`'s start reaches its set through `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree`.
 The check is proven on Unix (five widened modes). On Windows `cfg(windows)` cases prove it: an instance tree granted Users write is refused `Writable` beside a `create_private_dir` tree that passes, a `diagnostics/` granted Users read is refused, and a plain home made before viola is refused for its inherited write grant to a SID `trusted_sid` does not trust, read by its right whichever SID holds it, while a home `instance_tree()` makes reads none (as measured at ci#40439188053, `windows-2025`).

- `viola_state::strict` holds two rules. The read rule is the write rule plus, on Unix, a refusal of any group or other bit (`mode & 0o077`) and, on Windows, a refusal of any allow ACE, an inherit-only one included, that grants a right in `READ_RIGHTS` (`0x9000_0001`: `FILE_READ_DATA` | `GENERIC_READ` | `GENERIC_ALL`) to a SID `trusted_sid` rejects (`unix_read_verdict`, `windows_read_verdict`, `check_read`). `Refused` holds `Readable` for a read-rule refusal, `Symlink` for a symbolic link `check_diagnostics` or `check_socket_dir` meets and `NotADirectory` for a socket directory path that is no directory, each with a fixed message.

It checks only entries that exist and refuses as `TreeRefused::HomeLevel` or `TreeRefused::InstanceLevel`. `run`'s start and `viola revive`'s start call it through `checked_exe` (the instance's name and the `pin_key` of the exe bytes read once), and `verify` calls it with no name and no key.

The socket directory check at `client::connect`, hook `connect` and `mcp`'s `frame` is no part of this: it comes after the instance check, on the recorded `endpoint`, and its refusal writes the lines `diagnostics/`, above, states.

A window is the word `"unknown"` or `{used_percentage, resets_at}`, and either field may be `"unknown"`. It is replaced whole through `replace_private` at 0600 under an exclusive lock on `budget.json.lock` (`viola_state::budget::write_budget`).
