## 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup — verify's Ctrl-C / TERM stop, the owed literals moved, the Windows matrix line
**Section:** §Occupied Resources → Filesystem (`ledger/probes/<pid>/`, verify's interactive probe dirs, `diagnostics/` verify's spawn pairs) · §Occupied Resources → Claude Code integration names · [CLI Version Compatibility] (Run B's ending) · §Conventions → CLI exit codes · §Infrastructure Patterns → Crate dependency direction · CI/CD approach · Project directory structure
**Change:**
- Verify's dirs were "removed on every exit path"; now they are removed when verify passes, fails, or is stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM: Unix `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, Windows `CTRL_C_EVENT` / `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`, through `cmd::verify::stop`, installed by `viola verify` alone; its handler only sets one flag every wait reads. A stopped run kills and reaps its child with no key, and its drop guards remove only what that run created, never by a pattern or a listing. SIGKILL, a crash, a failed install (ignored, fail-open) and a Windows close, logoff or shutdown keep the OS default and leave the dirs by hand.
- Run B was ended only by Ctrl-C, Ctrl-C again, then a kill; a stopped run is now ended by a kill with no key, starts no later run and writes no stamp.
- Exit 1 covers an interrupted `verify`: no stamp, stdout empty, stderr exactly `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, and `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` under a `VIOLA_NAME`. A child killed at the stop closes its spawn pair with `duration_ms` and no `child_exit_status`.
- Was: Runs C and D's two `--settings` literals were owed to "Interrupted verify cleanup". Now verify reads `SETTINGS_FLAG` and its default program reads `viola_agent_claude::PROGRAM`.
- The root bin's `windows-sys` gains `Win32_System_Console` `SetConsoleCtrlHandler`, and its `libc` gains `sigaction`, both for `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs`; no dependency or feature was added.
- `windows-mutants.yml` was nine items with the root package four; now ten and five (`viola-cmd-verify-stop` · `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs`).
- The tree lists `verify/stop.rs`.
**Why:** The scope is the founder's narrow entry (relayed by the overseer, 2026-10-10). The event set, the exit 1 and the `detail` are the operator's P4 answers; the pair is a planning form with the founder's wording owed. The matrix line was forced by `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` and taken on the operator's word at implement; nothing was dispatched. A later chunk adding a `cfg(windows)` product file owes that workflow its line.
**Kept:** «all gone when verify ends» (`:100`) and run 38036448183's «all nine jobs» stand, both still true; real Windows console delivery stays owed to "Windows-only live measurements".
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-13T20-00-28-wrap/

## 2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup — the keepers' headroom floor and the census's second form
**Section:** §Occupied Resources (Filesystem: `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>/`; Repository: `target/e2e-home`, `target/profraw-census/`) · §Infrastructure Patterns → `project-directory-structure` (the `scripts/profraw-census.sh` comment)
**Change:**
- The two keepers (`prepare_home_base`, `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home`) refuse a linked base whose filesystem reads less than `HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB` (9 GiB) free by `statvfs` (`f_bavail × f_frsize`). The message is fixed: `e2e-home backing: {free} MiB free, below the {floor} MiB floor` (two counts, no path). There is one compiled constant per keeper, equal in both; no variable, flag or config key sets it. Its basis is the tmpfs's EDQUOT reading of about 8 GiB free plus 1 GiB. Was: three checks (absolute target, made 0700 when gone, a real owner-only directory). Now: four.
- `target/profraw-census/`: the script's second form, `--case <binary stem> <test name> <runs> <workers> [<name>]`, runs one integration case of the same instrumented build. Each profile is named with its binary signature (`r<i>-%p-%<nproc>m.profraw`) and offered alone to `llvm-profdata merge`; a refused one is kept under `refused/`. Its last line is `profraw-census: runs N · passed N · profiles P · refused R`; exit 0 only when every run passed and R is 0, 1 otherwise, 2 on usage, with no instrumented binary, or with no `llvm-profdata`. Was: the first form only (the start test). The tree comment names both forms.
**Why:** the stamped-home gates struck EDQUOT on the dev host's quota'd tmpfs, so a home is now refused before the quota is reached; the quota itself is unreadable from the session's shell. The census's second form is the witness that named the truncated profile's killer, a hangup reaching the fake agent's hooks.
**Kept:** a plain-directory base (every CI runner) reads no headroom. The boot refusal stays the closed `build-failed`, and `run --local-live`'s stays `verify-exit-none`; no reason was added.

**Why:** the chunk added the peer-pid read to both clients and the check to every frame-writing client; no dependency was added or bumped. interprocess 2.4.4's Windows peer pid was read in its source and witnessed by the two `server_pid` tests on windows-2025. ## 2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame — the hook's one connect and its fail-open on a failed server check
**Section:** §Established Decisions [Hook Transport], [Hook Contract] (established-decisions.md) · §Standard Contracts, Channel methods (standard-contracts.md: `hook.event`)
**Change:**

**Why:** the chunk built the shared connect in `src/cmd/hook.rs` for `deliver` and `ask`. ## 2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame — the snapshot's pid and started_at as the server identity every frame-writing client checks
**Section:** §Established Decisions [Session Liveness] (established-decisions.md) · §Occupied Resources IPC endpoints (occupied-resources.md) · §Standard Contracts, Channel methods and Session liveness (standard-contracts.md: a new detail group), Instance snapshot (architecture.md)
**Change:**
- Instance snapshot: was "`pid` and `started_at` identify the wrapper process for the liveness check"; now also, on Linux and Windows, for the server check every frame-writing client makes before its first frame: the connected peer's pid and its OS start time against these two fields, a mismatch writing no frame (macOS reports no peer pid, the recorded gap).
- Session liveness: `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint(instance_dir)` returns `Option<LiveEndpoint>`, `LiveEndpoint { endpoint, pid, started_at }`, all from its one `read_snapshot` call, so the liveness-only pre-check comes first and the server check after it. The closed `ServerVerdict` (no crate error enum) is `Matches` · `Mismatch` · `Unverifiable`. The pure `server_verdict(recorded_pid, started_at, observed_pid, observed_start, peer_pid_reported)` compares in whole seconds, `started_at` read through its RFC 3339 form; with `peer_pid_reported` false it returns `Matches` with no comparison. The joined `verify_server(recorded_pid, started_at, observed_pid, peer_pid_reported)` reads the start time through `process_start_time` (a zombie reads none).
- [Session Liveness]: the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` are also the server identity, returned by `live_endpoint` and compared by `verify_server`.
- Channel methods: before its first frame the client of `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `hook.event` and `hook.dialog`, and of the MCP `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools, makes that comparison from its one snapshot read; a mismatch or an unmakeable check writes no frame.
- IPC endpoints: every process connecting to the recorded `endpoint` but `run`'s collision check makes the check; a failure is CLI exit 21 `instance-unreachable`, MCP `instance-unreachable`, the hook failing open.
**Why:** the chunk retired the server-identity half of the first and the fourth to eighth dated gaps on Linux and Windows (`hook.event`; CLI `send`; `wait` / `last`; `answer` + `hook.dialog`; `pause` / `release`; `viola mcp`'s four frame tools); their strict-modes half stands until "Home and code-bearing file integrity". - New: `viola_state::fs::place_private_new(path, bytes, mode) -> Result<Placed, StateError>` (public `Placed { Written, Present }`), the pinned copy's absent-copy write (`viola_state::pin::place_absent`): a temp file beside the target (`NamedTempFile::new_in`), its mode set before any byte (the pinned `viola` at `DIR_MODE`), the bytes written, `sync_all`, the write handle closed (`into_temp_path`), then `TempPath::persist_noclobber`. `AlreadyExists` is `Ok(Placed::Present)`, the target untouched and the temp path removed; any other failure is an error leaving the target as it was; no retry and no error variant of its own.

A new reader lands bounded in its statement or as a named exception, or the census goes red.
- The subjects line gains `crosscut-bounded-readers`.

The needle is matched against the whole source line because the statement ends at the call's `(` and the executable argument the needle names lies past it (an implement deviation, its census hazard). ## 2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary — [MCP] the viola mcp stdin line cap
**Section:** §Established Decisions [MCP] (architecture.md: the body entry; established-decisions.md: three new `dec-mcp` groups)
**Change:**
- The body [MCP] entry gains: `viola mcp`'s stdin is read under a `MAX_FRAME` line cap, each line's newline counted; a longer line is refused whole, never truncated or skipped, and ends the session as a closed stdin does, with one `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin"}` line holding no byte of it; the bound sits in the reader viola hands rmcp, because rmcp 3.4.1's stdio transport reads each line unbounded.
- Detail: the reader is the crate-private `viola_mcp::stdin::CappedLines` at `MAX_FRAME` bytes per line, handed to rmcp as the reader of its `(reader, writer)` stdio transport (the path `transport-io` already enables; rmcp's features stay `server` + `transport-io`). A line of exactly the cap passes whole; at the end of stdin a held unterminated line within the cap is released; a longer line releases no byte, sets the reader's cut flag and then reads as end of stream. The wrapper channel's close-on-oversize rule is its precedent.
- Detail: after a session a cut ended, `viola_mcp::serve` writes exactly one `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin", detail:"oversize", count:1}` at WARN through `obs_event!`, holding no byte of the line, then returns `Ok(())` once the session initialized (exit 0, as at a closed stdin) or `ServeError::Initialize` (exit 11) when the cut lands before `initialize` completes.
- Detail: rmcp 3.4.1's stdio `AsyncRwTransport::receive` reads each line with an unbounded `read_until`, and `JsonRpcMessageCodec::new_with_max_length` bounds only the writer side (as read in rmcp 3.4.1's crates.io source); `CappedLines` signals a cut as end of stream, never as an I/O error, so rmcp writes nothing of its own.
**Why:** rmcp's unbounded `read_until` on `viola mcp`'s stdin was named this chunk's own subject (overseer1's ruling under the founder's night word). A truncated line would dispatch a padded valid request and a skipped one would leave the peer's request unanswered with no signal, so the line is refused whole. A cut before `initialize` keeps what a closed stdin before `initialize` gives (an implement deviation). No exit code, tool, method or error variant was added.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-27T06-19-22-wrap/

**Section:** Conventions (conv-refusal-reason, conv-exit-codes); Established Decisions ([MCP]); Standard Contracts (CLI `--json` output); Infrastructure Patterns → Project directory structure (`client.rs`, `viola-core`)
**Change:**
- conv-refusal-reason gains `viola_core::UnreachableCause` (`StrictModes` · `InstanceDead` · `UnwrappedName` · `EndpointLost` · `ServerVerify`, each word through `as_str`), exit 21's closed cause set: no serde path, the two clients write every word, and it is no `RefusalReason`.
- conv-exit-codes gains the CLI mapping: `client.rs` `answer_of` reads `Connect` as `Dead` and `Closed | Io` as `Lost`; the six no-endpoint arms (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `link`; `release` and `unlink` through `wheel_call` and `link_call`) read `Unreachable::without_endpoint`.

- [MCP] gains `result::unreachable(cause)`: `of_reply` reads `Connect` as `InstanceDead` and `Closed | Io` as `EndpointLost`, `of_board` reads the board's refusal as `StrictModes`, and `tools.rs` `frame` reads a refused `check_instance` as `StrictModes`, no `live_endpoint` by `without_endpoint` and a failed `server_verified` as `ServerVerify`, each with no frame and no line, `isError` the record.
- Standard Contracts gains the writer: `client::unreachable_document` is the one writer of the exit-21 CLI document; `refuse_untrusted` and `src/cmd/plugin.rs` write `StrictModes` through it, and `list.rs`'s `refused_document` builds `strict-modes-failed` as a `Value` for `board_document`.
- Project directory structure: the closed `Unreachable` was `instance-dead` · `server-verify-failed`; now `Dead` · `Unwrapped` · `Lost` · `ServerUnverified`, each an `UnreachableCause` through `cause()`. `client.rs`'s comment adds `unreachable_document` and its refused check's document names `strict-modes-failed`; `viola-core`'s adds `UnreachableCause`.
**Why:** the one exit-21 document could not tell its causes apart; each is now a closed word with one CLI writer. No `RefusalReason` and no exit code was added. ## 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order — tempfile `persist` snapshot writer, liveness by process check, start order as landed, `viola-state`
**Section:** §Stack (State-file primitives, Content hash) · §Established Decisions [Snapshot writer], [Session Liveness], [Deployment / Distribution] · §Conventions CLI exit codes (`1`) · §Standard Contracts Instance snapshot, Session liveness · §Occupied Resources Workspace crates, Filesystem (`bin/`), Repository (`target/e2e-home`) · §Infrastructure Patterns Build system (lint, rust plane, licence), Crate dependency direction (`viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`), CI/CD approach · §Inherited Defaults Database
**Change:**
- [Snapshot writer] + State-file primitives + Database: tempfile 3.27.0 `persist` through ONE shared helper (`viola_state::fs::replace_private`, mode set on the temp file before the write; `replace_private_shared` for identical concurrent writes) replaces atomic-write-file 0.3.1 (BSD-3-Clause, outside `deny.toml`); `.lock` siblings opened for write (Windows refuses the lock on an append-only handle).
- [Session Liveness] + Session liveness + exit `1`: pid + start time decide `gone` whatever the beat; same process → `live` (≤ 5 s) or `stale`; a `live`/`stale` name refuses (`already-live`), a `gone` one is taken over at once; start order as landed (resolution → collision → pin + plugin → [version gate, bind: later] → snapshot + heartbeat → events → spawn → `child_pid` rewrite).
- Instance snapshot: `endpoint?` (from "Wrapper channel"), `child_pid?` (post-spawn rewrite), `started_at` = the wrapper's OS start time.
- [Deployment] + `bin/`: re-hash before reuse, mismatch refuses (`pinned-hash-mismatch`); plugin rewritten every start, `hooks`/`mcpServers` empty until their verbs (operator ruling).
- Content hash: sha2 a `viola-state` product dependency; `[profile.dev.package.sha2] opt-level = 3`.

title: Infrastructure Patterns
body:
## Infrastructure Patterns

**Build system**
- Cargo workspace with `resolver = "3"` (the edition 2024 default, which prefers dependency versions compatible with `rust-version = "1.96"`). Shared `version.workspace = true`, `license.workspace = true` (`[workspace.package]` `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`) and `[workspace.dependencies]` pin every third-party version in one place (portable-pty as `=0.8.1`; rmcp minor pinned as `~3.4`).
- Lint: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings`.
  - `[workspace.lints.clippy]` denies `print_stdout`, `print_stderr` and `dbg_macro`, and every product member inherits it (`[lints] workspace = true`, asserted by `tests/contract_lints.rs`). `viola-e2e` opts out and denies only `dbg_macro`, because the harness prints its JSON document. The fake agent carries a crate-level print allow. The root bin carries no print allow: its only human writer is `src/human.rs`. On stderr, `write_refusal` writes the two fixed `unable:`/`hint:` lines as ONE `write_all` and `write_internal_error` writes exactly `error: internal error\n`; on stdout, `write_result` writes one line per `write_all`. The `refuse` / `internal_error` / `result` wrappers lock the stream, call the writer and drop the result (a closed pipe is swallowed, never a panic), a form `print_stdout`/`print_stderr` do not flag. Its callers are the `viola run` start refusals (`.cmd`/`.bat` child, live or stale name, tampered pinned copy, squatted endpoint) and `viola verify` (its refusals, step lines, `stamped` summary and the `cli` role's internal error); `hook` and obs never call it.
  - `clippy.toml` `disallowed-macros` bans `tracing::{info,warn,error,debug,trace}`, so `obs_event!` is the only sanctioned emitter. Raw `event!` is caught by a fail-closed grep in `scripts/lint-probes.sh`, because clippy 1.98.1 cannot exempt a macro's inner expansion (obs-plan §3 logger-stack-install).
  - `scripts/lint-probes.sh` proves every ban fires and every control passes, as `deny-probes.sh` does for cargo-deny.
- Typecheck: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`.
- Dependency policy: `cargo deny check` over `deny.toml` — advisories, licences (`allow` exactly `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `Zlib`, `Unicode-3.0`; `0BSD` only through per-crate `[[licenses.exceptions]]` for `doctest-file` and `recvmsg`, the two 0BSD crates interprocess 2.4.4 pulls in, never through `allow`: operator ratification 2026-09-25, security-plan Decisions Log), sources (crates.io only) and bans: C-building crates (`cc`, `libsqlite3-sys`, `openssl-sys`), telemetry crates (`opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-stdout`, `sentry`, `tracing-appender`) and feature bans (`veil/toggle`, `rmcp` `auth` / `transport-streamable-http-server`, `axum/http2`, `tracing-subscriber/env-filter`), evaluated for the Windows, macOS and Linux target triples so `cfg`-gated dependencies are covered. The ban on `tokio` anywhere in the normal dependency graph, direct or transitive, of `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-channel` without its feature, `viola-state` and `viola-agent-claude` lives in `deny-sync.toml` (the same three triples, `exclude-dev = true`) and runs once per crate listed in `scripts/sync-crates.txt`, that crate as the sole root: `cargo deny --config deny-sync.toml --manifest-path crates/<crate>/Cargo.toml check bans`. Never a direct-parent allowlist (`wrappers`), because Tokio could otherwise arrive unnoticed through a third-party feature such as interprocess's or notify's; never `--exclude` over the workspace, which false-fails under feature unification — a shared crate's optional `tokio` feature stays on after the crate enabling it is excluded (as measured at chunk 2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates, research.md §Measured facts, cargo-deny 0.19.4 and 0.20.2). Limit, same measurement: the crate owning the optional `tokio` feature (`viola-channel`) false-fails as its own root once `viola-mcp` enables that feature (`cargo metadata` reports the unified set), so it is covered through the sync roots that depend on it. Every ban is proven live by `scripts/deny-probes.sh`: a throwaway project per ban must fail with that ban's own diagnostic, and a clean control must pass both configs. `fuzz/` has its own `Cargo.lock` outside this graph, and its libfuzzer-sys builds C++ via `cc`: the only C build in the repository. The operator ratified this on 2026-09-24 as a test-only exemption. The crate is never linked into `viola`, and `fuzz` never joins the root `[workspace]`. Its lockfile is audited separately: the CI `supply-chain` step `Fuzz lockfile audit (advisories, sources)` runs `cargo deny --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --format json check advisories sources` into `target/supply-chain/deny-fuzz.json`, and the weekly nightly `advisories` job runs `cargo deny --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml check advisories`. Both run from the repo root: cargo-deny resolves the root `deny.toml` by walking up from the manifest, and under `fuzz/` rustup would demand the fuzz nightly (measured at chunk 2026-09-24-workspace-tree-and-code-graph-planes).
- Boundary review:
  - `cargo modules orphans --deny` is a CI gate. `scripts/orphans-check.sh` runs it in the per-OS `lint` job once per lib/bin target from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, with `--features` for a target's required features (`viola-fake-agent`), and its `--probe` mode proves it fires on a planted orphan first.
  - The `cargo modules dependencies` graph (`--acyclic`) stays an on-demand review, never a gate: cargo-modules 0.27.0 reports every type and its own inherent method as a cycle, whatever the filters (measured at the same chunk, 3 of 4 targets).
  - The rmcp release-graph check (`cargo tree -e features -p viola --edges normal`, rmcp exactly `server` + `transport-io`) has no subject until `viola-mcp` exists; it lands with the "MCP server for drivers" chunk.
- Code-graph planes (`scripts/code-graph.py`, one DuckDB per language plane under `.andromeda/cache/{plane}/`):
  - **rust:** the root workspace through rust-analyzer SCIP. It indexes every member (`viola`, `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-channel`, `viola-agent-claude`, `viola-state`, `viola-e2e`). `fuzz/`, a separate workspace, is outside it.
  - **ts:** `e2e-web/` only, from its first chunk, through a tracked `e2e-web/tsconfig.json` (noEmit, strict) and scip-typescript. No tsconfig, package manifest or bundler config ever covers `crates/viola-ui/` (the page has no JS build step); a CI-runnable guard lists any such file.
- Install: `cargo install --path .` from the repo root.
- Publishing: every workspace member, including the root `viola` bin, sets `publish = false`. Nothing goes to crates.io in v1.
- Licence: the project is `MIT OR Apache-2.0` (founder ruling 2026-09-25). `license` is set once in root `[workspace.package]` and inherited with `license.workspace = true` by `viola`, `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-channel`, `viola-agent-claude`, `viola-state` and `viola-e2e`; `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, its own workspace, carries the literal. The texts are `LICENSE-MIT` (holder Turbolet85) and `LICENSE-APACHE` at the root, and `README.md` names both.

**Deployment model**
- Local-only. There is no Docker, Compose, Kubernetes or serverless.
- The single `viola` binary is installed on PATH. `viola run <name> -- claude <args>` pins a copy of itself in `~/.viola/bin/<version>-<hash>/` (on Windows x64 also the embedded ConPTY companions in its `conpty/` subdirectory, with `conpty.dll` pre-loaded from there before the spawn), writes the embedded plugin (pointing at that copy) to `~/.viola/plugin/<version>-<hash>/` and launches the child with `--plugin-dir`. `viola ui` is started by hand and serves 127.0.0.1.

**Crate dependency direction** (enforced by manifests)
- `viola-core` depends on no viola crate. Third-party: nutype (`ViolaName`, `Percent`).
- `viola-pty` depends on no viola crate and knows no agent. Third-party (as landed): portable-pty, tracing (the `pty.spawn` span), windows-sys (Windows only), libc (Unix only; termios raw mode and the terminal size). No thiserror ([Error Handling]).
- `viola-channel` → `viola-core`, interprocess, serde, serde_json, thiserror, tracing, veil, windows-sys (Windows only: the SQOS client open adopted by `Stream::try_from`, and the listener DACL through `Win32_Security_Authorization`), libc (Unix only: the uid for the socket directory). As landed it is sync and tokio-free, with a sync client and server; the Tokio client arrives behind the `tokio` feature with `viola-mcp`.
- `viola-state` → `viola-core`, chrono, serde, serde_json, sha2 (the pinned-copy key and re-hash), sysinfo (the pid + start-time liveness check, shared by CLI `list`, `mcp` and `ui`), tempfile (the one `persist` helper), thiserror, tracing, and notify with tailing.
- `viola-agent-claude` → `viola-core`, `viola-state`, serde_path_to_error (drift reports on external payloads), vt100 (the screen model and signatures behind the readiness gate; `run`'s pump feeds it bytes). This is the only crate that knows Claude payload shapes, including `claude agents --json`. As landed it depends on `viola-core`, serde, serde_json, serde_path_to_error `=0.1.20` (the `hook` module: `HookEvent`, `normalise`, drift reports) and thiserror (`IDENTITY_FLOOR`, `plan_strip`, `resolve_program`, `Refusal`, `PLUGIN_DIR_FLAG`, `plugin_files` over the `include_str!`-embedded `plugin/` templates, and the pure `ledger` module: the six rows, `parse_version`, `capture_plugin_files`, `check`, `merge_stamp`, `verified`, `scrub`/`is_clean`; `CASE_INSENSITIVE` and `is_script` are `pub` for `verify`), with dev-dependencies proptest and rstest. The ledger chunk added no `viola-state` dependency: the stamps file I/O stays in `viola-state` and the root bin, so the crate stays pure. vt100, and `viola-state` if a later consumer needs it, arrive with the chunks that consume them.
- `viola-mcp` → `viola-core`, `viola-channel[tokio]`, `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`, rmcp, schemars, tokio.
- `viola-ui` → `viola-core`, `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`, axum, tower-http, tokio.
- serde, serde_json, chrono and thiserror are shared through `[workspace.dependencies]` by every workspace crate except `viola-pty`, which takes none of them. The sync crates (`viola-core`, `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`) list chrono directly, because they do not reach it through rmcp.
- `viola-e2e` (test-only; no product crate depends on it); its dependencies are not listed here.
- The `viola` root bin → all members, clap, anyhow, windows-sys (Windows only: the registry reader for the R8 persistent-environment names in `src/run/env.rs`, plus `Win32_System_Diagnostics_Debug` and `Win32_System_LibraryLoader` for `src/panic_frames.rs`'s `RtlCaptureStackBackTrace` / `GetModuleHandleExW` / `GetModuleFileNameW`) and libc `=0.2.189` (Unix only: `backtrace` + `dladdr` for the raw, never-symbolised panic frames). It contains the subcommand dispatch, the `run` pump, the wheel and the budget governor, all of which consume only normalised events.

**Project directory structure**
```
viola/
├── Cargo.toml                  # [package] viola (bin) + [workspace] members = ["crates/*"], exclude = ["fuzz"]
├── Cargo.lock
├── rust-toolchain.toml         # channel = "1.98.1" (exact pin), components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]
├── deny.toml                   # cargo-deny: advisories, licences, sources, bans (C, telemetry, features)
├── deny-sync.toml              # the tokio ban, run per scripts/sync-crates.txt crate as sole root
├── clippy.toml                 # disallowed-macros: tracing::{info,warn,error,debug,trace}
├── .gitignore
├── LICENSE-MIT                 # MIT text (holder Turbolet85); the project is MIT OR Apache-2.0

├── plugin/                     # embedded via include_str!, written out by `viola run`
│   ├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json

├── src/                        # the `viola` bin: anyhow edge only
│   ├── main.rs                 # clap 4.6.7 dispatch (Windows: the System32 DLL-search restriction is its second statement)
│   ├── conpty.rs               # Windows x64: the embedded ConPTY companions and their four pins (the vendor script parses this text)

│   │                           #   `sideload` (Windows): the System32 DLL-search restriction + the absolute-path conpty.dll pre-load)

│   ├── tests/*.spec.ts         # one spec per bay layout type; today the pipe stub's pipe-reachability.spec.ts
│   ├── fixtures/a11y.ts        # the shared makeAxeBuilder fixture
│   ├── schemas/a11y-row.v1.json  # tests-owned a11y violation-row schema (not obs schemas/)

│       └── nightly.yml         # weekly schedule + workflow_dispatch: cargo deny check advisories (root + fuzz/Cargo.lock),
│                               #   npm-advisories (npm-audit.sh --advisories-only) + fuzz time-box
```

**CI/CD approach**
- GitHub Actions, two workflows. `ci.yml`, triggered on push and pull request, with matrix `os: [windows-2025, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]` on native runners, is the only push/PR pipeline. `nightly.yml`, triggered by a weekly `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` (both fire from the repository's default branch), runs three ubuntu jobs with no cache. `advisories` runs `cargo deny check advisories` over the root lockfile and `cargo deny --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml check advisories` over the fuzz lockfile, because the advisory DB moves without code changes; `npm-advisories` does the same for `e2e-web/package-lock.json` (`Node (pinned)`, then `scripts/npm-audit.sh --advisories-only`). `fuzz` runs `cargo +<channel> fuzz run --fuzz-dir fuzz <t> fuzz/corpus/<t> -- -max_total_time=120` per target (the channel comes from `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml`) and uploads `fuzz/artifacts/` on `failure()`. Neither workflow has a `concurrency:` block. zizmor's pedantic `concurrency-limits` was declined because a concurrency group cancels pending runs, which would drop a cancelled run's `always()` gate and upload chain. (CI runs no mutation job — mutation testing moved to the epoch-boundary code audit on 2026-09-28 — so a cancelled run cannot lose mutation coverage; that half of the original reason is retired.)
- Least privilege, in every workflow: `permissions: {}` at the workflow top and `contents: read` per job; every `uses:` pinned by full commit SHA with a version comment; event-payload values reach a step only through `env:`. zizmor asserts it.
- Setup steps: `actions/checkout` v7.0.1 (`persist-credentials: false`), `rustup toolchain install` (reads `rust-toolchain.toml`: the exact pin plus rustfmt and clippy; no toolchain action), `Swatinem/rust-cache` v2.9.2 (`ci.yml` only), and `taiki-e/install-action` v2.87.19 for the version-pinned cargo tools (cargo-deny 0.20.2 included); zizmor 1.30.1 is installed by `cargo install --locked zizmor@1.30.1` in the job that runs it. ripgrep 15.2.0 (G1/G3) comes from `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh` in the `lint` job, because taiki-e/install-action has no ripgrep manifest: the official release asset, checked against its published sha256 and exported on `PATH`. hyperfine 1.20.0 is installed by `cargo install --locked hyperfine@1.20.0` as its own step in the `perf` job (the zizmor precedent; not on the taiki-e line, so the WSL provisioning replays nothing new). `jq` is runner-provided and never installed: the `test` and `perf` jobs presence-check it (`jq --version`) before G2, whose `scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh` refuses with `tool-missing: jq` without it, and `scripts/release-check.sh` (`release`), `scripts/orphans-check.sh` (`lint`) and `scripts/npm-audit.sh` (`supply-chain`, which also runs `jq --version` first) refuse with `tool-missing: jq` without it. cargo-modules 0.27.0 is installed by `cargo install --locked cargo-modules@0.27.0` in the `lint` job, because the pinned taiki-e/install-action has no cargo-modules manifest. The `test` job adds `rustup component add llvm-tools-preview` and `cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1` on the taiki-e line. `msrv` runs `rustup toolchain install 1.96 --profile minimal`. The fuzz jobs run `rustup toolchain install` in `working-directory: fuzz` (reading `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml`) and `cargo install --locked cargo-fuzz@0.13.2`. Node v24.21.0 comes from `scripts/install-node.sh` in the `test` and `supply-chain` jobs (and nightly `npm-advisories`), the install-ripgrep precedent with no setup-node action: the official nodejs.org archive for the OS, checked against its `NODE_PIN_SHA256_*` line, extracted to `$RUNNER_TEMP/node` and exported on `PATH`. The `test` job then runs `npm ci --prefix e2e-web` and the Playwright Chromium install per OS (`--with-deps` on ubuntu). No npm or browser cache.
- Jobs wired today in `ci.yml` (7; 15 check-runs per push, as measured at ci#36483042659 on `17b93c7`): `test` (per OS; on `windows-2025` only, before the coverage run, the `ConPTY vendor verification` step runs `bash scripts/conpty-vendor.sh --verify` then `--probe` (verdicts `conpty-vendor: verified <version>` and `conpty-vendor probe: 4/4 refused, control clean`); then one harness `run --coverage` through the OS's shim, i.e. the instrumented nextest run as suite `coverage` with the per-OS floors 85/95/80, followed by doctest, then the boot → status → logs → cleanup lifecycle, then the browser suite (`Node (pinned)`, `npm ci`, the Chromium install, and `agent-run run --browser` through the OS's shim: suite `playwright`); `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`; then, in obs-plan §9 order: `jq --version`, G2 (`scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh --probe && scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh`), G4 `schema-check` (`id: schema-conformance`), the `if: failure()` harness capture, and `secret-scan` (`id: secret-scan`, `if: always()`). The uploads are gated on that scan: `diag-<os>` and `junit-<os>` on `always() && steps.secret-scan.outcome == 'success'`, `harness-<os>` (`target/agent-run/` minus `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`, the file the scan skips) on `failure() && … == 'success'`, and `secret-scan-<os>` on `always() && … == 'failure'`, all with actions/upload-artifact v7.0.1 and 7 days (`junit-<os>` carries `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` and `target/agent-run/artifacts/junit-playwright.xml`); last, an `if: always()` `Gate verdict` step runs `gate --require coverage,doctest,playwright`). `perf` (per OS, `fail-fast: false`, `contents: read`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`; test-plan §9 Perf row) runs checkout, toolchain, rust-cache, `cargo install --locked hyperfine@1.20.0`, `jq --version`, `agent-run run --perf`, then G2 (probe then check), `schema-check` and `secret-scan` (`id: secret-scan`), all `if: always()`; it uploads `perf-<os>` (`target/agent-run/artifacts/perf-*.json`) and `diag-perf-<os>` (`target/e2e-home/**/diagnostics/*.ndjson`) only on `always() && steps.secret-scan.outcome == 'success'`, and `secret-scan-perf-<os>` on a scan failure; last, an `if: always()` `Gate verdict` step runs `gate --require perf`. `test`, the pre-push and the WSL provisioning carry no perf step. CI runs no mutation job: mutation testing runs only through `agent-run run --mutants` [`--file`], kept for the epoch-boundary `/andromeda-code-audit` (test-plan §10 Mutation gate). `msrv` (ubuntu, rust-cache `key: msrv`) runs `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96` steps for `rustc --version`, `cargo check --workspace` and `agent-run run --unit`, then `gate --require nextest-unit`. `fuzz-replay` (ubuntu, no cache) runs `agent-run run --fuzz-replay`, then `gate --require fuzz-replay`. `lint` (per OS: target job 3, then target jobs 1 and 2, the ripgrep install, `rg --pcre2-version`, G1 and G3 verbatim from obs-plan §9, `scripts/lint-probes.sh` on Linux, then `Install cargo-modules` and `Module orphans (per lib/bin target)`: `scripts/orphans-check.sh --probe && scripts/orphans-check.sh`). `release` (per OS, `fail-fast: false`, rust-cache: target job 6) runs `scripts/release-check.sh --probe`, then `scripts/release-check.sh`; like `lint` it is a plain exit-code job, with no upload and no `viola-harness gate` step. `supply-chain` (ubuntu) runs:
  - target job 4 as `cargo deny --format json check`;
  - the `Fuzz lockfile audit (advisories, sources)` into `target/supply-chain/deny-fuzz.json`;
  - `Node (pinned)`, then the `npm lockfile audit (advisories, sources)`: `scripts/npm-audit.sh` over `e2e-web/package-lock.json` (0 advisories at `--audit-level=low`, every `packages[].resolved` from `https://registry.npmjs.org/`), its JSON in `target/npm-audit/`, which is not uploaded;
  - the sole-root `deny-sync.toml` tokio ban per listed sync crate;
  - `scripts/deny-probes.sh` and `zizmor --format=json .github/workflows/`.

  Its JSON reports are uploaded from `target/supply-chain/` as artifact `supply-chain` with `if: always()`. Every gate step is fail-closed `shell: bash`.
- Target jobs per OS, each wired by the chunk that owns it (Supply-chain gates, Quality gates, Workspace tree):
  1. `cargo fmt --all --check`
  2. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings` (workspace lint bans and `clippy.toml` in force)
  3. `cargo check` with one `-p` per crate listed in `scripts/sync-crates.txt` (target set `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-channel`, `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`; each joins the list with its crate; an empty list or an absent package fails) — proves the sync crates, including the `hook` path, compile on each OS without `viola-channel`'s `tokio` feature; the ban itself is the sole-root `deny-sync.toml` step of job 4
  4. `cargo deny check` (once, on ubuntu)
  5. the workspace test suite against the fake agent, replaying `fixtures/claude/*`
  6. `cargo build --release --locked --bin viola` through `scripts/release-check.sh` (the `release` job): it judges that build's own `compiler-artifact` executables, fails on any other than `viola` (`viola-harness`, `viola-fake-agent`) or on none, fails first on any `compiler-artifact` record whose `features` hold the test-only `test-support` or `fake-agent` (`release-check: FAILED — test-only feature {feature} in {target}`; `--probe` reads `5/5 refused, control clean`), and never lists `target/release/`, where a shared or cached dir keeps stale test-only exes (measured at chunk 2026-09-24-workspace-tree-and-code-graph-planes: a bare `cargo build --release` and `--bin viola` yield `viola` only, `--workspace` adds `viola-harness`)
- The real `claude` CLI runs only locally, never in CI. `viola verify` runs in CI only against the fake agent's `-p/--print` mode (`tests/cli_verify.rs`); its real-CLI probe and `--record` run only locally.
- A local pre-push gate precedes every operator push. The operator pass runs, in order: `viola-harness pre-push` on the uncommitted tree → the pre-CI commit → the guarded push → the CI reads; a red `pre-push` stops the pass. `pre-push` runs on the Windows dev host only (elsewhere it refuses `pre-push-windows-only`, exit 2): it syncs the working tree into a history-carrying clone in WSL2 `Ubuntu` (the clone's tree id must equal the Windows tree id), checks the Linux tools there against their pins (the C linker, the channel, ci.yml's cargo tools and `node --version` = `v<NODE_PIN_VERSION>`, refusing `tool-missing` / `tool-pin-mismatch` with detail `node`), runs the ubuntu `test` job's `run --coverage`, `run --browser` (a red stops before the gate) and `gate --require coverage,doctest,playwright` there, terminates the WSL VM once the ubuntu verdict is on the host (`vm-release`, so its memory returns to the host), then runs `run --coverage` + `gate --require coverage,doctest` on the host (`windows-tests`): stages `tools → sync → cache → linux-tests → vm-release → windows-tests`, `ok:true` when `windows-tests` is green, and no mutation stage (test-plan §3 Internal harness subcommands). Every WSL call is `env -i HOME=… PATH=…` with no further assignment; the `cache` section reports the clone's `target/` as `bytes`, `cap`, `cleaned` and `bytes_after`. The host stages run with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=16`, set by the harness. `run --mutants` itself sets `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=0` and `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=0` on the `cargo mutants` command wherever `run --mutants` runs (a mutation run keeps no test home). It is a filter before the push; CI's run on the pushed sha stays the verdict of record.
- There is no deploy stage in v1. The v1.x release path adds a dist 0.33.0-generated release workflow with cargo-auditable 0.7.6.

title: security-plan
Security Plan — viola

body:
_Generated by `/andromeda-security`. This file is the single source of truth
for all security requirements. Read by downstream skills (design / tests /
obs / a11y per D26 cross-cutting), route (per D25 bootstrap phasing),
setup-project (materializes `@` imports + secure defaults per D22),
and the phase loop per chunk (`/andromeda-phase` distillers + `/andromeda-implement`)._

_Do not edit during phase loop runs (`/andromeda-phase` / `/andromeda-implement`).
Manual edits between runs are fine._

_**Stack adaptability:** viola is a local CLI binary with a local IPC channel, a stdio MCP server and a Claude Code hook contract. It has no public network surface. The IPC, filesystem and PTY controls stand in for the "auth", "database" and "API" rows of a web stack._

title: Threat Model Summary

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/threat-model-summary.md — read whole.
_[ALL tiers — VERBATIM copy from threat-assessment.md]_

**Security tier:** `Minimal (0), with targeted elevations for the local privilege boundary`
_Justification: viola is a local-only, single-user tool. It has no accounts, no public network listener, no database, no stored credentials and no regulated data (Sections 1, 3, 4, 5), which rules out Standard's user-account and HTTPS concerns and Hardened's compliance drivers. It still goes beyond a plain Minimal profile in two ways. First, the local IPC endpoint is effectively a code-execution interface (`send` types prompts, `answer` can allow PermissionRequest tool calls). It currently has no decided per-OS enforcement of its same-OS-user boundary, and its names are predictable in the shared Windows pipe namespace, the Unix socket standing in a per-user 0700 directory. Second, several state files decide what code runs and whether dialogs are answered: `snapshot.json`'s `statusline_command`, the `hooks.json` exec paths, the pinned binaries and the ledger stamps. The baseline is therefore Minimal (dependency audit, input validation on config and external payloads, error sanitization). On top of it sit specific local-boundary items: IPC endpoint access control and server impersonation, bracketed-paste breakout in `send.text`, and integrity of `~/.viola/`. Each of these traces to Section 2._
**Data classification:**

Data classes: user-content (prompts, assistant replies, tool-call arguments, plans and dialog text) logged to `events.ndjson` and sent over the channel; integrity-sensitive config, several files deciding what code runs (`statusline_command`, the hook and MCP exec paths, the pinned binary, the ledger stamps); a transient credential inherited from the environment, never stored by viola; operational metadata, PII limited to the OS username in paths.
The snapshot's recorded `cwd`, an absolute host path that can carry the OS username, stands in the 0600 snapshot only, on no log line, error body or stdout.
- **Type:** payment / health / multi-user PII: none. Stack lists no payment, identity or health SDKs, there is no database and no accounts (Stack; Established Decisions: Personal v1).
**Attack surface:**

**Vector:** Local IPC, the wrapper channel, the highest-impact surface: whoever can connect can type prompts into the driven session, allow PermissionRequest dialogs and read the whole conversation. v1 intends to trust every process of the same OS user and no other; there is no per-connection authentication, the self-reported `from` authenticates nothing, and the endpoint name is predictable.

**Vector:** CLI input, the `send` text written into the PTY as one bracketed paste of the typed text: an embedded paste terminator or other control sequence would end the paste early, and the rest would reach the `claude` TUI as typed keystrokes.

**Vector:** The human's terminal, `viola run`'s own stdin: a byte that is typing takes the wheel from the driver; only a sequence on the stdin classifier's closed non-editing list never counts as typing, and a reply no terminal has been measured to write is never added on a guess.

**Vector:** Hook stdin payloads from Claude Code, exec-form `viola hook <event>`: parsed tolerantly, upstream text treated as content, never as commands, and any failure failing open to the human; `hook statusline` runs `statusline_command` through a shell, its integrity set by filesystem permissions on the viola home.

**Vector:** MCP over stdio, the driver an LLM agent: tool input schemas and the `ViolaName` newtype check the input; each stdin line is capped at `MAX_FRAME` before rmcp reads it, an over-long line refused whole and ending the session, never dispatched in part; the driver model reads untrusted driven-session output and can answer that session's PermissionRequest, the decision resting with it, outside viola; leaving `release`, `pause`, `link` and `unlink` off the tool list is an affordance, not an enforcement.

**Vector:** CLI arguments, flags and environment: `--home` and `VIOLA_DIR` choose which state tree, snapshot, `endpoint`, `statusline_command` and ledger stamps are used; the trust boundary is same-user invocation, clap parsing, the `ViolaName` nutype and tolerant `config.json` parsing.

**Vector:** Filesystem state under `~/.viola/`, read across processes and holding the code-bearing artefacts Claude Code runs: its trust boundary is OS permissions on the user's home directory; readers tolerate torn lines, the pinned binary and plugin folders are never deleted in v1, and beyond the content hash in the folder name the start holds the home tree, the pinned binary and the plugin folders to the strict-modes check (owner and mode, or owner and DACL) before any log opens.

**Vector:** Child process spawning and PATH resolution (`claude agents --json`, the `--version` probe, `revive`'s `claude`, `viola verify`'s interactive children): the trust boundary is whatever the calling process's PATH resolves to; output parsing is tolerant and failure becomes `unknown`; verify's children are read only against the compiled signature literals, their row text leaving the process only as signature-only `--record` fixtures.

`viola verify`'s interactive children never get a byte written into any dialog, a start showing a modal killed with no key; each `agents-probe` spawn pair is logged with no row text, id, `cwd` or path.

**Vector:** Supply chain (build and CI): Cargo dependencies, SHA-pinned third-party GitHub Actions and rustup-installed toolchains; the trust boundary is `cargo deny check`, the sync-crate `tokio` bans, `Cargo.lock` and `publish = false`, the test-only `fuzz/` lockfile audited on its own by a ratified exemption; v1 has no release, no signing and no deploy stage.

- **Public internet API / file upload / OAuth / WebSocket / webhook:** none. Stack and Conventions list no public listener, no WebSocket ("No WebSocket and no polling endpoints in v1") and no hosting.
**Auth model:**

- **Approach:** none for v1 (as of 2026-09-23). The only principal is the local OS user.
  - Reason: Project Intent and Established Decisions (Personal v1) describe a single-user local tool with "no accounts, no hosting".
  - Access control therefore depends entirely on OS-level isolation: who can connect to each IPC endpoint and who can read or write `~/.viola/`. Cross-cutting Patterns (Local endpoint trust boundary) sets the target principal as "every process of the same OS user and no other".
  - Arch has decided no enforcement mechanism for that boundary on any OS. That decision is outstanding and belongs to this specialist.
- **Provider:** self-implemented. Stack contains no auth framework or identity SDK.
- **Scope:** per-OS-user for v1 (IPC and filesystem). Remote or phone access behind authentication is a later version and is N/A in this assessment (Project Intent: Scale path; Stack: Mobile N/A).

- **Development Style context:** agent-driven (Cross-cutting Patterns). The main automated callers are LLM driver sessions using MCP and the CLI, with no interactive login. That matches an ambient OS-user trust model rather than a credential flow.
**Infrastructure:**
- **Hosting:** local-only. Installed with `cargo install --path .`. No Docker, Compose, Kubernetes, serverless or PaaS (Infrastructure Patterns: Deployment model; Established Decisions: Hosting).

- **Database:** none. State is embedded flat files: ndjson append logs plus atomically replaced JSON snapshots, with std `File::lock` on sibling `.lock` files, under `~/.viola/` or `--home` (Stack: Database; Established Decisions: Database / State Store). Nothing is encrypted, and all of it is plaintext for readability by design.

- **Networking:** local only.
  - Per-instance named pipes (Windows) or Unix domain sockets (a verified per-user 0700 directory, never the `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` root); no Linux abstract namespace.
  - MCP over stdio.
  - No outbound network calls by viola itself. The `claude` child handles the network to Anthropic on its own.
  - Sources: Occupied Resources (IPC endpoints); Stack (AI/ML N/A).

**CI/CD:** GitHub Actions `ci.yml` on push and PR over a native `windows-2025`, `macos-latest` and `ubuntu-latest` matrix, plus the weekly `nightly.yml` advisory and fuzz run; no deploy stage, no release artefacts and no secrets in v1, the real `claude` CLI running only locally.

**Compliance triggers:**
None: no compliance-regulated data detected.
- No payment data (no payment SDK in Stack).
- No health data.
- No children's data.

- No collection of personal data from third parties. The tool has no accounts and no hosting, and all logged content is the operator's own Claude session content kept on their own machine (Established Decisions: Personal v1; Project Intent).
- The v1.x public distribution in Project Intent (Scale path) still keeps all data local on each user's machine, so it adds no trigger in this assessment.

This tier is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how much security rigor downstream
skills (the phase loop per chunk + cross-cutting reads from design / tests /
obs / a11y) should apply.

title: Authentication & Authorization

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/authentication-authorization.md — read whole.

_Included despite v1 auth approach "none". Threat Model Sec 6 elevates "IPC endpoint access control and server impersonation". Every principal check in viola is OS-level (IPC, filesystem). See the Security Decisions Log._
**Auth approach:** OS-user ambient trust, enforced per OS, on the IPC endpoints and `~/.viola/`.
**Library:**

- IPC: interprocess 2.4.4 (`ListenerOptionsExt::security_descriptor`, `Stream::peer_creds()`, its `pid()` also the client's read of the serving process: Linux `SO_PEERCRED`, Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the SQOS-opened client end, none on macOS; its `euid()` the Unix read of the peer on both sides, the wrapper reading a client and a client reading the server, none on Windows), windows-sys 0.61.2 (`GetTokenInformation(TokenUser)`, `ConvertSidToStringSidW`, the SDDL-to-descriptor conversion under feature `Win32_Security_Authorization`, `CreateFileW` with SQOS flags), std chmod on the bound Unix socket, and sysinfo 0.39.6 (pid + start time). Not used: interprocess `SecurityDescriptor::deserialize` (it needs a `widestring` dependency) and `ListenerOptionsExt::mode` (see IPC access control (Unix)).
_Adapter note: viola has no passwords and no user store. The rows are adapted to an OS-principal model._
Password hashing — N/A: no accounts or passwords.
RBAC / permissions — capability-based, all or nothing: any caller that passes the OS check gets the full surface; no roles, the only principal being the local OS user.

IPC access control (Windows) — the listener gets an explicit protected DACL granting the user SID and SYSTEM only; the logon SID is deliberately not added, since the boundary v1 promises is the OS user; remote clients stay rejected, the first-pipe-instance behaviour is kept and the handle is not inheritable.

IPC access control (Unix) — the socket lives in a per-user 0700 directory, checked before bind and before any client connect (owner, mode, not a symlink), and is chmod 0600 right after the bind; a failed check refuses `run`, reports `instance-unreachable` to clients and fails `hook` open; `try_overwrite` stays off and the Linux abstract namespace is never used.
IPC server-side peer check (Unix) — on every accept, a peer whose euid differs from the server's is dropped before a frame is read.

IPC client-side server verification (anti-impersonation) — before the first frame of any method, the client runs the instance's strict-modes check, a refusal writing no frame and no line, and only then verifies the server against its one snapshot read: on Linux and Windows the connected peer's pid (Windows over an SQOS identification-level open) and that process's start time, a mismatch, a snapshot replayed from the log (no endpoint, pid or start time) or a check that cannot be made sending no frame, never falling back to a default connect; on Linux and macOS the client also checks the recorded endpoint's socket directory before the connect, a refusal reading `socket-dir-refused`, and past the connect admits only a peer of its own euid, an unreadable peer refused, a refusal reading `server-verify-failed`, each sending no frame; macOS compares no peer pid or start time, the named carve-out, owned by no route entry, so there `server-verify-failed` means an euid mismatch alone.

Driver-originated `release` — the wrapper refuses a `release` whose params carry a string `from` (`-32602`, `release-from-driver`), before any budget is acted on: an affordance-level guard against drivers handing the wheel back to automation, not enforcement, since a same-user process can leave out `from`.

`~/.viola/` access control — the home is owner-only (Unix 0700 directories and 0600 files, the pinned `viola` 0700; Windows the inherited profile DACL, or a protected user + SYSTEM DACL outside it), every replaced file written through `replace_private`, its mode set before any byte, never relying on the umask; a strict-modes check refuses a trusted path another user can write, a home, instance directory or `diagnostics/` another user can read (Unix any group or other bit; Windows an allow ACE granting a read right to another SID, inherit-only included) or a symlinked `diagnostics/` folder or file, in every process that reads a trusted file, before its first read or open under the home.

**Accepted risk (driver prompt injection):** driven-session output (`wait`/`last`) can prompt-inject a driver LLM into an `answer` `allow`. What to answer is policy outside viola (R1/R4). viola's only part is the closed `behavior` enum and the `unverified-cli` gate: no non-`null` decision without a `viola verify` stamp for the child's CLI version.

title: Input Validation

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/input-validation.md — read whole.
_[ALL tiers]_

**Boundary:** Validate at every point where untrusted data enters viola. Arch has two validation regimes (Established Decisions: Validation): tolerant parsing for external payloads, and versioned-tolerant parsing for viola's own formats. The requirements below are security floors that apply in both regimes. Shared validators live in `viola-core`, so the CLI, MCP and the wrapper all call the same function.

Paste text: channel `send.text`, MCP `send.text`, CLI `send` stdin/`--file` — the exact set: LF, CR and TAB allowed, every other C0 control, DEL and every C1 refused, checked over decoded `char`s; a text holding a refused character is refused whole, never stripped; the typed text is the only text `send` uses, an empty one refused `empty-text`; checked client-side and again, authoritatively, by the wrapper before anything is typed.

Dialog free text: `answer.response.message` (permission, plan) and `answer.response.answers.*` values (question) — the same exact set as `send.text`, refused `control-character`, checked first on both sides: in `viola answer` before any frame, and again, authoritatively, in the wrapper's `answer` handler.

Channel frames (IPC ndjson) — a `MAX_FRAME` cap before `read_line` (over it `-32600`, the connection closed), serde_json's default depth limit, never `unbounded_depth`, the `v` check, closed types for `behavior`, `dialog_id` and names, and each method's params checked by the wrapper (`-32602`) before `validate_paste_text`; an invalid `hook.dialog` is not registered, an invalid `hook.event` not appended.

Hook stdin (all hook events + `hook statusline`) — capped at `MAX_FRAME`, an over-limit payload detected, never silently truncated; the event maps into the closed `HookEvent`, the payload must be one JSON object, and parsing is tolerant but the fields that decide security map into closed enums; every failure fails open (exit 0, no body); `budget.json` is written by `hook statusline` alone; the hidden capture arms read no `VIOLA_*`, open no channel and always exit 0.

MCP tool inputs (`target`, `text`, `dialog_id`, `response`, `after`, `timeout_ms`) — the schemars schemas are advisory only, since rmcp does not enforce them: each handler checks the raw arguments itself (`ViolaName`, `u64`, the closed response enums, `validate_paste_text` on text and free-text answers), a failure being `invalid-params` with a closed field word and no frame.

MCP stdin (`viola mcp`'s transport, the driver's JSON-RPC lines) — each line capped at `MAX_FRAME`, its `\n` counted, by the reader viola hands rmcp, which reads stdin lines unbounded; a longer line releases no byte, is refused whole, never truncated or skipped, and ends the session as a stdin close does, recorded as one `parse-rejected` line holding no byte of it.

CLI arguments / stdin — every name through `ViolaName::try_new`; the home resolved, canonicalised and passed through the strict-modes check before any snapshot, `statusline_command` or ledger read, `ledger/stamps.json` checked before `ledger/` is created and again under its lock, a refusal reading and writing nothing; `answer` and `send` input read under `MAX_FRAME`, into the closed enums or through `validate_paste_text`, before any frame; `revive --json` prints codes, closed words and session-shaped ids only, never a path or pid.

Configuration values (`config.json`) — a tolerant parse capped at `MAX_FRAME`, `v` checked; a bad value takes its key's default, or is rejected whole, and is reported as `parse-rejected`; no value switches the budget gate off or makes the dialog hold zero or unbounded, and an identity-floor name in `claude_env_keep` has no effect.

Persistent-environment names (Windows registry) — `viola run` reads value names only, never data, into a bounded buffer; they only decide which inherited `CLAUDE*` names the R8 rule keeps, and an identity-floor name is stripped whatever the registry holds.

Test seam `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (only in a `viola` built with the test-only `fake-agent` feature) — `u64` milliseconds capped at 5 000, only holding the `run` pump back after the child starts; compiled out of every release build, it configures nothing, disables no control and widens no redaction.

Test seam `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (only in a `viola` built with the test-only `fake-agent` feature) — a closed value, panicking only on exactly `1` with a fixed ASCII payload, the hook still failing open; compiled out of every release build, it configures nothing, disables no control and widens no redaction.

Terminal colour facts `NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `COLORTERM` (read in every build, `viola list`'s human mode only) — only compared, never echoed, they decide only whether and how deep SGR bytes are written; they reach no log line, error or refusal, are never set by viola, change no escaping or check and widen no redaction.

Own state files on read (`snapshot.json`, `events.ndjson` replay/tail, `ledger/stamps.json`, `budget.json`, `heartbeat`) — each ndjson line capped at `MAX_FRAME`, an over-long, non-object or unterminated line counted as torn; a reader never writes; read only after the home strict-modes check; a snapshot that fails to parse or carries a newer `v` is replayed from the log by its readers, and a replayed one carries no `endpoint`, `pid`, `started_at` or `statusline_command`, so no frame is written and no command runs from it; `statusline_command` is trusted only because of that check, write access to it being code execution; every failed `budget.json` read is no reading.
Tailed paths (notify) — tail only `instances/<name>/events.ndjson` where `<name>` passes `ViolaName::try_new`, under the canonical home; ignore symlinks and names that fail parsing.

Child process output: `claude agents --json`, `--version` probe, `viola verify`'s interactive PTY runs — read under `MAX_FRAME` and parsed tolerantly, a failed `claude agents --json` read failing open; verify's PTY output read only against the compiled signature literals; an unwrapped row's `name` is never a `ViolaName` and never a valid `target`.

PTY output bytes (vt100) — fed under `catch_unwind`, the human's bytes written first; a caught panic or a dropped copy poisons the screen model, which then reads `input-not-ready`, while byte passthrough to the human terminal continues; the feed queue is bounded and a full queue never blocks the passthrough.

Child executable resolution (`run`, `revive`, `claude agents`) — `claude` resolved from the calling process's PATH, a same-user trust and accepted risk, its output untrusted and bounded; `viola run` resolves its child itself and hands portable-pty an absolute path; on Windows a `.cmd`/`.bat` child is refused, except a `claude` shim, resolved to its fixed `claude.exe` sibling when that exists; `revive`'s recorded `cwd` is read after the strict-modes check and used only as the spawn directory.

Session id as a child argv value (`viola revive`, `viola verify`'s Run E) — the id after `--resume` has the closed session-id shape and is one argv element of a direct spawn, never a shell, built only by `resume_args`; an `--id` the log does not hold is `no-session` before any spawn; no refusal line or hint holds the recorded directory, a pid or a logged id.

Statusline source (read at `viola run` start) — one capped, tolerant read of `<home>/statusline-source.json`, else, for the default home only, the user's `~/.claude/settings.json`: a command only from a `statusLine` of type `command`, non-empty, with no NUL, recorded as `snapshot.json`'s `statusline_command`; viola writes neither source.

Statusline shell-out (`viola hook statusline`, Unix only) — the recorded command runs only from `hook statusline`, as `/bin/sh -c` with the command as one argument, never on Windows; its stdout is capped and printed byte for byte, never parsed, its wait bounded; no log line or span carries the command, and it remains the only shell-out.

DLL search order + sideloaded ConPTY companions (Windows x64) — every `viola` process restricts the DLL search to System32 as the second statement of `main`, so a bare-name load never resolves from the CWD or `PATH`; the companions are loaded only after the owner/DACL strict-modes check of `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` and each companion, made before the held open, and a full SHA-256 re-hash under a read-share-only handle, by absolute path, and any failure, a refused check included, degrades to the inbox ConPTY, recorded only as codes, never a refusal.
File upload / webhook / SQL — N/A: no upload, webhook or database surface.

**Parser surfaces (scope for fuzz / property coverage; tests owns the cases):** `validate_paste_text`, channel ndjson framing with `MAX_FRAME`, the hook stdin parser (including `hook statusline`), the `claude agents --json` output parser, and the vt100 feed under `catch_unwind`.

**Constants:** `MAX_FRAME` = 16 MiB, one const in `viola-core`, caps every external read (channel frames, hook stdin, the statusline source and command output, `answer` input, `viola mcp`'s stdin lines, sent text, child output, ndjson lines, `config.json` and the stamps read; viola's reads of its own executable are no external input); `replace_private_shared`'s fallback compare reads its target through `take(bytes.len() + 1)`, never the whole file; it is checked against data: a stamped largest hook payload within a factor of 4 of it is a signal to revisit the cap.
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Input for input-validation bans.)

title: Data Protection

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/data-protection.md — read whole.
_Minimal tier, adapted. "HTTPS enforced" does not apply, and viola does store sensitive user content (Threat Model: Data classification), so the file-permission controls stay in scope._
**In transit:**
- **TLS:** N/A. The IPC channel is local named pipes or Unix sockets, and MCP is stdio. Confidentiality in transit depends on the IPC ACLs (Authentication & Authorization).
- **HSTS:** N/A.
- **Certificate pinning:** N/A.

- **Handle inheritance:** portable-pty 0.8.1 calls `CreateProcessW` with `bInheritHandles = 0`, and interprocess listeners stay `inheritable(false)`, so channel handles never leak into the `claude` child. Any portable-pty swap (portable-pty-psmux 0.9.7 is the named candidate) must keep this property.
**At rest — per medium:**
- **Database:** N/A (none).

**Files (`~/.viola/`):** plaintext by design, protected by OS permissions only (Unix 0700 directories and 0600 files, the pinned `viola` 0700; Windows the inherited profile DACL, or a protected user + SYSTEM DACL outside it); the plugin files and the settings override are rewritten at every start, the override written on Unix only and only for a pinned path of plain characters, since a shell runs it unquoted; the pinned binary and the ConPTY companions are re-hashed before use.

Probe captures and probe dirs are owner-only and removed when verify passes, fails or is stopped, each run's guards removing only what that run created, never by a pattern or a listing; a kill or a crash leaves them to be removed by hand.

- **Logs:**
  - `events.ndjson` and the files in `instances/<name>/diagnostics/` are 0600 inside 0700 directories.
  - serde_path_to_error drift reports, which can quote tool `input`, are written only to `diagnostics/`.
  - Logging format and fields belong to obs.

**Repository fixtures:** `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/` is recorded by `viola verify --record` from live sessions with synthetic probe prompts; before any write verify scrubs the home prefix and the user word, and refuses the whole recording when a path, the user word or an email-shaped token survives, naming the file and a closed code, never the content; recorded payloads are reviewed for home paths, usernames and tool `input` before committing.

Key management and Data lifecycle are omitted for Minimal tier: there are no keys at rest; `events.ndjson` retention and bounding is an open item owned by arch, and any rotation scheme must keep 0600/0700 permissions and valid offsets.

**Accepted risk (verify's trusted runs, B, C, D and E):** Runs B, C and D are real interactive turns under a trusted parent, so the CLI persists their transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/` and the user's own global hooks run for them; Run E adds no transcript, the print-mode probe leaves only an empty project dir, viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude`, and Run A leaves nothing.

**Accepted residual (a scratch footer reading of a newer CLI):** one `viola run` start under a tmpfs `--home`, no key typed, only the footer rows, scrubbed, written to evidence; it is no product path and no standing permission: another such reading needs its own answer.

**Accepted residual (a live round of `viola plugin install`):** a live round runs the CLI's own four plugin commands at local scope from a `proj/` outside the work tree, passing the folder-trust dialog by keys into its own pty only, never a desktop key; the CLI's writes are its own, and viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude` or into `~/.claude.json`.

**Dev-host prerequisite (the real-CLI probe):** `viola verify` against the real `claude` runs from a folder the user trusts in Claude Code whose external CLAUDE.md import is already answered; verify never answers it.

**Accepted risk (local availability):** until arch resolves `events.ndjson` retention, unbounded growth of the file can exhaust local disk, an availability impact only, with no confidentiality or integrity impact.

The test-only `viola-e2e` (`publish = false`) takes rmcp `client` only, never `transport-child-process` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers). `transport-streamable-http-server` and `auth` are banned in `deny.toml`.
