title: Dependency Security

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/dependency-security.md — read whole.
_[ALL tiers]_
**Audit tool:**
- cargo-deny `>=0.20.2` (advisories, bans, licences, sources).
- zizmor `>=1.30.1` for GitHub Actions workflows.
- cargo-audit `>=0.22.2` is not gated in v1 (it would duplicate cargo-deny advisories on the same `Cargo.lock`). It is reserved for v1.x `cargo audit bin` scans of cargo-auditable release binaries.

The vendored Microsoft ConPTY binaries sit outside every cargo graph, so no lockfile audit reaches them: their gate is `scripts/conpty-vendor.sh` (`--verify` checks the nupkg and per-file SHA-256 and the Microsoft Authenticode signer; `--probe` shows its refusals and a clean control); at run time the SHA-256 pin carries the signer. An own audit, never an exemption.
**`deny.toml` additions** (beside arch's licence list, C-crate bans and obs's telemetry-crate and `veil` / `tracing-subscriber` feature bans — arch §Build system):

- `[advisories]`: `unmaintained = "all"` (the default), `unsound = "all"`, `yanked = "deny"`, and `ignore = [{ id = "RUSTSEC-2017-0008", reason = "serial via portable-pty =0.8.1; serial ports never opened" }]`. This is the only expected ignore; re-check it whenever the portable-pty pin moves.
- `[sources]`: `unknown-registry = "deny"`, `unknown-git = "deny"` (crates.io only; this also keeps CVE-2026-5222's sparse-registry class out of reach).

- `[licenses]`: the `allow` list stays exactly `["MIT", "Apache-2.0", "Zlib", "Unicode-3.0"]` (arch §Build system). `0BSD` is admitted only per crate, by `[[licenses.exceptions]]` for `doctest-file` and `recvmsg`, the two 0BSD crates interprocess 2.4.4 pulls in (measured at chunk 2026-09-25-security-prerequisites: `cargo deny` 0.20.2 read `licenses FAILED` without them). It is never added to `allow`, so any other 0BSD crate still fails the gate, and each new exception needs its own Decisions Log entry (operator ratification `2026-09-25`).

- `[[bans.features]]`:
  - `rmcp` denies `transport-streamable-http-server` and `auth`.
  - `serde_json` denies `unbounded_depth` (every parse of external bytes keeps serde_json's default recursion limit), its firing proven by `scripts/deny-probes.sh`.

The arch bans stay as they are: C-building crates in `deny.toml`, and `tokio` in the sync crates' graph in `deny-sync.toml`, run per sync crate as the sole root, `viola-channel` covered instead by the `cargo tree` form `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`; every ban is proven live by `scripts/deny-probes.sh`.

`fuzz/` is a separate test-only cargo workspace with its own committed lockfile, outside `cargo deny`'s root graph by a ratified test-only exemption that holds only while the crate is never linked into a shipped binary and `fuzz` never joins the root `[workspace]`; its lockfile is audited separately for advisories and sources, and the C-build ban does not apply to it.
**Pinning:**

- `Cargo.lock` and `fuzz/Cargo.lock` are committed. `[workspace.dependencies]` pins every third-party version of the root graph (portable-pty `=0.8.1`), and `fuzz/Cargo.toml` pins its own crates exactly (`libfuzzer-sys =0.4.13`, `arbitrary =1.4.2`). The exception is rmcp, which takes the minor range `>=3.4.1, <3.5` (the `~3.4` pin floored at the catalogued 3.4.1), and `Cargo.lock` must resolve rmcp `>=3.4.1`.
- `Cargo.lock` must resolve bytes `>=1.11.1` (RUSTSEC-2026-0007). If obs selects tracing-subscriber, it needs `>=0.3.20` (RUSTSEC-2025-0055).
- notify stays on 8.2.0 (no 9.0 pre-release).

- The product toolchain is pinned exactly by `rust-toolchain.toml` (`channel = "1.98.1"`, rustfmt + clippy); the native Linux dev host (where `pre-push` runs) and CI install it through rustup. The workspace `rust-version` floor is 1.96, and the CI `msrv` job checks it with `rustup toolchain install 1.96 --profile minimal` selected by `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96`. The fuzz-only `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml` pins `channel = "nightly-2026-09-20"`, also installed through rustup.
- External CLI tools use minimum floors, not exact pins.

The vendored ConPTY package is pinned exactly by four pins with one textual home, `src/conpty.rs`, from which `scripts/conpty-vendor.sh` parses them; the files are committed as binary, and a version move is a re-vendor through the script's default mode, never a hand copy.

- `viola-harness pre-push` runs on the native Linux dev host and is never a new version source: its `tools` stage checks the host against CI's own pins — `cc`, the `rust-toolchain.toml` channel, and the cargo-nextest, cargo-mutants and cargo-llvm-cov versions it parses from ci.yml's `test`-job `tool:` line — and installs nothing. It refuses `tool-pin-mismatch` when an installed tool differs from its pin line, and `tool-missing: cc` for an absent C toolchain. No harness command, gate or pre-push stage launches anything as uid 0, and no provisioning script exists (§Secret Management, Development).

**Update policy:** Manual review, triggered by the scheduled advisory run below. No automated update bot was researched (see the Decisions Log). The rmcp minor range (`>=3.4.1, <3.5`) makes the scheduled run the main signal for that crate.
**CI integration** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, `.github/workflows/windows-mutants.yml`):

- Job 4 (ubuntu) runs `cargo deny check` over all four check families, and fails the build on any advisory, yanked crate or unknown source. It covers the root `Cargo.lock` only. The same job then audits `fuzz/Cargo.lock` for advisories and sources in its own step (see the `fuzz/` exemption above).

- A separate workflow, `nightly.yml` (weekly `schedule:` cron + `workflow_dispatch`, no cache), runs `cargo deny check advisories` and `cargo deny --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml check advisories`, because the advisory DB changes without code changes (the default `maximum-db-staleness` is P90D). Its `fuzz` job installs `cargo-fuzz@0.13.2` with `cargo install --locked`, runs each target for 120 s on the `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml` nightly, and uploads `fuzz/artifacts/` on failure.

`windows-mutants.yml` runs only on `workflow_dispatch`, with no `inputs:`, at the epoch-boundary audit; it is never a gate and never a dependency of `ci.yml`, holds workflow `permissions: {}` and `contents: read` on its one job, SHA-pinned actions, `matrix.*` only through `env:`, and uses no secret, cache or `needs:` and uploads nothing.

- The workflows carry no `concurrency:` block. zizmor's pedantic `concurrency-limits` (3 low findings, one per workflow, as read with zizmor 1.30.1 on the dev host 2026-10-04) was declined on 2026-09-24 and stays visible: a concurrency group cancels pending runs even with `cancel-in-progress: false`, which would drop a cancelled run's `always()` gate and upload chain. (No push or pull-request run carries a mutation job since 2026-09-28 — mutation testing moved to the epoch-boundary code audit, and `windows-mutants.yml` uploads nothing — so a cancelled run cannot lose mutation coverage; that half of the original reason is retired.) The default persona, which CI runs, does not report it.

- The per-OS `test` job's `windows-2025`-only step `ConPTY vendor verification` runs `bash scripts/conpty-vendor.sh --verify` and `--probe` before the coverage run (verdicts `conpty-vendor: verified 1.24.260710001` and `conpty-vendor probe: 4/4 refused, control clean`) and fails the build otherwise.

- The per-OS `release` job builds `cargo build --release --locked --bin viola` through `scripts/release-check.sh`. The script judges that build's own `compiler-artifact` records, never a `target/release/` listing. It refuses any executable other than `viola`, and any artifact whose `features` include a test-only feature (`test-support`, `fake-agent`): `release-check: FAILED — test-only feature {feature} in {target}`. `--probe` runs first and must read 5/5 refused with a clean control. `viola-channel`'s test-only `test-support` feature (shared test helpers) is enabled only by the root package's `[dev-dependencies]`.
- `zizmor .github/workflows/` runs on the ubuntu leg and fails on unpinned actions, `excessive-permissions`, template injection and cache poisoning.

- The per-OS `perf` job (job-level `contents: read`) installs hyperfine with `cargo install --locked hyperfine@1.20.0` as its own step (no new action, no `github.event` value) and runs `agent-run run --perf`, then G2, G4 and its own `secret-scan`. Its uploads `perf-<os>` (hyperfine exports) and `diag-perf-<os>` (the perf home's diagnostics) go up only when that scan succeeds, and `secret-scan-perf-<os>` only when it fails; every input is synthetic (obs-plan §8 item 6).

CI's G2 zero-panics gate has exactly one exemption, a role-file `panic` line whose `panic_location` is exactly the `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` seam's, compared as a whole string, its `--probe` run before every G2 check; any further G2 exemption needs its own Decisions Log entry.
Actions are pinned by full commit SHA with a version comment (the set `ci.yml` uses), `actions/checkout` with `persist-credentials: false`.

- Toolchains come from `rustup toolchain install` steps: `rust-toolchain.toml`, `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml` (run in `working-directory: fuzz`, in the fuzz jobs) and `1.96` in the `msrv` job (selected with `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96`). No toolchain action is used.

- A value from the event payload reaches a step only through `env:`, never through `${{ }}` inside `run:`. Today no workflow reads a `github.event` value at all. `ci.yml` runs no mutation job. `run --mutants` (local, and the epoch-boundary code audit) derives its base from git history, with `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` only a local override. The dispatch-only `windows-mutants.yml` runs the `--package` arm, which reads no base.
- Workflow-level `permissions: {}` and job-level `contents: read`.
- Optionally, enable GitHub's Actions policy for SHA pinning on the repository.
**Critical CVE response SLA:**
- Within 7 days of a RustSec/GHSA advisory against a crate and feature viola enables: bump, or swap along arch's named path (portable-pty → portable-pty-psmux 0.9.7).
- Within 7 days of an advisory confined to a disabled feature: add a `deny.toml` `ignore` entry with a `reason` naming the disabled feature.

> **Tool-version syntax.** External CLI / audit tools (cargo-audit, cargo-deny, gitleaks, govulncheck — binaries
> installed via `cargo install` etc., whose signal is fetched fresh at runtime) are expressed as minimum
> **floors** (`>=0.22`), NOT exact pins — an exact pin triggers a false drift escalation when a patch-behind
> build is installed. Exact pins are only for lock-pinnable library deps in the lockfile.

_Supply chain integrity subsection omitted (Standard + Hardened only). v1.x release prerequisites are recorded in the Security Decisions Log._
**v1.x release prerequisites** (Supply chain integrity, deferred with the release):
- dist `>=0.33.0` with GitHub Artifact Attestations and Azure Artifact Signing (x86_64).
- cargo-auditable `>=0.7.6`, plus `cargo audit bin` (cargo-audit `>=0.22.2`) run on the release binaries.
- self_update 1.3.0 built with `signatures` (zipsign).
- zizmor's cache-poisoning findings addressed.
- No `rust-cache` in the release workflow.
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Code Patterns for supply-chain bans.)

title: Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project)

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/bootstrap-phases.md — read whole.
_[ALL tiers — adapted for Minimal with local-boundary elevations]_

The downstream skills derive the following bootstrap phases from
the contract above. Listed for explicitness — route may reorder /
combine, setup-project may add stack-specific intermediate steps.

**auth-scaffolding-baseline:** narrowed to the local boundary, no auth library: per-OS listener hardening and client server verification in `viola-channel`, owner-only home creation, the strict-modes checks and the pinned binary's SHA-256 re-hash in `viola-state`, and code-bearing files rewritten at every start, every exec-form `command` the absolute pinned path; each arch amendment is folded in before the first chunk that implements it.

- **input-validation-library-install:** No new library. nutype 0.8.0 is already in the stack, and arch rejected garde/validator.
  - Wire `ViolaName::try_new` into the clap `value_parser`, the MCP handlers, the channel `link`/`unlink` params and the notify path filter.
  - Add `viola_core::validate_paste_text` and the `control-character` detail.
  - Add the `MAX_FRAME` const and the `Read::take` wrappers on every external reader.

- **dep-audit-tooling-install:** cargo-deny `>=0.20.2` with the `deny.toml` `[advisories]`, `[sources]` and `[[bans.features]]` additions; zizmor `>=1.30.1`. cargo-audit `>=0.22.2` is deferred to v1.x binary scans. For the vendored ConPTY binaries: `scripts/conpty-vendor.sh` (re-vendor by default; `--verify`: the nupkg and per-file SHA-256 plus the Authenticode signer; `--probe`).
- **secret-management-init:** N/A for stored secrets (none in v1).

**secret-scanning-ci-gate:** no repo secret scanner in v1, there being no secrets in the repo or CI; the CI `test` job runs obs-plan §9's artifact canary scan against this plan's NEVER-log floor, never printing or writing the matched bytes, and every scan-gated upload waits for it to pass; one upload leaves CI unscanned, admissible by content: the nightly fuzz job's crash inputs, mutated from the committed synthetic corpus, which a non-synthetic seed must first drop.

- **error-sanitization-wire:**
  - The `Display` impls on the product error enums (`thiserror`, or hand-written for `PtyError`; §Error Handling lists them) must not interpolate upstream text or absolute paths.
  - MCP `structuredContent` carries only `refusal`/`detail`/`error` codes.
  - anyhow chains stop at the `viola` bin's human-mode stderr. A chain printed there never includes a serde_json or serde_path_to_error source, or any other source whose `Display` can quote upstream text (serde errors quote the offending value). Map it to a fixed message before it joins the chain, and write the full error only to `instances/<name>/diagnostics/` when an instance is resolved (NEVER-log floor, `logging-redaction-wire`).

- **logging-redaction-wire:** Security floors that obs must satisfy (obs owns the logger and format; the Logging section is skipped at Minimal tier). This list is the consolidated NEVER-log floor. Data Protection § Logs, Error Handling and Anti-Patterns § Secrets / § Logging restate parts of it and must not diverge from it:
  - Never write `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` or any other R8-stripped `CLAUDE*` value to any log, diagnostic, snapshot, `events.ndjson` or fixture.
  - Scope: this floor governs log lines, diagnostics and error output. It does not restrict the contract payloads that carry content by design: `events.ndjson`, `wait`/`last` results (CLI and MCP), `hook.dialog`, and `statusline_command` in `snapshot.json` (the user's command stands there only; `instances/<name>/settings.json` holds the pinned path and the words `hook statusline`). Outside those payloads, user content (prompts, `last_assistant_message`, plan, question and option text), tool `input`, the `statusline_command` string, and serde_path_to_error drift reports (paths and values) go only to `instances/<name>/diagnostics/`. They never go to stderr log or error lines, CLI `--json` error output, MCP `isError` results or channel `error.data`.
  - Operational metadata (TMS §1): absolute paths, which carry the OS username (the only PII in scope), and internal type names never go to CLI `--json` error output, MCP `isError` results or channel `error.data`. Pids, `agent_session_id`, `started_at` and `budget.json` values may be written to `diagnostics/`.
  - `diagnostics/` files are 0600.
  - Human-mode CLI output of `wait`/`last` escapes C0/C1 controls (keeping `\n` and `\t`). Human-mode `list` rows escape every control character, `\n`, `\t`, DEL and C1 included, as `\xHH` text (`escape_row`), so each row stays one line: since chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board an unwrapped row's NAME (the row's `sessionId`) is taken from `claude agents --json` and printed through the same `escape_row`, on one line, its width counted in characters; every other field is viola's own state or a closed word (STATUS `idle` · `busy` · `unknown`, `n/a`).
  - If obs picks tracing-subscriber, the floor is `>=0.3.20`.

- **dep-security-ci-gate:** Wire the scheduled weekly `cargo deny check advisories`, the zizmor step, SHA-pinned actions and `permissions: {}` / `contents: read` into `ci.yml`. The `test` job's `windows-2025` step `ConPTY vendor verification` (`conpty-vendor.sh --verify`, `--probe`).
- **supply-chain-signing-init:** Skipped (Minimal tier; no release in v1). The v1.x prerequisites are in the Decisions Log.

route uses this list to plan phase ordering (typically:
auth-scaffolding-baseline (if applicable) → input-validation-library-install
→ dep-audit-tooling-install → secret-management-init →
secret-scanning-ci-gate → error-sanitization-wire →
logging-redaction-wire → dep-security-ci-gate →
supply-chain-signing-init (if applicable)). setup-project uses this
list to materialize each phase's bootstrap script + dependency list +
CI workflow snippet.

title: Secret Management

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/secret-management.md — read whole.
_[ALL tiers]_
**Storage:**

**Production:** no stored secrets in v1, and environment variables are not a configuration channel; the inherited `CLAUDE*` credentials stay only in the `viola run` wrapper's environment, removed from the child by the R8 rule (the identity floor whatever the persistent set says) and never serialised into events, snapshots, diagnostics or the ledger; the strip handles names only and never reads a value.

**Development:** same as production, tests using their own `--home`; the local pre-push gate runs only on Linux and launches every child under `env -i` with exactly `HOME` and `PATH`, so no host environment value crosses into a child; any assignment whose value comes from the host is a boundary widening needing its own Decisions Log entry, and no uid-0 launch exists.
**Never in code:** No token, key or credential literal in source or in the embedded plugin files (`hooks.json`, `.mcp.json`, `plugin.json` carry only exec paths).

**Secret scanning in CI:** No repo secret scanner in v1. The repo and CI hold no secrets, and security-research.md catalogues no secret scanner (see the Decisions Log). Revisit when the v1.x release workflow adds signing credentials.
What CI does run is the obs-owned artifact canary scan (`viola-harness secret-scan`, `id: secret-scan`, `if: always()`, obs-plan §9 step 3). Its classes:
- the stripped `CLAUDE*` canaries (the twelve `claude-stripped` needles);
- the `cookie:` header, case-insensitive;
- the content canary, which fails only in home-level role files;
- a non-`0600` diagnostics file, Unix only.

It reads every file under `target/agent-run/` except `run --mutants`' `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`, which is skipped by exact path and excluded from the `harness-<os>` upload, so it is never uploaded. It never prints or writes the matched bytes, and the test-home uploads run only when it succeeds.
**Rotation cadence:**
- **API keys / DB passwords:** N/A.
- **JWT signing keys:** N/A.
- **TLS certificates:** N/A.
**Access auditing:** N/A in v1 (no secret manager).
**What counts as secret:**
- The inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN` / `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`.
- From v1.x: Azure Artifact Signing credentials (dist) and the zipsign private key (self_update `signatures`), both held only as CI secrets in the release workflow.
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Secrets for secret-handling bans.)

title: Error Handling

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/error-handling.md — read whole.
_[ALL tiers]_
**External responses** (to channel clients, CLI `--json` and MCP drivers): sanitised.
- No anyhow context chains, no absolute paths, no upstream text (prompts, tool `input`, assistant output), no serde_path_to_error paths or values, and no internal type names.

- The `Display` impls on `PtyError` (hand-written) and on `AgentError`, `ChannelError`, `StateError`, `PinError`, `StampsError`, `StampsReadError`, `Refused`, `McpError` and `ServeError` (`thiserror`) use fixed messages. Variant fields that hold paths or payloads are excluded from `Display`.
- Channel `-32603` uses a fixed `message` ("internal error") with `data: null`.

- MCP `isError` results carry only the `structuredContent` codes from Conventions (`refusal`/`detail`, or `error: instance-unreachable | wrapper-fault | invalid-params` — `instance-unreachable` with `detail` its closed cause, `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, `wrapper-fault` with `{code,message,data}` as `viola_channel::sanitised_fault` closes them, never the peer's own, `invalid-params` with a closed field word), a `refusal` that is no code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`) reading `unknown` and a string `detail` that is none reading null, `of_reply` here and `reply_of` on CLI `--json` alike, and every `isError` text is `refused: <code>`. Any other handler fault, a reply of no known shape or a panicked call is the JSON-RPC error `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers).
**Internal logging (for debugging):**

- Full error detail goes only to `instances/<name>/diagnostics/` (files 0600; format owned by obs) or, for short-lived CLI verbs, to stderr. stderr never carries upstream text, tool `input`, drift-report values or any other value on the NEVER-log floor (Bootstrap phases, `logging-redaction-wire`).

`hook` never writes to stderr and never exits non-zero: a security check failing in `hook` still ends in exit 0 with no body, so the dialog renders for the human; its hidden capture arms print nothing on every failure, their stderr always empty, their exit always 0.
**Error format:**

- **Channel:** JSON-RPC `error` for protocol faults, including `-32600` for frames over `MAX_FRAME` and `-32602` for `release`-with-`from`, and `result.refusal` for `not-delivered`/`control-character` and `not-delivered`/`empty-text`.
**Error reporting integration:** None. viola makes no outbound network calls. If obs ever adds an external reporter, the Logging bans below apply before transmission.
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Logging for error-disclosure bans.)

title: Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)

body: _[ALL tiers — single source of truth for all security bans]_

title: Authentication

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/security-anti-patterns.md — read whole.
- NEVER create an interprocess Windows listener without `ListenerOptionsExt::security_descriptor`. The default DACL grants read to Everyone and anonymous.
- NEVER place a Unix socket directly in `/tmp` or at the `$TMPDIR` root (`/tmp/viola-<h12>.sock`). Always use a verified 0700 per-user directory (the Kea DHCP CVE-2025-32801/32802/32803 precedent).

- NEVER rely on the socket file's 0600 mode as the only Unix control: `unix(7)` says socket permissions may be ignored. NEVER set it with `ListenerOptionsExt::mode`: it returns `Unsupported` on macOS, which fails the bind; chmod after the bind instead.
- NEVER use Linux abstract-namespace sockets (no filesystem permissions).

- NEVER write any channel frame before verifying the server against a `snapshot.json` that passed the strict-modes check in the same process (the euid check never skipped), except the named carve-out: macOS's pid and start-time check (no peer pid), owned by no route entry, its euid and verified socket-directory checks standing; no other frame or process may borrow it.

- NEVER open a Windows client pipe without `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION` (the default `connect_without_waiting` lets a squatter with SeImpersonatePrivilege impersonate the client).
- NEVER treat the channel `from` param as an authenticated identity. It is self-reported and serves link records and the `release` affordance guard only.
- Account-flow bans (reset enumeration, recovery questions, login rate limiting): N/A. There are no accounts or login endpoints (Threat Model: Auth model).

title: Input

body: - NEVER trust schemars MCP schemas or client-side CLI checks alone. The wrapper re-runs `ViolaName::try_new`, the closed-enum deserialisation and `validate_paste_text`.
- NEVER join `instances/<name>` with a string that did not come out of `ViolaName::try_new` (MCP `target`, `link`/`unlink` params, notify events).

- NEVER write `send.text` or answer free text into the PTY if it contains any C0 control other than LF, CR and TAB (ESC above all), DEL (U+007F) or any C1 control (U+0080–U+009F), and NEVER strip them silently. Reject with `control-character`. The wrapper's `send` typing every CR LF pair and every other CR inside a text as one LF, and dropping its trailing CR and LF characters, of a text that has already passed `validate_paste_text` is not this stripping: CR and LF are allowed characters, validation runs first on the text as received, and no refused character is ever removed or typed (§Input Validation, Paste text row). Answer free text is typed as validated. NEVER refuse LF, CR or TAB: multi-line relays, plans and answers are normal. Refusing a text whose typed text is empty (`empty-text`) is not a refusal of those characters: there is nothing to type, and a text with content is never refused for holding LF, CR or TAB.
- NEVER run the control-character check over raw bytes. Check decoded `char`s, or valid UTF-8 continuation bytes (0x80–0xBF) are misread as C1.

- NEVER call `read_line` on a channel stream or `read_to_end` on hook stdin or child output without `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)`, and NEVER hand rmcp a `viola mcp` stdin reader that does not cap each line at `MAX_FRAME`, nor truncate or skip an over-long line instead of ending the session.
- NEVER enable serde_json's `unbounded_depth` feature; `deny.toml` bans it (§Dependency Security).
- NEVER model `behavior`, `dialog_id`, the wheel holder or the dialog kind as free `String`s. Use closed enums or integers even under tolerant parsing.
- NEVER use a `claude agents --json` row `name` as a `ViolaName` or `target`.
- SQL ban: N/A (no database or query language).

title: Data Protection

body: - NEVER create `~/.viola/`, `--home` or any file under it with the default umask. Directories are 0700 and files 0600 (`OpenOptionsExt::mode`); the only exception is the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` at 0700, and NEVER make it group- or world-writable. On Windows, NEVER accept a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%` without an explicit protected user + SYSTEM DACL, and NEVER skip the Windows owner + DACL strict-modes check at startup (`#[cfg(windows)]` must not return `Ok(())` unchecked), and NEVER pass a NULL DACL, a volume without persistent ACLs, or an inherit-only `GENERIC_*` grant just because no specific-rights ACE matched.
- NEVER run `statusline_command` from a `snapshot.json` whose home or instance directory fails the strict-modes check. Write access there equals code execution.

- NEVER reuse an existing `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` without re-hashing it (SHA-256, truncated) against `<hash>`, NEVER derive `<hash>` from a non-cryptographic hash (FNV, `DefaultHasher`), and NEVER reuse existing `plugin/` files without rewriting them. NEVER load or launch a `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` companion without its full SHA-256 re-hash against the compiled pin through a `FILE_SHARE_READ`-only handle held until the spawn, and NEVER overwrite or delete a companion that fails it (left as found; the child runs on the inbox ConPTY).
- NEVER spawn a `.cmd`/`.bat` PTY child through portable-pty. Resolve to a real `.exe` (portable-pty 0.8.1 bypasses std's BatBadBut escaping).
- NEVER make channel handles inheritable, and NEVER adopt a portable-pty replacement that calls `CreateProcessW` with `bInheritHandles = TRUE`.

- NEVER commit `fixtures/claude/*` recorded from sessions that used real (non-synthetic) prompts, or before checking them for home paths and usernames (a `workspace.repo` naming this repository's own remote is kept, Data Protection → Repository fixtures).

title: API

body: - NEVER enable rmcp's `transport-streamable-http-server` or `auth` features.
- NEVER skip request size limits: `MAX_FRAME` on the channel and on each `viola mcp` stdin line.

title: Secrets

body: - NEVER write `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` or any R8-stripped `CLAUDE*` value into any log or stderr, `events.ndjson`, snapshots, `diagnostics/` or fixtures (consolidated floor: Bootstrap phases, `logging-redaction-wire`).
- NEVER commit `.env` files, local `--home` test directories or signing material to git.
- NEVER hardcode credentials in source or in the `include_str!` plugin files.

title: Logging

body: - NEVER echo serde_path_to_error drift reports or anyhow chains into MCP `structuredContent` or channel `error.data`, and NEVER print an anyhow chain to stderr that still contains a serde_json or serde_path_to_error source (its `Display` quotes input values such as tool `input`).
- NEVER write to stderr from `viola hook`, and NEVER exit non-zero from it, including on security-check failures.
- NEVER print `wait`/`last` human-mode output, or `list` rows taken from `claude agents --json`, to a terminal without escaping C0/C1 controls (the same class as RUSTSEC-2025-0055).
- NEVER use tracing-subscriber `<0.3.20` if obs selects it.
- NEVER create `diagnostics/` files readable by other users.
- NEVER expose absolute paths in any external error.

title: Code Patterns

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/security-anti-patterns.md — read whole.

- NEVER interpret upstream text (prompts, `last_assistant_message`, plan text, question and option text, tool `input`) as a viola command or config (R1). `statusline_command` is the only shell-out, and NEVER add a second one.

- NEVER build screen signatures, harness prefixes or local-command lists from runtime or upstream text. They come only from compiled `viola-agent-claude` ledger rows. The harness prefixes are four compiled literals matched on the prompt's raw start, no trim (`<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message`, `<cross-session-message`); the escaped cross-session form is the one escaped tag that classifies `harness`, so a human who types it at a prompt's start is filed `harness` (the founder's ratified side effect, Decisions Log `2026-09-29`).
- NEVER enable interprocess `try_overwrite` (TOCTOU deletion of an attacker-swapped file).
- NEVER feed vt100 outside `catch_unwind`. A parser panic must not take down the human's terminal path.
- NEVER reference a GitHub Action by `@stable`, `@v2` or any mutable ref. Use a full SHA with a version comment.
- NEVER restore `Swatinem/rust-cache` in the v1.x release workflow.
- NEVER ship `self_update` without its `signatures` feature (zipsign). A checksum from the same release proves nothing.

- NEVER let `run --mutants` wipe any directory except the Windows host mutation scratch `<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch`, guarded by its exact final component; NEVER re-create it without owner-only permissions, loosen the strict-modes check for it, fall back to `%TEMP%` or the repository, or print the path.

- NEVER let a test-side removal under `target/e2e-home` take anything but a dir the test side itself created; its two keepers NEVER follow a linked base unless its target is absolute and an owner-only real directory, create the target 0700 and remove nothing; `viola` itself never reads or writes the backing by that name.

title: Universal

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/security-anti-patterns.md — read whole.
- NEVER add a listener (TCP port, WebSocket, `http` hooks, MCP HTTP transport) or a new channel method without a Security Decisions Log entry mapping it to this plan's IPC controls.
- NEVER let a security refusal block the human. Refusals go only to automation (`send`/`answer`), and hooks fail open.

- NEVER let a `viola` process on Windows reach any DLL load before `viola_pty::sideload::restrict_dll_search()` (System32-only default search, the second statement of `main` in every role): a bare-name load, portable-pty's `LoadLibraryW("conpty.dll")` included, must never resolve from the CWD or `PATH`. NEVER pre-load the sideloaded `conpty.dll` by a relative path. A sideload failure degrades to the inbox ConPTY silently: NEVER a refusal, an exit change or a byte on the human's terminal.

- NEVER let an exec-form `command` in the embedded `hooks.json` or `.mcp.json`, or in `viola plugin install`'s `.mcp.json`, or the statusline command `viola run` writes into `instances/<name>/settings.json` (it wraps the statusline with `viola hook statusline`), resolve `viola` through PATH. It must be the absolute pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` path, or the absolute path of the exe that ran `plugin install`. Claude Code runs these on every hook event and for MCP, so a PATH lookup hands code execution to whatever is earliest on the session's PATH (architecture.md Deployment / Distribution and Plugin Scope; Threat Model Sec 2, child process spawning and PATH resolution).

- NEVER answer a `hook.dialog` with a non-`null` decision unless `ledger/stamps.json` holds a `viola verify` stamp for the child's CLI version on which every relied ledger row passes, and NEVER let any process other than `viola verify` write `ledger/stamps.json`: a stamp is what switches on dialog answering, PermissionRequest `allow` included.

- NEVER answer a `hook.dialog` with a non-`null` decision unless `viola run`'s version gate read `ledger/stamps.json` through the strict-modes check (`read_stamps_strict`); a refusal is `cli_verified:false`.

- NEVER let a process other than the instance's own wrapper write `instances/<name>/snapshot.json`. `endpoint`, `pinned_bin` and `statusline_command` in it decide where clients connect and what `hook statusline` executes (architecture.md Instance snapshot, "written only by that instance's wrapper"; Threat Model Sec 1 config).

- NEVER let `config.json`, a `VIOLA_*` environment variable or a CLI flag switch off any control in this plan (the IPC DACL or socket-directory check, the peer or server verification, the home strict-modes check, `validate_paste_text`): environment variables are not a configuration channel. The carve-outs, the two test-only seams and the terminal colour facts, switch off nothing; NEVER add another such seam or environment read without its own Decisions Log entry.

title: Security Decisions Log

body: History: security-plan-amendments.md (live); the log moved verbatim to security-plan-amendments-archive.md (U35).

- **Requirement:** Password hashing
  - **Implementation:** N/A. No accounts or passwords (Established Decisions: Personal v1).
  - **Stack reference:** —

- **Requirement:** RBAC / permissions
  - **Implementation:** Capability-based, all or nothing. Any caller that passes the OS check (IPC) gets the full surface: the nine served methods (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `hook.dialog`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`) and the `hook.event` notification, each behind the IPC rows below and its own params check (§ Input Validation, Channel frames). No roles, because the only principal is the local OS user (Threat Model: Auth model).
  - **Stack reference:** Enforcement rows below

- **Requirement:** IPC access control (Windows)
  - **Implementation:** The listener gets an explicit protected DACL, `D:P(A;;GA;;;<user-SID>)(A;;GA;;;SY)`: the user SID + SYSTEM only. The SDDL string is converted to a descriptor with windows-sys (`Win32_Security_Authorization`), owned, and passed to `ListenerOptionsExt::security_descriptor`. Windows reads it back in its own canonical form, `D:P(A;;FA;;;<sid>)(A;;FA;;;SY)` (GA maps to FA on a pipe), and may render the user SID as an alias (`LA` for the built-in Administrator), as measured in CI run 36313377307; the control is the protected flag plus exactly those two allow ACEs. The SID comes from `GetTokenInformation(TokenUser)` + `ConvertSidToStringSidW`. The logon SID is deliberately **not** added: a driver and a driven session in different logon sessions of the same user (an SSH or scheduled-task driver later) must still connect, and the boundary v1 promises is the OS user. Keep `accept_remote(false)` (the default, `PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS`), the `FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE` behaviour (a squatted name gives exit 1 per Session Liveness) and `inheritable(false)`.
  - **Stack reference:** `viola-channel` server, `#[cfg(windows)]`; interprocess 2.4.4; windows-sys 0.61.2

- **Requirement:** IPC access control (Unix)
  - **Implementation:** **Primary control:** the socket lives in a per-user directory with mode 0700: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` on Linux, `$TMPDIR/viola/` on macOS, and `/tmp/viola-<uid>/` only as a fallback. The endpoint becomes `<dir>/viola-<h12>.sock`. **Directory check:** before bind, and again before any client connect, `lstat` the directory and require owner == `geteuid()`, `mode & 0o077 == 0` and not a symlink. On failure `run` refuses to start (exit 1), CLI/MCP clients report `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `socket-dir-refused` (the CLI exit 21), and `hook` fails open (exit 0, empty streams, one `hook-decision` of `detail` `socket-dir-refused` at WARN) without writing any frame. **Socket-directory failure at bind:** a failed create and a refused check read one code: `run` and the start of `revive` exit 1 with `socket-dir-refused` and one `process-exit` of that `detail`; a `Server::bind` failure is outside this code. **Secondary control:** the socket file is chmod 0600 right after the bind, on every Unix OS. `ListenerOptionsExt::mode(0o600)` is not used: interprocess 2.4.4 returns `Unsupported` on macOS, which fails the bind, and ignoring it would leave the macOS socket at the umask mode. `try_overwrite` stays off. Linux abstract namespace is never used.
  - **Stack reference:** `viola-channel` server, `#[cfg(unix)]`; interprocess 2.4.4; `viola-state` `strict` (`check_socket_dir`, `socket_dir_verdict`, and `check_endpoint_dir`, called by `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/cmd/client.rs`, `src/cmd/hook.rs` and `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`)

- **Requirement:** IPC access control (Unix), the directory verdict
  - **Implementation:** `viola_state::strict::check_socket_dir` makes one `symlink_metadata` read of the path: an absent path passes and an unstattable one is `Refused::Unreadable`; then the plain `socket_dir_verdict` reads a symlink as `Refused::Symlink`, a non-directory as `Refused::NotADirectory` ("a trusted state path is not a directory"), and anything else through `unix_read_verdict`. Off Unix `check_socket_dir` returns `Ok(())`.
  - **Stack reference:** `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs` (`check_socket_dir`, `socket_dir_verdict`)

- **Requirement:** IPC access control (Unix), a refused directory
  - **Implementation:** The socket-directory check never chmods: a refused directory stays as found.
  - **Stack reference:** `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs` (`check_socket_dir`); `tests/security_negatives_socket_dir.rs`

- **Requirement:** IPC access control (Unix), the recorded endpoint
  - **Implementation:** `check_endpoint_dir` is the check on a recorded endpoint's parent, the one helper the bind and the three client seams share.
  - **Stack reference:** `crates/viola-state/src/strict.rs` (`check_endpoint_dir`); `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/cmd/client.rs`, `src/cmd/hook.rs`, `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`

- **Requirement:** IPC access control (Unix), at a start
  - **Implementation:** `socket_dir_ready` runs `check_endpoint_dir`, creates the parent only when absent, then checks again, so a race's loser reads the same. It runs before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, and the start of `revive` shares it; its refusal is the **Socket-directory failure at bind:** clause of IPC access control (Unix).
  - **Stack reference:** `src/cmd/run.rs` (`socket_dir_ready`, `refuse_socket_dir`, `enum Bound`)

- **Requirement:** IPC access control (Unix), a leftover socket file
  - **Implementation:** A killed wrapper's socket file stays in the per-user directory until a next bind of that name takes it over: nothing removes it, by choice, a harmless file in a 0700 directory.
  - **Stack reference:** `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/cleanup.rs` (`unconnectable`, which removes no leftover file)

- **Requirement:** IPC server-side peer check (Unix)
  - **Implementation:** On every accept, `stream.peer_creds()`; if `euid() != geteuid()`, drop the connection before reading a frame.
  - **Stack reference:** `viola-channel` sync server (`crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs`, `accept_loop`), the one server; `TokioClient` is a client

- **Requirement:** IPC server-side peer check (Unix), the drop
  - **Implementation:** The drop filters `incoming()` in `accept_loop` by the peer's euid decision on the accept thread, before the stream's worker thread and before any frame: the peer reads end-of-file, and no line and nothing on the terminal is written.
  - **Stack reference:** `crates/viola-channel/src/server.rs` (`accept_loop`, `serve_admitting`), the decision `peer_admitted`

- **Requirement:** IPC client-side server verification (anti-impersonation)
  - **Implementation:** **Windows client open:** open the pipe through windows-sys ` CreateFileW(..., SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, ...) `, then adopt the handle with `interprocess::os::windows::named_pipe::local_socket::Stream::try_from(OwnedHandle)`. The adoption spike passed (Decisions Log `2026-09-25`): after adoption a same-user server reads `SecurityIdentification`, as measured at chunk 2026-09-25-security-prerequisites (research.md §Measured facts, CI run 36138441784 windows-2025), and `tests/channel_sqos_open.rs` pins the recipe. `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` is required: a non-overlapped handle adopted this way hangs its first exchange (same measurement). The client never falls back to interprocess's default connect, which opens without SQOS and lets the server impersonate (measured: `SecurityImpersonation`) (§ Authentication). **Windows identity check:** the connected stream's peer pid (the observed server pid, below) must equal the snapshot `pid`, and sysinfo's process start time must equal snapshot `started_at`. **Unix identity check:** `peer_creds().euid()` must equal `geteuid()` (checked at `cmd::client::connect`, the `connect` of `cmd::hook` and the `frame` of `viola-mcp`, through `peer_admitted`; a peer whose euid cannot be read is refused, and a refused euid reads `server-verify-failed`), and where available (Linux/FreeBSD) `peer_creds().pid()` must equal the snapshot `pid`, with the sysinfo start-time match (built on Linux, the `SO_PEERCRED` peer pid). **macOS:** `peer_creds()` gives no pid, so verification there is euid + the verified 0700 socket directory, with no pid check. This is accepted for v1 (macOS is CI-only, brief O5) and recorded as a known gap for the public version. **Timing:** all of this runs before the first frame of any method is written on the connection, including `hook.event` notifications (UserPromptSubmit, Stop and PostToolUse carry prompt text, `last_assistant_message` and tool data) and `wait`/`last` requests, not only `send`, `answer` and `hook.dialog`.

A security check failing in `hook` (server verification mismatch, refused socket directory, oversized stdin, strict-modes failure) still ends in exit 0 with no body, so the dialog renders for the human. As landed, `viola hook <event>` runs the stdin cap, the `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` shape checks and the one-object parse and, on Unix, the socket-directory and peer euid checks and, on Linux and Windows, the server verification (macOS the recorded gap), and fails open with `hook-decision` detail `oversize-stdin` · `malformed-json` · `channel-unreachable` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`. Before it reads the diagnostics level or initialises obs, the event and dialog paths run the instance's strict-modes check (`canonical`, then `trusted`): a refused or absent instance, a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing directory included, exits 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd append; the two `--capture` arms run ahead of that check. Its hidden `--capture <DIR>` arm runs the stdin cap, the absolute, existing `<DIR>` check and the exclusive `create_private_new` claim, and writes the capture raw; with `--answers <DIR>` it also runs the `take(64)` closed-`ProbeAnswer` read and `probe_body`'s payload shape check, and prints one `decision_body` body to stdout only for a mapped answer. Its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]` runs the same stdin cap and `<DIR>` check and claim, writes the payload raw and the closed shell verdict, and prints nothing on any path. On every failure it prints nothing, its stderr is always empty, and it exits 0 (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, capture arm; the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05 on `--answers`; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows («Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`), on the statusline form).

- **Vector:** Local IPC, the wrapper channel (JSON-RPC 2.0 over ndjson). This is the highest-impact surface.
  - **Entry point:**
    - One endpoint per `viola run`: named pipe `\\.\pipe\viola-<h12>` on Windows, socket file `<dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` on Unix, `<dir>` the per-user 0700 directory (§ Authentication & Authorization, IPC access control (Unix)).
    - Methods: `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`, `hook.dialog`, and `hook.event` notifications.
    - Whoever can connect can type prompts into the driven Claude session (`send`) and allow PermissionRequest dialogs (`answer` with `behavior:"allow"`). That amounts to running arbitrary tools, and so arbitrary code, as the user. They can also read the whole conversation (`wait`, `last`).
    - Whoever can connect can also add or remove a driver link (`link` / `unlink`), whose effect is a `link` / `unlink` line in `events.ndjson` and the snapshot's links only; neither method reads the self-reported `from`.
    - Sources: Occupied Resources (IPC endpoints); Cross-cutting Patterns (Local endpoint trust boundary).
  - **Trust boundary:**
    - v1 intends to trust every process of the same OS user and no other. How that is enforced per OS (pipe DACL, socket file mode, directory permissions) is not decided in arch and is explicitly handed to security.
    - There is no per-connection authentication. The `from` parameter is self-reported by the caller (the CLI and MCP take it from their own `VIOLA_NAME`), so link records and driver identity are not authenticated.
    - The endpoint name is predictable: FNV-1a over `ViolaName` + home path, which is not secret (Conventions: Endpoint name).
    - Consequences:
      - On Unix the socket sits in the per-user 0700 directory, not in world-writable `/tmp`; a directory another user owns, a loosened one or a symlink is refused by the socket-directory check, with no bind on `run` and no frame on a client.
      - On Windows, the named-pipe namespace is shared across the machine.
      - Clients (`hook`, `send`, `mcp`) connect to the `endpoint` recorded in the snapshot and act on whatever server answers there. A process holding that name while the real wrapper is gone could receive `hook.dialog` payloads and send back dialog decisions.
      - As built, on Linux and Windows every frame-writing client (CLI `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`; `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths; `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools) compares the connected peer's pid and that process's start time with the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` before its first frame, and sends no frame on a mismatch or a check it cannot make. Each first runs the instance's strict-modes check (`check_instance`: the CLI verbs through `client::refuse_untrusted`, `viola hook` before its obs init, the `viola mcp` tools before `live_endpoint`), a refusal sending no frame, and then reads the snapshot through `read_snapshot_or_replay`, a replayed or absent snapshot giving no endpoint and so no frame; ahead of that comparison, on Linux and macOS, each runs the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint before connecting (a refusal `socket-dir-refused`, no frame) and the peer euid decision past the connect (a refusal `server-verify-failed`, no frame); macOS, where the peer reports no pid, compares no pid or start time, the named carve-out, owned by no route entry.
      - `run`'s exclusive bind means a squatted name blocks startup (exit 1).
    - Input validation is limited to JSON-RPC parsing, the `v` check (`-32602`) and the `ViolaName` nutype.
    - That limit is the wrapper's read of a frame. A client's read of the answer is screened on its own: `reply_of` and `of_reply` take a `refusal` or a string `detail` only as a code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`) and a fault only through `viola_channel::sanitised_fault`, so nothing of the peer's but closed values reaches a CLI `--json` document or an MCP result; a code word outside the closed list stays visible by design.
    - An `instance-unreachable` on CLI `--json` or an MCP result names its cause in `detail`, one of six closed words from `viola_core::UnreachableCause` (no serde path, every word written by the two clients, no path, pid or upstream text): `strict-modes-failed`; `instance-dead` (no endpoint with the instance directory standing, or a failed connect); `unwrapped-name` (no endpoint with anything else at that path: absent, a regular file or a symlink); `endpoint-lost` (the wrapper lost with the call open); `server-verify-failed` (Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone); `socket-dir-refused` (the socket directory of the recorded endpoint refused). The no-endpoint reading is `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`, a `symlink_metadata` that opens nothing and writes no line, with the strict-modes check first at every caller (its status at § Authentication & Authorization, the no-endpoint reading). MCP writes no line for any cause, `isError` the record.
    - It is open (arch defers it to security) whether a driver-originated `release` (params carrying `from`) should be refused. Established Decisions (MCP) records that an agent's Bash tool can call CLI `viola release` through `VIOLA_BIN`.

- **Vector:** CLI input, the `send` text written into the PTY.
  - **Entry point:** A bridge send is one `ESC[200~…ESC[201~` + CR write of the typed text: the text from stdin, `--file` or MCP `send.text`, with every CR LF pair and every other CR inside it as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters (Established Decisions: Delivery Confirmation; Human Takeover / Wheel). A text whose typed text is empty is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` and nothing is written.
  - **Trust boundary:** Arch does not say whether sent text is checked for an embedded bracketed-paste terminator (`ESC[201~`) or other control sequences. Text containing one would end the paste early, and the rest would reach the `claude` TUI as typed keystrokes. The only post-hoc check is delivery confirmation, which compares `prompt-submitted` text with the typed text, that is the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters, by exact equality with no tolerance on the submitted side (Established Decisions: Delivery Confirmation).

- **Vector:** The human's terminal, `viola run`'s own stdin.
  - **Entry point:** Every byte the terminal writes to `viola run`'s stdin: the human's keys, and the terminal's own focus reports, mouse reports and replies to the child's queries. A byte that is typing takes the wheel from the driver (`wheel{holder:"human",cause:"human-input"}`), and the next automation `send` is refused `human-typing` (Established Decisions: Human Takeover / Wheel).
  - **Trust boundary:** The stdin classifier's closed non-editing list (the founder's ruling F-W2): only a sequence on it never counts as typing, and every other byte does. The list was widened once, a boundary widening ratified by the founder himself on 2026-10-08 after the exact grammars and a narrower option of two were shown (relayed verbatim by the overseer; chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive): seven terminal reply shapes after `CSI`, each by exact grammar, the fields compared as bytes, no intermediate byte and the field count exact (`0 n`, `? 997;1 n` and `? 997;2 n`, `4;n;n t`, `6;n;n t`, `8;n;n t`, `48;n;n;n;n t`, `> 4;n m`), as measured on foot 1.28.0 on the Linux dev host, where those replies had taken the wheel from the driver at a live session's start. The nearest human keys (`n`, `t`, `m`, their Alt forms, their kitty key events) and a sequence one field or one prefix away stay typing, each pinned by a unit case, and a reply no terminal has been measured to write is never added on a guess. The classifier reads bytes, not time: a human who types a listed reply's bytes one key at a time is read as that reply. A key that reaches this stdin is the human's by construction, whoever typed it: at the same chunk an agent typed five keys into session terminals with `wtype`, each on a compositor the chunk started itself (nested as one client window of the locked desktop's compositor, one start for all live work) and each after a guard read that its one window was the active one. That crossing of the human's own input is the founder's ruling for that chunk's takeover proof (his answers of 2026-10-08, the method first, then the compositor's form and its price after they were shown, relayed verbatim by the overseer): the desktop's lock was never touched and read locked after the start, before each live step and twice after the end, the one call naming the desktop instance was a `locked` read, and no product code took part.

- **Vector:** Hook stdin payloads from Claude Code, exec-form `viola hook <event>`.
  - **Entry point:** JSON on stdin for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse (`AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`), PermissionRequest, Stop, SessionEnd, Notification, PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure, plus `hook statusline` with statusline JSON (Established Decisions: Hook Transport; Occupied Resources).
  - **Trust boundary:**
    - Parsing is tolerant in `viola-agent-claude`: no `deny_unknown_fields`, serde_path_to_error for drift reports (Established Decisions: Validation).
    - Upstream text is treated as content, never as commands (R1).
    - Any failure fails open to the human: exit 0 with no body.
    - `hook statusline` runs `statusline_command` from `snapshot.json` through a shell. That snapshot is found through `VIOLA_DIR`, so its integrity is set by filesystem permissions on the viola home.
    - Every hook path (event, dialog and `hook statusline`) runs the instance's strict-modes check on the canonicalised `VIOLA_DIR` instance before anything under the home is read or opened, the `--capture` arms ahead of it; a refused or absent instance exits 0 with no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line and no frame. `hook statusline` reads the snapshot through `read_snapshot_or_replay`, and a replayed snapshot carries no `statusline_command`, so nothing runs.

- **Vector:** MCP over stdio. The driver is an LLM agent.
  - **Entry point:** Tools `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer` and `list`, called by the driver session's model (Established Decisions: MCP).
  - **Trust boundary:**
    - Tool input schemas (schemars) and the `ViolaName` newtype check the input.
    - Before its frame, each of `send`, `wait`, `last` and `answer` runs the instance's strict-modes check (`check_instance` on the home and the instance directory) ahead of the liveness pre-check and the server check; a refusal is `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, no frame and no line. Past the liveness pre-check `frame` runs the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint, a refusal `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `socket-dir-refused`, and past the connect the peer euid decision beside the server check, a refusal with `detail` `server-verify-failed`, each with no frame and no line.
    - The driver model reads the driven session's output (`wait`/`last`), which arch classes as untrusted upstream text. The same model can then call `answer` on that session's PermissionRequest.
    - viola does not interpret that text (R1: mechanism, not policy). The decision to allow a permission rests with the driver model, outside viola.
    - Leaving `release`, `pause`, `link` and `unlink` off the MCP tool list is described as an affordance, not an enforcement.

- **Vector:** MCP over stdio, the driver's stdin lines.
  - **Trust boundary:** Each stdin line reaches rmcp only through viola's `CappedLines` reader at `MAX_FRAME`, its `\n` counted: an over-long line from the driver is refused whole and ends the MCP session after the earlier lines are answered, never truncated, skipped or dispatched in part, with one `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin", detail:"oversize", count:1}` WARN holding no byte of it.

- **Vector:** CLI arguments, flags and environment.
  - **Entry point:**
    - All subcommands.
    - `--home <dir>` and `VIOLA_DIR` choose which state tree, snapshot, `endpoint`, `statusline_command` and ledger stamps are used (Cross-cutting Patterns: Config management).
    - `answer` takes its `response` JSON from stdin or `--file`.
    - `viola run <name> -- <program> <args>` spawns the program as given.
  - **Trust boundary:** Same-user invocation, clap parsing, the `ViolaName` nutype, and tolerant `config.json` parsing.
    - Before its first read or open under the home, `run`, `revive`'s start and `verify` hold the home tree to the strict-modes check (`check_home_tree`; a refusal exit 1, no log opened), and the frame verbs `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` hold the instance to it (`check_instance`; a refusal exit 21), so a state tree chosen by `--home` or `VIOLA_DIR` that another user can write, or whose home, instance directory or `diagnostics/` another user can read, is refused.
    - `viola list`'s board scan holds the home to the read rule on every OS (`check_read`) and `instances/` to `check_path`, so a home another user may read is refused whole, with or without an instance; the scan keeps its check order and its no-open, and `read_budget_stamped`, `mcp`'s start and `plugin install` keep the write rule on the home.
    - `src/main.rs`'s `json_asked` reads `--json` from argv ahead of clap, as `role_of` reads its role, taking the flag only among the arguments before a `--`. It chooses only the form of the catch site's output where `prints_internal_error` is true: `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout with stderr empty, in place of the human line `error: internal error`. `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` print nothing at the catch site.

- **Vector:** Filesystem state under `~/.viola/`.
  - **Entry point:**
    - Readers across processes: `snapshot.json`, `events.ndjson`, `budget.json`, `config.json`, `ledger/stamps.json`, `heartbeat`.
    - Code-bearing artefacts: `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` and `plugin/<version>-<hash>/hooks/hooks.json` / `.mcp.json`. Claude Code runs these on every hook event and for MCP. And `marketplace/viola/.mcp.json` (`viola plugin install`, never read back by viola), which Claude Code runs for MCP in a session that installed the plugin.
    - Sources: Occupied Resources (Filesystem); Established Decisions (Deployment / Distribution).
  - **Trust boundary:**
    - OS permissions on the user's home directory.
    - Readers tolerate torn lines (they skip and count them, and the next append heals a torn last line). The replay of the log for a snapshot that fails to parse, or carries a newer `v`, is taken by these product readers: `viola revive`'s preflight, `viola list` (`viola_state::board::read`), `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (the CLI frame verbs and the `viola mcp` tools), `viola hook`'s `connect`, `hook statusline`'s `serve` and `run`'s collision check, each after the strict-modes check on the instance's files; a replayed snapshot carries no `endpoint`, `pid`, `started_at` or `statusline_command`, so it yields no frame and runs no command (Standard Contracts: Snapshot envelope).
    - The pinned binary and plugin folders are never deleted in v1.
    - Beyond the content hash in the folder name, `run` and `revive`'s start hold the home tree to the strict-modes check (Unix owner and mode, Windows owner and DACL) before the wrapper log opens (`check_home_tree`: the home, the instance's files, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, `bin/<version>-<hash>/`, the pinned `viola(.exe)`, `plugin/<version>-<hash>/`, its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`), and on Windows `pin_companions` checks `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` and each companion before the held open; `marketplace/` is off the integrity set.

- **Vector:** Filesystem state under `~/.viola/`, the pinned binary's first placement by concurrent first starts.
  - **Trust boundary:** The pinned binary is placed once and never replaced. An exec of a copy that another start still holds open for write fails with `ETXTBSY` (raw 26 on Linux), so the placement closes its write handle before the name appears (`viola_state::fs::place_private_new`, § Data Protection): 0 of 24 two-instance boots failed, as measured at viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds/report.md.

- **Vector:** Child process spawning and PATH resolution.
  - **Entry point:**
    - `list` and `mcp` spawn `claude agents --json`, resolving `claude` from their own PATH with npm-shim → `claude.exe` resolution. As landed (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) CLI `list` spawns one per run after `board::read`, `viola revive`'s preflight one before its recorded-directory reading (skipped under `--fork`; a logged id listed live elsewhere is the closed refusal `session-live`, no child; a failed read passes — the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board (`inputs#I1`, relayed verbatim by the operator)), and `viola verify`'s Run B one (below); each spawn pair `agents-probe` is logged only under an open log and holds no row text, id, `cwd` or path. The `mcp` process spawns one per `list` tool call (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers; the widening the founder's own answer ratified, `inputs#I2` Q1 of that chunk, relayed by the overseer), its `agents-probe` pair logged in `diagnostics/mcp.ndjson` under the same no-row-text, no-id, no-`cwd`, no-path rule.
    - `run` resolves the child executable and runs it once with `--version`.
    - `revive` launches `claude`, looked up by name on the reviving process's own PATH by `run`'s resolver, as a direct spawn in the snapshot's recorded `cwd`. Its child arguments are `--plugin-dir <dir>` (the wrapper's, first), `--settings <instance dir>/settings.json` when the start wrote a settings override, `--resume <id>`, `--fork-session` when `--fork` is given, then the words after `--`. Program resolution and the version gate never read the recorded directory. The logged id on the child's command line is a crossing the founder ratified on 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the overseer (§ Input Validation, the session-id row). `resume_args` has a second caller, `viola verify`'s Run E (the entry point below), whose id comes from Run B's first SessionStart capture rather than a log (the same row).
    - `run` puts the pinned copy's folder first on the child's PATH.
    - `viola verify`, after its print probe, spawns five interactive `claude` children under a PTY, each a direct spawn (never through a shell) under the R8 strip at a fixed 80×24, its output capped at `MAX_FRAME` into a `Screen` fed under `catch_unwind`. Run A runs untrusted in a fresh 0700 `viola-verify-*` dir under the OS temp dir, with empty input, and is ended by a kill. Run B runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`; on a wrapped OS (Unix), and only when the pinned path and the captures dir are shell-plain, it also gets exactly one `--settings <probe dir>/typed/statusline.json` after its `--plugin-dir` pair (a 0600 file under its own probe dir, written by `replace_private`), whose `statusLine` command is `<pinned viola> hook statusline --capture <probe dir>/typed/statusline --shell "$0"` (Hook stdin row); Windows passes none, Runs A, C and D keep their arguments, and no run or start is added (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows («Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`)). Once its first turn has settled, before its framing pastes, Run B also makes ONE bounded `claude agents --json` read (Run B's program, the probe dir as cwd, the R8 strip, `VERSION_DEADLINE`, none once a stop is read; the capture held in memory, never written to the captures dir; `--record` keeps only Run B's own row in `Agents.recorded-1.json`, through the scrub; no live start added — the founder's own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board (`inputs#I1`, relayed verbatim by the operator)). Run B gets six bracketed pastes, all compiled literals: `PROBE_PROMPT`, then `PROBE_LONG_PASTE` (1 500 bytes, one line), `PROBE_TAG_PASTE` (200 bytes), `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (113 bytes, ASCII, one inner LF, no CR), `PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND` (`/compact`, the local-command list's `LOCAL_COMMANDS[2].0`, which compacts Run B's session in place and keeps its `session_id`) and `PROBE_LOCAL_COMMAND` (`/clear`, which opens a second CLI session inside Run B's process). The `/compact` paste is the founder's own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row («Шестая вставка в Run B», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I3`); it adds no run, start or spawn pair (verify still makes six starts and an uninterrupted verify eight spawn pairs). Each of the five added pastes goes only into rows that hold an input-box literal and no modal literal, and none after the stop; after the long, the tag-like and the newline turns Run B waits for those rows (a quiet screen holding a compiled literal, a poisoned screen, or `PROBE_DEADLINE`, 120 s, from that turn's Stop); `/compact` goes only into the settled input box the newline turn left, its answer is waited for up to `PROBE_DEADLINE` (reading the stop), then Run B waits for those rows before `/clear`; so a modal, a poisoned screen, a failed wait and the deadline each end the added pastes with no key. It is ended by Ctrl-C, Ctrl-C again after 500 ms, then a kill; a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM is ended by a kill with no key and pastes nothing more, and no later run starts. Run C runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/` with `--model haiku --settings <DIALOG_SETTINGS>` (a compiled `ask` rule for `Bash(touch viola-probe-permission)`) and pastes the three compiled dialog prompts; its one `allow` runs that `touch` inside its own dir. Run D runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/` with `--model haiku --permission-mode plan` and `plansDirectory` set to a 0700 `plans/` inside its own dir, and pastes the compiled `PLAN_PROMPT`. Run E runs last, trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/` (a 0700 dir its guard removes when verify passes, fails or is stopped), with the run args, then `--plugin-dir` and the capture plugin under `<probe dir>/resume/`, then `--resume <id>` from `resume_args(id, false)`, the id being the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture accepted by `is_session_id` (`ledger::resume_target`; with none it spawns nothing), and no `--settings`; its input is empty, so no key is ever typed, and it waits for one SessionStart capture up to `PROBE_DEADLINE`, settles, and is ended by a kill. An uninterrupted verify writes eight spawn pairs (`version-probe`, `verify-probe`, five `verify-pty-probe`, one `agents-probe`). Run E is the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows («Run E, шестой старт», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`). Runs C and D wait for an input box with no modal before any paste; their dialogs are answered only by the probe hook's `decision_body` output (the capture arm's `--answers`), they settle after their last Stop and are ended by a kill. No run writes a byte into any dialog (CLI-native trust or external imports, or the probe's own), and a start showing a modal is killed with no key. viola writes nothing under `~/.claude`. These are the founder's live rulings of 2026-10-05, each answered after the widening was shown and relayed by the overseer: R-S2 (~00:00Z, the typed-input probe, local to the dev host); "two runs, never accept" (~07:00Z, re-affirmed ~08:50Z); the two dirs (08:25Z); M7 = A at the "Dialog rows and re-probe" plan review (the hook answers, the one `touch`, the +2 transcripts); and the STOP 7 Run D re-run with `plansDirectory`. Run B's first three added pastes are the founder's live answer of 2026-10-06T19:38Z, given after that widening was shown and relayed by the overseer (the card named the three compiled pastes and the one more transcript per verify); the fourth, the newline paste, is his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row («Пятая вставка в Run B», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I2`; 0 starts, 0 spawn pairs and 0 transcripts added); its wait for the input box up to the probe deadline is his live answer of 2026-10-06T20:49Z on the red record round, relayed by the overseer (that card named the wait up to the 120 s probe deadline instead of 5 s with the guard kept; it was not labelled a widening).
    - Sources: Standard Contracts (Session liveness); Established Decisions (CLI Version Compatibility, Deployment / Distribution, Plugin Scope).
  - **Trust boundary:** Whatever the calling process's PATH resolves to. Output parsing is tolerant, and failure becomes `unknown`. verify's interactive children read their screen only against the compiled signature literals, and their row text leaves the process only as signature-only `--record` fixtures.

- **Vector:** Supply chain (build and CI).
  - **Entry point:**
    - Cargo dependencies. Arch notes interprocess has a single main maintainer and rmcp releases nearly weekly with its minor version pinned.
    - Third-party GitHub Actions, SHA-pinned: `actions/checkout` v7.0.1, `Swatinem/rust-cache` v2.9.2, `taiki-e/install-action` v2.87.19, `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.1, `actions/download-artifact` v8.0.1. Every toolchain is installed by `rustup`, with no toolchain action: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.98.1), `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml` (`nightly-2026-09-20`, fuzz jobs only) and the MSRV `1.96` (selected with `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`).
    - Future v1.x public distribution and `self_update`.
    - Sources: Stack; Infrastructure Patterns (Build system, CI/CD approach).
  - **Trust boundary:** `cargo deny check` over `deny.toml` (advisories, licences, sources, C-crate / telemetry-crate / feature bans), the sole-root `deny-sync.toml` tokio ban per sync crate and `viola-channel`'s `cargo tree` form (`scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`; its Tokio client behind the `tokio` feature), `Cargo.lock`, and `publish = false`. `cargo deny`'s root graph covers the root `Cargo.lock` only. The test-only `fuzz/` workspace (its own `fuzz/Cargo.lock`, with the C++-building `libfuzzer-sys`) sits outside it by an operator-ratified exemption, and its lockfile gets its own advisory and source audit (see §Dependency Security). In v1 there is no release, no signing and no deploy stage.

- **CI/CD:**
  - GitHub Actions `ci.yml`, triggered on push and PR, on a native matrix of `windows-2025`, `macos-latest` and `ubuntu-latest`; plus `nightly.yml` (weekly `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`) for `cargo deny check advisories` over the root and fuzz lockfiles, and a time-boxed fuzz run.
  - Jobs: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo check` of the sync crates, the cargo-modules orphans gate per lib/bin target, the per-OS `rmcp features` lint step (`scripts/rmcp-features.sh`: rmcp's features in `viola`'s release graph exactly `server transport-io`, rmcp present), the ubuntu supply-chain job (`cargo deny check`, the `fuzz/Cargo.lock` advisories and sources audit, the sole-root tokio ban then `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`, the ban probes, zizmor), tests against the fake agent with recorded fixtures (per OS under coverage), the per-OS `perf` job (`agent-run run --perf`), MSRV 1.96, fuzz corpus replay, and the per-OS release build (`cargo build --release --locked --bin viola` through `scripts/release-check.sh`, which refuses any test-only binary). No job of `ci.yml` runs mutation since 2026-09-28: mutation testing moved to the epoch-boundary code audit.
  - No deploy stage, no release artefacts and no secrets in v1. The real `claude` CLI runs only locally; `viola verify` runs in CI only against the fake agent, and its real-CLI probe and `--record` only locally.
  - v1.x adds a dist 0.33.0 release workflow with cargo-auditable 0.7.6, signing, winget/Homebrew/Scoop and `self_update` 1.3.0.
  - Sources: Infrastructure Patterns (CI/CD approach); Stack (Release).

## 2026-09-24-quality-gates — fuzz lockfile exemption, fifth pinned action, fuzz and MSRV toolchains, unscanned uploads, declined concurrency
**Section:** Threat Model Summary (Supply chain entry point and trust boundary; Infrastructure CI/CD) · Dependency Security (`deny.toml` additions; Pinning ×2; CI integration: cargo-deny scope, nightly fuzz job, declined `concurrency:`, pinned actions, toolchains) · Bootstrap phases `secret-scanning-ci-gate` · Security Decisions Log (new 2026-09-24 entry)

## 2026-09-27-wrapper-channel — listener hardening as landed: SDDL through windows-sys, chmod 0600 after the bind
**Section:** §Authentication & Authorization (Library: IPC; IPC access control (Windows); IPC access control (Unix)) · §Bootstrap phases (auth-scaffolding-baseline: amendment 2, `viola-channel` listener hardening) · §Security Anti-Patterns → Authentication
**Change:**
- Windows: the protected DACL `D:P(A;;GA;;;<user-SID>)(A;;GA;;;SY)` is converted by windows-sys (`Win32_Security_Authorization`) into `ListenerOptionsExt::security_descriptor`; was `SecurityDescriptor::deserialize` (not used: it needs `widestring`). Windows reads it back canonical as `D:P(A;;FA;;;<sid>)(A;;FA;;;SY)` with the SID possibly an alias (`LA`); the control is the protected flag plus exactly the two allow ACEs.
- Unix secondary control: was `ListenerOptionsExt::mode(0o600)` "where supported, `Unsupported` on macOS ignored"; now chmod 0600 right after the bind on every Unix OS (`mode` fails the bind on macOS, and ignoring it left the socket at the umask mode). The anti-pattern bans `ListenerOptionsExt::mode` and keeps "never the only control".
- Bootstrap: arch amendment 2 is folded (arch IPC endpoints); the SDDL, the per-user dir and the 0600 socket landed with "Wrapper channel", ahead of Epoch 6's admission entry; the `peer_creds` decision and the directory verification stay with their route entries.
**Why:** the report disproved the `mode(0o600)` premise and the GA read-back literal (CI run 36313377307). Weighed against "Boundary widening": not that class — nothing new crosses, and the socket now reaches 0600 on every Unix OS.
**Kept:** the Decisions Log IPC entry and the Threat Model Summary (a verbatim copy) keep their wording as history.

## 2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds — the pinned `viola` placed by `place_private_new`, never replaced
**Section:** §Authentication & Authorization (authentication-authorization.md: `~/.viola/` access control, its Implementation and Stack reference) · §Data Protection (data-protection.md: Code-bearing artefacts, two new groups: the pinned copy's placement, a present pinned-copy name)
**Change:**
- `replace_private`'s mode clause: was "0600, or 0700 for the pinned `viola`"; now 0600 only. The pinned `viola` is never replaced: its absent copy goes through `viola_state::fs::place_private_new`, which sets the temp file's mode (0700) before any byte is written, `sync_all`s it, closes its write handle and places it with `persist_noclobber`, never over a present name.
- Stack reference: adds `into_temp_path` + `persist_noclobber` via `viola_state::fs::place_private_new` (the pinned `viola`) beside tempfile 3.27.0 `persist` via `replace_private`.
- New group, the placement: `pin_bytes` writes an absent `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` by a no-clobber placement, never a replace: a temp file beside it (`NamedTempFile::new_in`), its mode set before any byte, the bytes written, `sync_all`, the write handle closed (`into_temp_path`), then `persist_noclobber`, so the name never appears while a handle holds it open for write. `replace_private_shared` keeps only the plugin files and the ConPTY companions.
- New group, a present name: `place_private_new` never replaces one: `AlreadyExists` is `Placed::Present`, the target untouched and the temp file removed; any other failure is an error that leaves the target as it was, with no retry.
**Why:** `pin_bytes`' absent-copy arm moved from `replace_private_shared` to `place_private_new`, because tempfile's `persist` renames while the write handle is still open and `into_temp_path` closes it first. The chunk measured the mode set before any byte (0700 / 0600 on Unix) and a present name left byte-identical with no temp left. No dependency was added: tempfile 3.27.0 already holds both methods.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-27T02-51-54-wrap/
