title: Iconography

body: Detail: .andromeda/design-system-detail/iconography.md — read whole.
A 0.2.0 frontend design input; 0.1.0 renders no page.
**Style:** Custom text glyphs only. Phraseology words carry the meaning.

Glyphs: on the web `→` (U+2192) marks the outbound marker, `link` / `unlink` lines and a send's target, `←` (U+2190) only the inbound twin; the readback strike is a CSS `linear-gradient`; `·` separates on the web. The CLI is ASCII only: `->` with no inbound form, two spaces between columns, ` - ` inside one field; `viola list` carries no link column in v1, so its six columns stay fixed.
**Library:** None. `img-src 'self'` rules out CDN icon sets. SVG through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and inline SVG markup are banned, and no icon font can load (`font-src 'none'`).
**Size grid:** Glyphs are 1em of the text that carries them (13px), with a 4px (`--space-micro`) gap. The readback box is a 16px square, drawn with borders, not a glyph.

**Rule:** icons clarify, not decorate. If removing an icon loses no meaning, remove it. In viola there are no robot or person icons, no status dots, no checkmarks and no warning triangles. Every one of those states is already a printed word.

title: Surface: web-spa

body: The frontend is deferred to 0.2.0; its technology is not chosen.

title: Surface: cli

body: **Platform:**
- Windows 10/11 (Windows Terminal, conhost), macOS and Linux terminals.
- stdout/stderr of the `viola` binary.
- Callers: the human on a TTY, and LLM driver sessions via `--json` / MCP.
**Toolkit / Framework:**

- clap 4.6.7 (derive) built without its `color` feature, Rust stable: clap's help and usage output is plain in every mode, and no dependency reads a colour or terminal variable, so every styled byte of human output is viola's own SGR module's.
- TTY detection uses std `IsTerminal`.
- Windows VT enabling uses windows-sys 0.61.2 `SetConsoleMode(ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING)`, already in the stack. If it fails, output has no colour.
- Styling is a small hand-written SGR module in the `viola` bin. It adds no dependency.

title: Tokens (platform-specific)

body: Detail: .andromeda/design-system-detail/surface.md — read whole.

CLI colour tokens, at truecolor, 256-colour and 16-colour depth: attention (arrival amber) on the `DIALOG` word only, always followed by the kind word; SGR dim on a whole `stale` row, the cock winning for `DIALOG`; bold for NAME values; a reset after every styled span. Handoff blue is never used, and backgrounds are never set: the terminal background belongs to the user.

**Colour decision order** (the first match wins, and results in no colour, no glyph and no SGR; here, as in the 0.0 expression row and the cli bans, a glyph is a non-ASCII symbol, so the ASCII readback mirror `[RB]` / `[  ]` / `[/ ]` and `->` are words that still print in every human output, piped, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` included, and only `--json` replaces them with its JSON document):
1. `--json`
2. `viola run` (while the child runs, nothing is printed at all)
3. `viola hook` (never writes stderr) and `viola mcp` (stdout carries MCP frames only)
4. `NO_COLOR` set (present, an empty value included)
5. `TERM=dumb`
6. stdout is not a terminal
7. Windows VT enable failed
Otherwise the depth is chosen once per process, first match wins:
- truecolor if `COLORTERM` is `truecolor` or `24bit`;
- 256-colour if `TERM` contains `256color`, or on Windows once VT enabling has succeeded;
- otherwise the 16-colour fallback column.
**Streams:**
- stdout: results and data (tables, send/wait results, `last` text).

- stderr: context lines, refusals (two-space `unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>`, or the fixed `unable: <text>` form for the exit-1 refusals of `run`, `revive` and `verify` and the exit-21 strict-modes refusals of `list`, `link`, `unlink`, `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release`), each refusal's `hint:` line directly after it, and errors.

- For `--json`, the whole result, including refusals and `error` objects, is one JSON document on stdout with the typed exit code, except an oversize `viola answer` and an unusable `viola send`, which exit 2 with their fixed stderr line and no document, and a `pump_child` error under `viola revive --json`, which prints none, the child having held the terminal. At the catch site `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent. No `hint:` line is printed under `--json`: the typed `refusal` / `error` fields and their `detail` are the whole answer, exit 21's cause being its `detail`.
**Width:**
- Where stdout's own terminal width is known (`COLUMNS` is never read, a piped stdout has none), human tables truncate only the NAME of unwrapped rows (`...`); the CLI has no tape.
- Otherwise nothing is truncated. Lines are never wrapped.
- Human output is ASCII only (`->`, `[RB]`, `[/ ]`, `[  ]`).

title: Component Patterns

body: Detail: .andromeda/design-system-detail/surface.md — read whole.
**1. `viola list`: the k9s strip table**

```
BAY  5H 62 %  7D 41 %  read 4m ago  gate open  skipped 0 - 0 - 0
NAME          LIVE   STATUS   WHEEL                    DIALOG             CLI
builder       live   busy     driver                   none               2.1.280 verified
overseer      live   idle     human                    DIALOG permission  2.1.280 verified
scratch       stale  unknown  driver - budget-paused   none               2.1.281 unverified-cli
-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --
c1f9e2a4      live   idle     n/a                      n/a                n/a
```
- NAME is bold, `DIALOG` is amber, and the `scratch` row is dim.
- Rows are ordered by name.

- The BAY line is the ATIS without `resets` times (those are printed by `viola release <name> --budget`) and without a TAPE cell (the CLI has no tape). A window whose `resets_at` has passed still prints `expired` after its figure (`5H 62 % expired`), because old information is shown as old.

- Every field of `claude agents --json` origin (unwrapped names) has C0/C1 controls escaped as `\x1B`-style hex text (security plan). In `list` table rows, `
` and `	` are escaped too (`\x0A`, `\x09`), so every row stays one fixed-width line. The security plan's "keeping `
` and `	`" is a floor, and this is stricter (T5, ratified). `wait` / `last` message text keeps `
` and `	`.
- Empty: `no wrapped sessions  start one: viola run <name> -- claude`.

As built: a wrapped row joined to a `claude agents --json` row reads STATUS `idle` or `busy`, else `unknown`; unwrapped sessions follow the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line; only an unwrapped NAME is cut, and only where the terminal width is known; colour follows the decision order above, laid over the plain board's columns; every control character of a row is escaped as `\xHH`. A failed strict-modes check refuses the whole board (exit 21) in the fixed `unable:` / `hint:` form, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`.
**2. `viola send`: the readback mirror**

```
[  ] open           builder  issued 19:43:58.912Z                 (stderr, TTY only)
[RB] read back      builder  19:43:59.004Z  cursor 48213          (stdout, exit 0)
[/ ] unable         builder  not-delivered  no-prompt-submitted   (stderr, exit 13)
hint: builder did not submit the prompt; check it, then send again
[  ] unconfirmable  builder  local command, no measured post-condition   (stdout, exit 0)
```

A refusal prints `unable` plus `reason  detail`, then one `hint:` line per reason, detail or cause; `run`'s and `revive`'s start refusals take a fixed-message `unable:` line and one hint per cause, `revive`'s read in a fixed order that stops at the first; the exit-21 strict-modes refusal of `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` prints the fixed instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair (Exit-code phraseology below), not the `[/ ]` mirror. No hint names `viola release`, since a driver's `release` is refused. Under `--json` no hint prints; exit 21's document names its cause in `detail`, one of six closed words (Exit-code phraseology below). Faults and `unknown` get no hint.
- A hint never quotes the sent text or any upstream text.
**3. `viola wait` / `viola last`**

- `wait` prints one static `waiting: builder` line on stderr (TTY only), then one result line on stdout:
  - `turn-ended  builder  19:44:10.221Z  cursor 49102`; `session-end` and every other kind without a `dialog_id` take the same `<kind>  <name>  <time>  cursor <n>` form
  - `question  builder  dialog 7  cursor 49310` (`DIALOG` is not coloured here: this is a result, not the board); `dialog unknown` when the event carries no `dialog_id`
  - `dialog-expired  builder  dialog 7  cursor 49400`: an expired hold takes the dialog form, as `question`, `permission` and `plan` do
  - `timed out  builder  30000 ms`
- There is no spinner and no elapsed-time counter.
- `last` prints `last  builder  turn-ended 19:44:10.221Z` on stderr (TTY only), then the message text on stdout with C0/C1 escaped, or `no message` on stderr for `null`.

- Message mode, the escaper `wait` and `last` share and `viola link` uses for a `since` that is no RFC 3339 instant: over decoded characters every control character (C0, DEL, C1) except `\n` and `\t` prints as `\xHH` text, two uppercase hex digits (ESC → `\x1B`, CR → `\x0D`, DEL → `\x7F`, U+009B → `\x9B`); nothing is stripped. `--json` output stays serde-escaped.
**4. Wheel, link and gate verbs** (the phraseology is the design)
- `viola pause builder` → `builder  wheel human  manual-pause  I have control`
- `viola release builder` → `builder  wheel driver  you have control`
`viola release builder --budget` → `builder  budget gate lifted until <time>  wheel human` when a pause stood, else `builder  budget gate open  wheel human`, one unstyled stdout line.
- `viola link overseer builder` → `link    overseer -> builder  since 19:43:58Z` (an existing pair prints `link    overseer -> builder  already linked`)
- `viola unlink overseer builder` → `unlink  overseer -> builder`
- `viola answer builder 7 < response.json` → `answered  builder  dialog 7`, or `unable  builder  not-delivered  unknown-dialog`

- `viola plugin install` → four stdout lines in one write: `viola@viola  written  <dir>` / `run these to add it to Claude Code:` / `  claude plugin marketplace add <dir>` / `  claude plugin install viola@viola`, `<dir>` the marketplace dir, quoted only where the host's shell would split it; plain ASCII, no SGR.
**5. `viola verify` / `viola run`**

`verify` is a step counter, the project's one progress pattern: one static stdout line per relied ledger row (`pass` / `fail`, uncoloured), then a summary line `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail`, n + m the relied count; a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM before its rows are checked, or refused by the strict-modes check of its home tree before its log, prints no step line and no summary, only its fixed `unable:` / `hint:` pair, and exits 1; a `stamps.json` update refused by its strict-modes check prints the home-state pair.

- **`run`:** prints nothing once the child starts. A start refusal (exit 1) prints its cause's fixed-message line, for example `unable: builder is already live`, then that cause's hint (`hint: viola list`). The per-cause lines are listed under the send hints above. None of them shows a path or a pid.

`revive` prints nothing once the child starts, as `run`; `--list` prints one plain stdout line per logged session; a refusal (exit 1) prints its cause's fixed-message line and hint, and under `--json` every refusal of the start it shares with `run` prints one stdout document and no hint, stderr empty, its code one of `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `batch-script-child` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`; a `pump_child` error prints none, the child having held the terminal.
**Exit-code phraseology** (typed codes from architecture.md):

Each typed exit code has its human stderr form and, where it has one, its `--json` document: 0 the result on stdout, 1 `error: internal error` or a fixed-message `unable:` refusal with its hint (a `--json` document for every refusal of `viola revive`'s start, and in place of the `error: internal error` line the catch site's `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty), 2 clap usage or the fixed `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE` / `UNUSABLE_TEXT` stderr line of an oversize `viola answer` / an unusable `viola send` (no document under `--json`), 10 to 14 an `unable` refusal with its reason (a refusal object under `--json`), 20 `error: wrapper fault`, 21 `unable  instance-unreachable` then the cause's hint, or for a refused strict-modes check its fixed home-state or instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair instead (pattern 1 and the paragraphs below), its `--json` document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, one per cause, the cause one of `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, with stderr empty.

`viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check (exit 21) prints the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair as `viola list`'s does, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty.

`viola link` / `viola unlink`'s refused strict-modes check of the driven instance, and that of `viola send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` on their instance, made before any frame (exit 21), prints the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair naming that instance, as `viola list`'s does, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty; no frame and no line are written.

title: Navigation Pattern

body: Detail: .andromeda/design-system-detail/surface.md — read whole.
- Flat verbs, one lower-case word each: `run · revive · send · wait · last · list · answer · verify · pause · release · link · unlink · plugin install`.
- `viola list` is the board and the other verbs act on one strip. There is no interactive prompt, no TUI mode and no pager.

- `viola --help` lists the served verbs as `board: list` / `traffic: send, wait, last, answer` / `wheel: pause, release` / `handoff: link, unlink` / `setup: run, revive, verify, plugin install`, then `Options:`.

title: Platform-Specific Notes

body: - **Git Bash on Windows** rewrites leading-slash arguments. Prompt text therefore comes only from stdin or `--file`. The warning for a rewritten-path argument is one plain stderr line, `warning: argument looks like a Git Bash rewritten path`.
- **conhost without VT** falls back to no colour. The words already carry every state, so nothing is lost.

- **`hook`** writes nothing to stderr and always exits 0. **`mcp`** writes only MCP frames on stdout. Neither has a human design surface. `mcp` is a hidden verb (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): run by the plugin, never by a person, it appears in no `viola --help` row.
- **Stack traces** never print. Errors are fixed messages, and full detail goes only to `instances/<name>/diagnostics/`.

title: Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)
Universal Bans

body: - **NEVER use color purely for decoration. Every color communicates meaning.** Amber means `dialog_pending` and nothing else. Blue means handoff and nothing else. Any third hue has no domain meaning.
- **NEVER converge on common "safe" choices across generations.** The readback box and the cocked strip exist because agent dashboards converge on dots, toasts and graphs.

title: Rejected Defaults (from exploration)

body: - **Traffic-light status dots** (green `live`, yellow `busy`, red `stale`). Rejected because a strip prints its status word in a fixed column. `stale` is a coasting track (lamp-off), not red, and the bay's only colour state is the cocked strip's amber beside its `DIALOG` word.

- **Optimistic "Sending…" spinner, then a green "Sent ✓" or a toast.** Rejected because a clearance does not count until it is read back. The readback box stays `open` until the matching `prompt-submitted` (for `/clear`, its new-session post-condition; for `/compact` on a verified CLI, its same-session compact post-condition), then fills instantly or is struck with `unable` plus the typed reason. There is no green, no toast and no presumption.

- **Auto-sorting "needs input" or recent sessions to the top.** Rejected because a controller cocks a strip in place. Re-ranking breaks the founder's "where builder lives" memory, and the cock (12px offset plus amber band) already says "needs you".

- **Budget as circular rings or green/yellow/red bars.** Rejected because fuel state is figures in ruled fields (`5H 62 %  7D 41 %`), always with the ATIS age (`read 4m ago`). `budget-paused` is a phraseology word, not a colour.

- **Robot and person icons or emoji for the wheel, and a clickable-looking toggle.** Rejected because the WHEEL field prints `human` / `driver`. Taking control is spoken (`viola pause`, "I have control"), never implied by a switch.
- **Skeleton shimmer and a terminal-green or neon-glow "hacker" theme.** Rejected because nothing glows in a tower cab unless the lamp is on it. Missing values print `unknown` in their box at once.

title: Per-Surface Bans

body: **cli**
- **NEVER use green `✓` / red `✗` prefixes or emoji.** The readback mirror `[RB]` / `[  ]` / `[/ ]` and the words `read back` / `unable` are the prefixes.
- **NEVER colour anything except `DIALOG` (amber) and `stale` rows (dim), and never either without its word.** The quiz confirms colour as a second cue only.

- **NEVER emit colour, glyphs or cursor control under `--json`, non-TTY, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb` or `viola run`.** LLM drivers parse this output, and `viola run`'s terminal belongs to the child's screen; a passed `viola revive` is the same passthrough.

- **NEVER use a spinner, progress bar or live-redrawing dashboard.** `wait` prints one static `waiting:` line and `verify` prints step-counter lines, because a spinner is progress presumed before it is confirmed.
- **NEVER mix data and messages.** Results go to stdout. `waiting:`, refusals and their `hint:` lines, and errors go to stderr.

- **NEVER print upstream text, paths, pids or anyhow chains with serde sources in errors or hints.** This is the security plan's NEVER-log floor, and human output of `last` / `list` escapes C0/C1 controls.

- **NEVER print "done" or "success" without context.** Say what was read back, by whom, and at which cursor (`[RB] read back      builder  19:43:59.004Z  cursor 48213`, padded as in the `viola send` sample).
- **NEVER hardcode widths or wrap at arbitrary points.** Truncate only where the terminal width is known, and never wrap.
- **NEVER print stack traces.** Full detail goes to `diagnostics/` only.

title: Self-Validation Protocol

body: Before presenting ANY UI output, downstream implementation phases (per project's specialist plans) must run these checks:

title: 1. Swap Test

body:
Replace your typeface with Inter, your colors with Tailwind defaults, your
layout with a standard sidebar+cards. If the design doesn't feel
meaningfully different → you defaulted. Redo with intent.

title: 2. Squint Test

body:
Blur your eyes at the interface. Can you still perceive hierarchy? Does
anything jump out harshly? Good craft whispers — nothing should scream.
In viola, `open` and `unconfirmable` readback boxes look identical under the squint (`unconfirmable` reuses the open drawing and is never filled); only the word cell tells them apart. That is intended, not a failed squint.

title: 3. Signature Test

body: Point to the readback box in its one 0.1.0 place: the `[RB]` / `[  ]` / `[/ ]` column of CLI `viola send`. If that column lacks the box or draws it differently, the signature does not exist. Inject it. A 0.2.0 frontend's places for the box, and its test, are that version's to name (its technology is not chosen).

title: 4. Token Test

body: Detail: .andromeda/design-system-detail/self-validation-protocol.md — read whole.
A 0.2.0 frontend design input; 0.1.0 renders no page.

Every colour traces to one of the eight `--c-*` values, read only where a role alias is assigned (components use the role aliases, never `--c-*`); every length traces to a token or a `ch` track, every duration to `--cock-dur` or `--fade-dur`; the only literal lengths are the two width breakpoints, because `@media` conditions cannot read custom properties. A ninth hex value or any other untokened px value signals no system.

title: 5. Sameness Test (from Interface Design)

body:
If another AI given a similar prompt would produce substantially the same
output — you have failed. The interface must emerge from THIS product's
domain exploration, not from statistical patterns in training data.

- **Transfer arrows.** On the web, `→` (U+2192) marks the outbound marker (blue, with the name), `link` / `unlink` tape lines, and the target of a `send` tape line (`send  → builder`). In tape lines the arrow is buff and only link names are blue. `←` (U+2190) marks only the inbound twin (`← overseer`, arrow and name in blue). The CLI uses ASCII `->` and has no inbound form. `viola list` carries no link column in v1, so the six columns shared with the web strip stay fixed. Links print only as `link` / `unlink` verb output (`overseer -> builder`).
- **Readback strike.** A CSS `linear-gradient` inside the box.

- **Separator.** Middle dot `·` on the web. The CLI is ASCII only:
  - Two spaces separate columns, and a refusal's reason from its detail (they are separate fields, as in the exit-code table).
  - ` - ` (space, hyphen, space) replaces `·` inside one field or label: `driver - budget-paused`, `skipped 0 - 0 - 0`, `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --`.

Components use the role aliases (`--surface-*`, `--ink*`, `--rule-*`, `--attention`, `--handoff`, `--focus-ring`, `--rb-*`) and never `--c-*`. Every length traces to a token (`--space-*`, `--fs-*`, `--track-*` (em), `--lh-display`, `--lh-label`, `--strip-h`, `--line-h`, `--band-w`, `--rb-size`, `--rule`, `--rule-strong`, `--radius`, `--cock-offset`, `--focus-w`, `--focus-offset`) or to a `ch` track in `--strip-cols` / `--strip-cols-wrapped` / `--tape-cols`, with the wrapped strip's rows in `--strip-rows-wrapped`. Every duration is `--cock-dur` or `--fade-dur`. The only literal lengths allowed are the two Navigation → Width breakpoints (`760px`, `1024px`), because `@media` conditions cannot read custom properties. A ninth hex value or any other untokened px value signals no system.

- Exit 0 under `--json`: `viola link`'s document is `{"v":1,"ok":{"since":<ts>,"already_linked":<bool>}}`, `<ts>` the time the wrapper recorded the link, and `viola unlink`'s is `{"v":1,"ok":{}}`.

- Exit 20 is also reached by `viola link` / `viola unlink` on a pair the wrapper refuses (`-32602`; a `driver` equal to `driven`, which the CLI never refuses itself): `error: wrapper fault  <code>`, or under `--json` the `wrapper-fault` document.

- Exit 20's `--json` `detail` is closed for the five known codes (`viola_channel::sanitised_fault`): `message` is each code's fixed text; `-32602` with an integer `data.supported` and a version-text `data.wrapper` reads the unsupported-version body with those two values, `data.reason` exactly `release-from-driver` reads that body, and any other `-32602` reads `invalid params` with null `data`; every other known code has null `data`.

- A code outside the five prints the same human line, `error: wrapper fault  <code>`, and under `--json` the document `{"v":1,"error":"wrapper-fault","detail":{"code":<code>,"message":"wrapper fault","data":null}}`; MCP carries the same fixed `message`.
- Each CLI `--json` failure `tests/cli_error_bodies.rs` drives prints one document, exits its literal code, leaves stderr empty, and holds no ESC, no path and no upstream text.
- Under `--json` the `cli` catch site prints row 1's `internal-error` document on stdout in place of `error: internal error`, stderr then empty; without `--json` it prints that line, byte for byte.
- The catch site counts `--json` only among the arguments before a `--`, read from argv.
- `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent at the catch site, under `--json` too.

- Exit 21's server-verification cause is built for `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink`: a process on the endpoint that is not the recorded wrapper (its pid or start time differs, or the check cannot be made; on Linux and macOS also a peer whose euid is not this user's or cannot be read, on macOS the euid alone) gets no frame, and the verb prints `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` with the server-verification hint last on stderr, or under `--json` the document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` with stderr empty.
- With no live endpoint a frame verb reads its instance directory after the strict-modes check: a directory is `instance-dead`; absent, a regular file or a symlink is `unwrapped-name`.
- A failed connect is `instance-dead`; a wrapper lost with the call open is `endpoint-lost`.
- A frame verb against a stale instance reads `instance-dead`: stale heartbeat is exit 1's cause alone.

- `viola --help` groups verbs as `board: list` / `traffic: send, wait, last, answer` / `wheel: pause, release` / `handoff: link, unlink` / `setup: run, revive, verify, plugin install` (`revive` beside `run`: the operator's answer at the chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive wrap). As built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline) it lists the served verbs only: `board: list` / `traffic: send, wait, last, answer` / `wheel: pause, release` / `handoff: link, unlink` / `setup: run, revive, verify, plugin install`, then `Options:`.

| Role | Font | Weight | Size | Tracking | Usage |
|------|------|--------|------|----------|-------|
| Display | Bahnschrift stack, semi-condensed | 600 | 16px / 24px line, uppercase | 0.08em | `VIOLA` as the board's display word (there is no hero; a 0.2.0 frontend's page markup is that version's). The `BAY` after it is Label and `127.0.0.1:47319` is Data, as in the ATIS anatomy |

| Heading | Bahnschrift stack, semi-condensed | 600 | 11px / 16px, uppercase | 0.12em | Rack separator labels: `WRAPPED`, `UNWRAPPED · READ-ONLY`, `TAPE`, each rendered as an `<h2>` (a11y-plan D-A11Y-02); the two rack labels sit in their rack table's `<caption>` |

| Callsign | Bahnschrift stack, normal width | 600 | 15px / 32px (strip height) | 0.02em | The NAME cell. Never text-transformed: a `ViolaName` is lower-case `[a-z0-9-]` and must read exactly as it is typed as a `target`. |

| Body | Cascadia Mono stack | 400 (600 for `human` in WHEEL and in `prompt · human`, and for the strip's `DIALOG` word) | 13px / 20px | 0 | Field values, tape text, transfer markers, phraseology words |

| Label | Bahnschrift stack, semi-condensed | 400 | 11px / 16px, uppercase | 0.06em | Column captions (NAME · LIVE · STATUS · WHEEL · DIALOG · CLI), and `BAY`, `5H` / `7D` and `TAPE` in the ATIS header (the tape panel's `TAPE` separator is Heading). The strip's `DIALOG <kind>` value is not Label: it is Body (Cascadia 13px) with `DIALOG` at weight 600, so the 20ch DIALOG track measures it in `ch` like every other field. |
| Code | Cascadia Mono stack | 400 | 12px / 20px | 0 | Commands shown in empty states (`viola run <name> -- claude`), the expanded tape body (`white-space: pre-wrap`) |

| Data | Cascadia Mono stack | 400 (600 for `RB`) | 13px / 20px. The one exception is `RB` inside the readback box: `--fs-label` 11px, line-height 1, `--fw-strong` 600, identical in every place the box appears | `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` | Percentages, timestamps `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, `since`, cursors, dialog ids, ages, skipped counts |
- `--font-label: "Bahnschrift", "DIN Alternate", "Avenir Next Condensed", "DejaVu Sans Condensed", sans-serif;`

- `--font-field: "Cascadia Mono", Consolas, "SF Mono", Menlo, "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace;`

| Role token | Windows (live target) | macOS (CI-tested) | Linux (CI-tested) | Last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--font-label` | Bahnschrift (DIN 1451) | "DIN Alternate" (DIN, ships with macOS), then "Avenir Next Condensed" | "DejaVu Sans Condensed" (the condensed system sans) | `sans-serif` |
| `--font-field` | "Cascadia Mono", then Consolas (on every Windows) | "SF Mono", then Menlo | "DejaVu Sans Mono" | `monospace` |

- Semi-condensed labels use `font-stretch: 87.5%`, which Bahnschrift's variable width axis honours. On the fallbacks it is a no-op: DIN Alternate, Avenir Next Condensed and DejaVu Sans Condensed are already narrow cuts.

- Strip and tape columns are sized in `ch` of `--font-field` (`--strip-cols`, `--tape-cols`), so they re-measure to whichever monospace resolves. DejaVu Sans Mono is wider than Cascadia Mono, so the Linux render is the widest case the layout must hold without horizontal scroll.

title: 2026-10-01-t12-19-55-wrap — web-spa toolkit: React + TypeScript, measured details open
body:
## 2026-10-01-t12-19-55-wrap — web-spa toolkit: React + TypeScript, measured details open
**Section:** Iconography → Library; Surface: web-spa → Toolkit / Framework; Surface: web-spa → state attributes; Component Patterns → session strip Semantics; Component Patterns → event tape Expanded body; Platform-Specific Notes → CSP; Platform-Specific Notes → Constructable stylesheets; Anti-Patterns (the output-encoding NEVER)
**Change:**
- Toolkit was Lit 3.3.3, vendored ESM, no JS build step; now React + TypeScript, a built bundle embedded in `viola`. The bundler and its version, the React version, the embedding, the CSP the bundle needs and the npm gates are OPEN, owned by the route's frontend-toolchain entry (Epoch 8's head). Until it lands the page has no JS build step.
- The Lit-era host form (light-DOM custom elements via `createRenderRoot`, role-less `display: contents` hosts, Lit `static styles`) is retired; how each `viola-*` name maps onto React's output is OPEN, and the rendered-DOM requirements stand. Styling stays `/assets/app.css` alone: no Shadow DOM, no component-scoped or runtime-injected styles.
- Session strip: renders a native `<tr>` with `<td>` cells; any element left between `<tbody>` and the `<tr>` is role-less with `display: contents`; no role set by script.
- Text bindings are JSX text children (was Lit `${}`).
- CSP: `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` stands; "lit-html's built-in policy satisfies it" is retired, and what satisfies it under React is OPEN.
- Bans name React sinks: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, `style="…"` with React's `style` prop (were `unsafeHTML`, `unsafeSVG`, `styleMap`).
**Why:** founder ruling of 2026-09-30, relayed by the overseer: 0.2.0 renders the session hierarchy as a node graph, which a build-less Lit page does not fit. Standing rule: relaxing any CSP directive or a ban is a boundary widening the founder rules live at the frontend-toolchain entry.
**Kept:** every CSP directive and every ban (Lit API names swapped for their React sink counterparts, a narrowing); `viola-*` names and selectors as component names.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-01T12-19-55-wrap/

## 2026-10-10-viola-revive — the `revive` refusals and hints, its `--list` rows, the verb in the `setup` help group
**Section:** §Brand Identity (the expression table, the cli 0.0 row) · §Surface: cli → Component Patterns (the stderr rule; pattern 2, hints; pattern 5, a `revive` bullet; Exit-code phraseology, the exit 1 row) · §Surface: cli → Navigation Pattern · §Per-Surface Bans (the no-colour ban)
**Change:**
- Pattern 2: the exit-1 refusals of `viola revive`, one fixed-message line and one hint per cause, read in a fixed order that stops at the first refusal: `<name>'s state files can be written by another user` → `viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only`; `run`'s `already live` pair and its stale sibling, unchanged; `<name> has no logged session to resume` → `start one: viola run <name> -- claude`; `<name> has no logged session with that id` → `viola revive <name> --list`; `<name>'s recorded directory is missing` → `resume it by hand from a directory you choose: viola run <name> -- claude --resume <id>, ids from viola revive <name> --list`. None shows the recorded directory, a pid or a logged id; no hint names `viola release`.
- The stderr rule: the fixed message form `unable: <text>` is used by the exit-1 refusals of `viola run`, `viola revive` and `viola verify` (was "only the exit-1 start refusal"). The exit 1 phraseology row lists revive's four lines.
- Pattern 5, `revive`: prints nothing once the child starts; `--list` prints one static stdout line per logged session, `<time>  <cause>  <session id>`, two spaces between fields, no header, no colour, plain ASCII; no `--json`.
- The detail-code sentence names `no-session` and `cwd-missing`; revive's strict-modes refusal reuses `strict-modes-failed` at exit 1.
- Navigation Pattern: the flat verb list names `revive`; `viola --help` groups it as `setup: run, revive, verify, plugin install`.
- The 0.0 expression row and the no-colour ban name a passed `viola revive` as the same passthrough as `viola run`.
**Why:** the chunk landed the verb. The four pairs stand as the plan worded them on the founder's answer, live, 2026-10-10, relayed by the operator. The help group is the operator's answer at this wrap's Phase 2 halt: the binary's own help lists `revive` right after `run`.
