title: Design Decisions Log
body:
## Design Decisions Log

_Orchestrator records key decisions here. Manual additions welcome._

2026-09-24: Initial design system generated by /andromeda-design
- **Brand personality:** "Strip-bay handoff, read back". An ATC tower strip bay after dark with standard-phraseology voice. Base expression is 0.2 (web-spa 0.3; cli TTY 0.2; machine output and passthrough 0.0). Dark only.
- **Surfaces:** web-spa (`viola ui`: Lit 3.3.3 light-DOM `viola-*` elements, hand-written `@layer` CSS, system-installed Bahnschrift + Cascadia Mono) and cli (clap, hand-written SGR: amber `DIALOG` + dim `stale` only).
- **Signature:** the readback box (`open` / `RB` read back / `unable` strike, plus the printed word `unconfirmable`) in tape send lines, transfer markers and the CLI `[RB]` / `[  ]` / `[/ ]` column. The cocked strip is the supporting attention element.
- **Key rejection:** the optimistic "Sending… → Sent ✓" toast. Nothing is shown as delivered until it is read back.
- **Contrast finding:**
  - Lamp-off #9C9278 (4.4:1), amber (4.3:1) and blue (3.9:1) fail AA as text on holder #2A2E33.
  - Therefore: column captions live in the rack header on anthracite, the cocked DIALOG cell is inset anthracite, transfer markers sit in the rack gap, and a `stale` strip drops its holder fill to anthracite (the lamp has moved off).
- **Customisations of the Color World:**
  - The in-strip field grid uses lamp-off buff rather than strip buff, so buff borders stay reserved for borders that are a state.
  - Instance `budget_paused` prints inside the WHEEL field (`driver · budget-paused`) to keep the six fixed columns shared with the CLI.
  - Absent-by-contract fields print `n/a`, and failed readings print `unknown`.
- **Data dependency (extends cross-lane follow-up CL-1):**
  - `send-issued` must carry `cursor` and `from`.
  - `send-refused` must carry `refusal` + `detail`.
  - A logged outcome is needed for `ok`/`confirmed:false` (`unconfirmable`) so the box can reach that word.
  - Readback pairing uses the next `prompt-submitted` with origin `driver` on that instance (at most one send in flight), or `session-start` cause `clear` for `/clear`.
  - Until CL-1 lands the page shows only `read` boxes, and `unknown` in marker last-send cells.

2026-09-24: Phase 4.5 review round 1 — fonts get explicit per-OS fallback stacks (founder: Bahnschrift and Cascadia Mono are Windows-only, D3 supports macOS + Linux, and CI's headless GUI checks run on ubuntu). `--font-label`: Bahnschrift → "DIN Alternate" → "DejaVu Sans Condensed" → sans-serif; `--font-field`: "Cascadia Mono" → "SF Mono", Menlo → "DejaVu Sans Mono" → monospace. Contrast and render assertions must hold on the Linux fallback, the resolved family is asserted, no web fonts. Colours, expression levels and signature approved as drafted.

2026-09-24: Phase 4.5 review round 2 — restored the two fallbacks the round-1 exact list dropped: Consolas right after "Cascadia Mono" in `--font-field` (on every Windows, so Windows 10 without Windows Terminal stays in a named face), and "Avenir Next Condensed" right after "DIN Alternate" in `--font-label` (macOS). Draft approved; proceed to Phase 5.

2026-09-24: Phase 6 iteration 1. This entry records decisions the body already applied but the log did not carry. No founder-approved colour, expression level, signature drawing or font stack changed.
- **Library shortlist direction:** Precision & Density (primary) with Utility & Function (secondary). The style preset is Minimalism & Swiss Style (#1), with E-Ink / Paper (#56) as the surface reference, inverted to buff on anthracite. Rejected presets: Dark Mode (OLED) (#7), Real-Time Monitoring (#31: pulsing dots, blink, toasts) and HUD / Sci-Fi FUI (#51: glow, telemetry animation). The Swiss preset's 200–250ms hover is dropped.
- **Shortlist deviations:**
  - Palette #81's run-green accent is dropped and its slate warmed to neutral laminate.
  - #96's route blue is lightened from #2563EB (fails AA) to #5B8DB8.
  - Typography pairing #1 (Fira Code + Fira Sans) is translated to Bahnschrift + Cascadia Mono under `font-src 'none'`. The `--font-field` stack follows the founder's Phase 4.5 review rounds 1–2 rather than the shortlist's: "SF Mono" is added for macOS and "Noto Sans Mono" is not carried.
  - Fallback pairing #3 (a mono name cell) is not taken. The Callsign role sets NAME in Bahnschrift at normal width, which answers the "too condensed / too signage" concern.
  - UX guideline 8, Loading Indicators (#78, "spinner or skeleton"), is overridden per the exploration. Waiting is shown as words: `open`, `unknown`, `read 4m ago`, `sessions: no reading yet`, `waiting:`.
- **Signature states:** the exploration's `data-rb="open|read|refused"` is extended to four values with `unconfirmable`, the honest outcome of an `ok` send with `confirmed:false`. It deliberately reuses the open drawing and is never filled. In the Squint Test, `open` and `unconfirmable` therefore look identical, and only the word cell tells them apart.
- **Motion vs the 0.3–0.4 calibration row:** viola overrides the row. Hover is 0ms (link underline only), there is no page transition, and there is one entrance: the 120ms linear `@starting-style` fade on `data-live` tape lines and transfer markers. The cock (12px / 160ms) is the only high-impact moment.
- **Brake scope:** "never on this page" and "view-only" are v1 statements. Web-spa component 7 (`I HAVE CONTROL`, `UNLINK`), Raised-3, the `radius-sm` brake usage and `Problem::cross-origin-forbidden` stay reserved for v1.x and do not contradict the v1 bans.
- **Geometry:** `--strip-cols` changes LIVE from 6ch to 8ch, STATUS from 8ch to 10ch, and the WHEEL and CLI maxima from 24ch to 25ch, so `stale`, `unknown` and the 22ch WHEEL / CLI words fit with `space-xs` padding in DejaVu Sans Mono. Field-cell inline padding is `space-xs` (8px) only.

2026-09-24: Phase 6 iteration 8.
- **UX guideline 5, Content Jumping (#19):** met for order, not for pixel position. When a transfer marker appears or is removed, the content below moves instantly by the 20px marker line plus its `space-xs` gap. When the sticky ATIS header gains a line (`expired`, `TAPE stopped`, a nonzero `skipped`), it moves by one `--line-h`. No strip ever changes order or slot, and nothing animates the shift. Only the cock stays out of flow (`transform`), because it is the one state change the eye must not lose.
- **Unwrapped names:** an over-long unwrapped name ends in an ellipsis on the web, as it does in the CLI. It is not a target, so its tail is not needed to act on.

2026-09-24: Phase 6 iteration 9.
- **Holder colour vs state (deviation from the exploration's Strip holder concept):** the exploration says a holder's colour marks the kind of traffic, never its state, and that a cocked strip is not recoloured. Two state changes touch the holder anyway, both forced by the contrast table. `stale` drops the fill to anthracite, because lamp-off ink fails AA on holder. A cocked strip insets its DIALOG cell, because amber text fails AA on holder. Kind stays readable without the fill: a `stale` wrapped strip keeps its solid rail edge and 4px band slot, and an unwrapped strip has a dashed rail outline and no band slot.
- **`DIALOG` weight:** the cocked strip's amber `DIALOG` word is 600 (Typography, Body row) and the `states` layer sets it. `human` is therefore one of two heavier words after the callsign, not the only one.

2026-09-24: Overseer decisions (founder-delegated), closing two choices Phase 7 left open.
- **Caption-row spacing:** the gap between a rack's caption row and its first strip is the rack's existing row gap, `space-xs`, the same gap strips and transfer markers use. No new token. `space-md` now reads as the gap between the rack separator label and the caption row.
- **Exit-1 start refusal hint:** `unable: <name> is already live` is followed by `hint: viola list` (no paths, no pids), like every other refusal. `error: internal error`, the other exit-1 outcome, keeps no hint.

2026-09-24: Overseer fix pass 2026-09-24 (cross-plan findings, founder-delegated). Each item was checked against the cited upstream line first.
- **T3:** the `human-typing` and `budget-paused` hints no longer name `viola release`. These refusals reach drivers, and the wrapper refuses a `release` that carries `from` (security: driver-originated `release`, `-32602`, `release-from-driver`, exit 20). Tests assert that no driver-facing hint contains `release`. `release` remains a human verb (cli pattern 4).
- **T4:** cli pattern 2 now gives one hint per cause for exit 21 and exit 1.
  - Exit 21 causes: not running, unwrapped name, strict-modes, server verification.
  - Exit 1 causes (`run` start refusals): already live, stale heartbeat, squatted endpoint, pinned SHA-256 mismatch, `.cmd` / `.bat` child, strict-modes home.
  - Every cause has its own fixed-message line. The exit-code table follows.
  - Not changed: `error: internal error` keeps no hint. It is a fault, and tests' exit-cause matrix does not list it among the exit-1 causes.
  - Under `--json` no hint text is printed. A per-cause detail code there is **pending an arch amendment**: arch fixes `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` for exit 21 and gives exit 1 no `--json` document. Design does not change that payload. It points at obs-plan D-20's codes and notes that the stale-heartbeat and unwrapped-name causes have no code yet.
- **T5 (ratified):** `list` table rows also escape `\n` and `\t`, so each row stays a single fixed-width line. The security plan's "keeping `\n` and `\t`" is a floor. `wait` / `last` text keeps them.
- **By:** manual edit, overseer fix pass 2026-09-24.

2026-09-24: overseer fix pass 2, 2026-09-24 (cross-plan findings "a11y P3.5", founder-delegated). Each item was checked against the cited line first. These are design amendments accepted with the a11y plan.
- **Y1 (a11y-plan D-A11Y-02):**
  - Racks are native `<table>` / `<tr>` / `<td>` with `<th scope="col">` captions. They replace `role="row"` on `<viola-session-row>` inside a `role="table"` rack: semantic HTML first, with no ARIA role on a custom-element host.
  - `VIOLA` is the page's `<h1>`, and the rack separator labels are `<h2>`, the rack labels inside each table's `<caption>`.
  - Visual anatomy, grid tracks and tokens are unchanged. Web-spa component 1 Semantics, the column captions and the Typography Display / Heading rows are updated.
- **Y2 (a11y-plan D-A11Y-03):** the tape keeps `role="log"` with an explicit `aria-live="off"`, which removes the implicit polite live region. This enforces the existing rule that the whole tape is never announced. Web-spa component 4 Anatomy is updated.
- **By:** manual edit, overseer fix pass 2, 2026-09-24 (founder-delegated).

2026-09-24: overseer fix pass 3, 2026-09-24 (cross-plan findings "a11y vs upstreams", founder-delegated). Each item was checked against the cited line first.
- **Z2:** the strip and marker hosts are `display: contents` (Y1), which cannot carry transform, transition or grid layout. The cock `transform` and its `transition`, the marker's `data-live` fade and the strip grid anatomy now target the `<tr>` the host renders (`viola-session-row[data-dialog="pending"] > tr`, `viola-transfer[data-live] > tr`). Tokens, durations and the visual result are unchanged. The `stale` custom-property swap stays on the host, because custom properties inherit through `display: contents`. A grid `<tr>` must still expose `row`; the a11y plan's aria snapshot asserts `table` / `row` / `cell` in every state.
- **Z9:** the ATIS is a native `<dl>` after the `<h1>`. The printed labels are the `<dt>`s (`BAY`, `5H`, `7D`, `TAPE`, `skipped`). `read … ago` and `gate open` / `budget-paused` get visually hidden `<dt>`s (`budget read`, `budget gate`). Visible text is unchanged. Web-spa component 5 gains a Semantics bullet.
- **Z10:** the announcer scope matches a11y-plan D-A11Y-06: cocks, refusals and `TAPE stopped`, plus the 401 access strip (announced instead of `TAPE stopped` after a `viola ui` restart) and the 503 / 404 / 405 rack strips that appear after first render. Updated in "Attention outside the tab" and the tape `aria-live` ban.
- **By:** manual edit, overseer fix pass 3, 2026-09-24 (founder-delegated).

title: layout-templates
Layout Templates — viola

body:
_Generated by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8 (one-shot, no iteration loop).
Foundation document for downstream implementation. Per-surface wireframes
and component-level detail for primary sections._

_The security tier has already shaped the design system foundation
(Phase 5 / 5a / 6)._

_Do not edit during implementation runs. Manual edits between Andromeda
runs are fine._

title: Surface: web-spa

body: The frontend is deferred to 0.2.0; its technology is not chosen.

title: Surface: cli

body: **Tooling context:** Rust stable with clap 4.6.7 (derive). TTY detection uses std `IsTerminal`. Windows VT output is enabled with windows-sys 0.61.2 `SetConsoleMode`, and colour is off if that fails. Styling is a small hand-written SGR module in the `viola` bin, with no colour or table crate. Columns are padded to fixed widths by that same module.
**Token names on this surface:**
| Token name | cli rendering |
| `color-accent` | The design system's attention SGR token (truecolor / 256 / 16-colour fallback row). Only on the `DIALOG` word, always followed by the uncoloured kind word |
| `color-text-muted` | The `stale` token: SGR dim across a whole `stale` row, and never without the word `stale` in LIVE |
| Callsign role | The callsign token: SGR bold on NAME values only |
| `color-text-primary` / `color-text-secondary` | The terminal's default foreground. The terminal owns ink |
| `color-role-handoff` | Not used. Link output is plain |
| `color-surface-*` | Never set. The terminal background belongs to the user |
| Label role | Uppercase column captions (`NAME LIVE STATUS WHEEL DIALOG CLI`) and group labels, plain |
| Data role | Tabular figures and timestamps |
| `space-xs` equivalent | The column gutter: two spaces on the terminal grid. Inside one field, ` - ` is the separator |
| `radius-*` | No terminal analogue. Square brackets `[ ]` keep the ruled-rectangle reading |

| Motion tokens | None. Nothing redraws in place |
One token vocabulary (`color-*`, `space-*`, `radius-*`, the typography roles) resolves on the cli to the SGR tokens, the terminal default foreground or "not used". Its platform mechanics are ANSI depth, the two-space gutter, ASCII `->` / ` - `, and brackets for the ruled box.

**Expression level (this surface):** 0.2 on a human TTY: static fixed-column rows, one static context header, and colour only as a second cue. 0.0 for `--json`, non-TTY, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb` and the `viola run` / `viola revive` passthrough: no colour, no non-ASCII glyph and no cursor control.
**Signature placement:** the readback mirror `[RB]` / `[  ]` / `[/ ]` is the first column of `viola send` output, in two components:
1. The issue line `[  ] open …`, on stderr and only on a TTY. It is printed when the request goes to the wrapper.

2. The outcome line: `[RB] read back …` on stdout with exit 0 when the send is confirmed, by the matching `prompt-submitted` or, on a verified CLI version, for `/clear` by its new-session post-condition (a `session-start` with cause `clear` and a new session id) and for `/compact` by its compacted-session post-condition (a `session-start` with cause `compact` and the session's own id, inside its own 40 s PROVISIONAL window, else `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`); `[/ ] unable …` on stderr with exit 13 (or 10/11/12/14) when the wrapper returns a refusal, or with exit 13 when the client itself refuses the text before any frame (`not-delivered` with `control-character` or `empty-text`); `[  ] unconfirmable …` on stdout with exit 0 for a local command with no measured post-condition (`/remote-control`, and `/compact` or `/clear` on an unverified CLI version).

The word half of the box (`unable` plus `reason  detail`) is also the first-word column of every other verb's refusal line (`viola answer`, `viola pause`, `viola release`, and `viola wait` / `viola last` / `viola link` / `viola unlink` for exit 21). So the struck-box vocabulary is shared, while the glyph itself belongs to `send`. Under `--json` the mirror is replaced by the typed `ok` / `refusal` document. The supporting attention element, the amber `DIALOG` word, appears only in `viola list`.

title: Primary screens (commands)

body: - `viola list` is the board: every session as one strip row, with the BAY context header.
- `viola send <target>` is the readback mirror. It types at a turn boundary and reports read back, unable or unconfirmable.
- `viola wait <target>` / `viola last <target>` return one turn-boundary result or the last assistant message, with no spinner.
- `viola pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink` / `answer` are the wheel, handoff and dialog verbs. Their output is spoken phraseology.
- `viola verify` stamps a CLI version with a step counter, the project's only progress pattern.
- `viola run <name> -- claude` is passthrough and prints nothing while the child runs.

- `viola mcp` is no screen (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): the hidden, plugin-run stdio MCP server with no human surface. Its five tools `send · wait · last · answer · list` are a driver's machine view of those verbs: each success and refusal is the CLI verb's `--json` document less `v`, a refusal `isError: true` with the text `refused: <code>`, the bodies codes only (`invalid-params` with a closed field word as `detail`), and no tool, description or result names `release`, `pause`, `link` or `unlink`.

- `viola revive <name>` resumes a dead instance in place (its newest logged session, in the recorded directory) and is passthrough like `viola run`. `viola revive <name> --list` prints the instance's logged sessions, one static line each.

- `viola plugin install` writes an MCP-only local marketplace under `<home>/marketplace/` (no hooks) and prints the two `claude plugin` commands that add it; it spawns no `claude` (Output structure — `viola plugin install`).

- `viola --help` is the grouped verb table, built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline) with the served verbs only: the board, traffic, wheel, handoff and setup rows, `handoff:` holding `link, unlink` and `setup:` holding `plugin install`.

title: Output structure — `viola list` (human TTY)

body:
```
$ viola list
BAY  5H 62 %  7D 41 %  read 4m ago  gate open  skipped 0 - 0 - 0                <- context header (Label BAY/5H/7D, Data figures), one static line
NAME          LIVE   STATUS   WHEEL                    DIALOG             CLI    <- captions, Label, plain
builder       live   idle     driver                   none               2.1.280 verified
overseer      live   busy     human                    DIALOG permission  2.1.280 verified     <- DIALOG in color-accent, `permission` plain
scratch       stale  unknown  driver - budget-paused   none               2.1.281 unverified-cli <- whole row color-text-muted (SGR dim)
-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --                                                      <- rack separator, Heading-equivalent, plain
c1f9e2a4...   live   idle     n/a                      n/a                n/a    <- NAME truncated with `...` only when the width is known
```
- NAME values are bold (Callsign). Rows are ordered by name. Nothing is re-sorted by state.
- A closed budget gate prints `budget-paused` in place of `gate open`. A passed window prints `5H 62 % expired`.
- On a cocked + `stale` row, `DIALOG` stays amber and not dim, and the kind word and the rest of the row stay dim.
- Empty board: `no wrapped sessions  start one: viola run <name> -- claude`.

title: Output structure — `viola list` (piped / `NO_COLOR` / `TERM=dumb`)

body:
```
$ viola list | cat
BAY  5H 62 %  7D 41 %  read 4m ago  gate open  skipped 0 - 0 - 0
NAME          LIVE   STATUS   WHEEL                    DIALOG             CLI
overseer      live   busy     human                    DIALOG permission  2.1.280 verified
...
```
These are the same characters with no SGR. The words carry every state, so nothing is lost. Nothing is truncated when the width is unknown.

**As built** (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; the agents read, chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board; the colour layer and the width cut, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline): `viola list` prints this form as one stdout write: the BAY line, the caption row, then one row per wrapped session in name order, or the BAY line, the caption row and the empty line; then the unwrapped rack when there is one. It is uncoloured under `--json`, a piped stdout, `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included), `TERM=dumb` or a failed Windows VT enable; on a terminal that takes colour it is the styled human-TTY form above: every NAME value bold, the `DIALOG` word of a wrapped row with a pending dialog in the attention token with its kind word plain, a wrapped `stale` row dim from its first byte to its last (NAME dim and bold; on a stale row with a dialog only `DIALOG` amber and not dim), the BAY line, caption, empty line and separator plain, the depth truecolor / 256 / 16 from `COLORTERM` / `TERM`. One `claude agents --json` read follows the board read, its rows joined to the wrapped rows by child pid or agent session id: a joined wrapped row reads STATUS `idle` or `busy`, else `unknown`; every unjoined row prints after the wrapped rows (or after the empty line) under the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line, sorted by name, NAME the row's `sessionId` through `escape_row`, LIVE `live`, its STATUS, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI; with no unwrapped row no separator prints, and a failed, oversize or malformed read prints the board as with no `claude`. NAME is padded to the longer of 4 and the longest name over both racks, counted in characters, LIVE to 5, STATUS to 7, WHEEL to 23 (the widest word `unknown - budget-paused`; implement's decision, confirmed by the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer), DIALOG to 17, CLI last and unpadded; no line ends in a space. With the terminal's width known (`viola_pty::host_size()`, never `COLUMNS`; a piped stdout reads none) NAME's column is the largest of 4, the longest wrapped NAME and the longest unwrapped NAME capped at the width less 65, and an unwrapped NAME longer than the column is cut to the column less 3 characters plus `...` (the wireframe's `c1f9e2a4...`), never inside a `\xHH` escape; a wrapped NAME is never cut; with no known width nothing is truncated. A replayed row with no logged holder reads WHEEL `unknown`; a row with no recorded version reads CLI `unknown`; a pending dialog of unknown kind reads `DIALOG unknown`. The planning forms of design-system cli pattern 1 (a figure rounded down, the whole-minute age and `read unknown`, bare skip counts, `human - budget-paused`, the empty board's three lines) are the founder's wording, confirmed as built in the same answer (the operator's word superseded 2026-10-13).

title: Output structure — `viola list --json`

body:
```
$ viola list --json
{"v":1,"ok":{"items":[…],"budget":{…},"skipped":{"unknown_kinds":0,"unknown_fields":0,"torn_lines":0}}}
```

One JSON document on stdout, with no header line, no colour and no glyph. The item, `budget` and `skipped` shapes are the `list` payload contract (architecture §Standard Contracts). A failed strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance prints instead `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` with exit 21 and stderr empty, opens no log and leaves the home's mode as found (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer, the operator's answer superseded 2026-10-13).

title: Output structure — `viola send`

body:
```
$ viola send builder < step4.txt
[  ] open           builder  issued 19:45:05.300Z                 <- stderr, TTY only (issue: box open)
[RB] read back      builder  19:45:05.912Z  cursor 48213          <- stdout, exit 0 (SIGNATURE: filled)

$ viola send builder < clear.txt
[  ] open           builder  issued 19:44:31.007Z
[/ ] unable         builder  not-delivered  input-not-ready       <- stderr, exit 13 (SIGNATURE: struck)
hint: builder was not ready for input; send again, and if it repeats a human must look at the session   <- stderr, the last line

$ viola send builder < remote.txt
[  ] open           builder  issued 19:46:12.001Z
[  ] unconfirmable  builder  local command, no measured post-condition   <- stdout, exit 0 (never filled)

$ viola send builder --json < step4.txt
{"v":1,"ok":{"submitted_at":"2026-09-23T19:45:05.912Z","cursor":48213}}   <- stdout; no glyph, no issue line
```

The word column is padded so `open`, `read back`, `unable` and `unconfirmable` line up, and the name always starts in the same column. Lines are appended, never redrawn: the issue line stays and the outcome is printed under it. When stdout is piped, the TTY-only issue line is dropped and the outcome line alone carries the mirror.

title: Output structure — `viola wait` / `viola last`

body:
```
$ viola wait builder --after 48213
waiting: builder                                          <- stderr, TTY only, printed once
turn-ended  builder  19:44:10.221Z  cursor 49102          <- stdout
session-end  builder  19:52:03.118Z  cursor 50117         <- stdout (every kind without a dialog_id takes the turn-ended form)
question  builder  dialog 7  cursor 49310                 <- stdout (DIALOG is not coloured: this is a result, not the board)
dialog-expired  builder  dialog 7  cursor 49400           <- stdout (an expired hold takes the dialog form)
timed out  builder  30000 ms                              <- stdout

$ viola last builder
last  builder  turn-ended 19:44:10.221Z                   <- stderr, TTY only
41 passed, 0 failed                                       <- stdout, C0/C1 escaped; `no message` on stderr for null

$ viola wait builder                                      (no live instance: exit 21)
unable  builder  instance-unreachable                     <- stderr
hint: builder is not running; viola list shows the live instances   <- stderr, the last line
```

There is no spinner and no elapsed-time counter. `waiting:` is printed only when stderr is a terminal and `--json` is not set. A dialog line whose event carries no `dialog_id` reads `dialog unknown`. A `wait` woken by `dialog-expired` (the wrapper's record of an expired hold, chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver) prints `dialog-expired  <name>  dialog <id>  cursor <n>`, ASCII, no SGR, written once. Under `--json` each verb prints exactly one document on stdout (`{"v":1,"ok":…}`, or the exit-21 / wrapper-fault document) and nothing on stderr. A failure or a caught panic prints `error: internal error` once, exit 1, no hint, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout with stderr empty (Primary content block 2).

title: Output structure — wheel, handoff and dialog verbs

data.head: ### Output structure — wheel, handoff and dialog verbs

body:
```
$ viola pause builder
builder  wheel human  manual-pause  I have control
$ viola release builder
builder  wheel driver  you have control
$ viola release builder --budget
builder  budget gate lifted until 21:00:00Z  wheel human   <- a pause stood; `YYYY-MM-DD 21:00:00Z` when the end is on another UTC date
builder  budget gate open  wheel human                     <- no pause stood (the reply holds no `override_until`)
$ viola link overseer builder
link    overseer -> builder  since 19:43:58Z               <- `already linked` for an existing pair
$ viola unlink overseer builder
unlink  overseer -> builder
$ viola answer builder 7 < response.json
answered  builder  dialog 7
unable  builder  not-delivered  unknown-dialog             <- stderr, exit 13, then its hint line
hint: that dialog is not pending; viola list shows the current DIALOG
```

`viola release <name> --budget` prints one of two stdout lines, exit 0, with the wheel left where it is. `<name>  budget gate lifted until <end>  wheel <holder>` when a pause stood: `<end>` is the reply's `override_until` as `HH:MM:SSZ` on the current UTC date and as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SSZ` on any other date, and a value that is no RFC 3339 instant prints escaped. `<name>  budget gate open  wheel <holder>` when no pause stood. The date form and the `budget gate open` line are the founder's wording: planning forms as built (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor, on the operator's word) that he confirmed as they were shown to him, his own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's word superseded 2026-10-13) (design-system §Surface: cli, Component Patterns 4).

`viola link <driver> <driven> [--json]` and `viola unlink <driver> <driven> [--json]` act on the driven instance and each print one stdout line in one write, plain in every mode, exit 0: `link    <driver> -> <driven>  since <HH:MM:SSZ>`, the reply's `since` as UTC clock time in whole seconds (a `since` that is no RFC 3339 instant, such as the restore's `unknown`, prints escaped); `link    <driver> -> <driven>  already linked` for a pair already held; `unlink  <driver> -> <driven>` whether or not a pair was removed. The names printed are the verb's own arguments, never names read back from the reply. Under `--json` each prints the reply's `ok` as `{"v":1,"ok":<ok>}`: `{"v":1,"ok":{"since":<ts>,"already_linked":<bool>}}` for `link`, `{"v":1,"ok":{}}` for `unlink`. A wrapper error, a `driver` equal to `driven` (`-32602`) included, is the wrapper-fault line, exit 20; the exit-21 refusals are under Primary content block 2.

title: Output structure — `viola verify`

body:
```
$ viola verify                                             (a Unix host: 24 relied rows)
[01/24] shim-resolution claude resolves to a real executable  pass
...
[06/24] largest-hook-payload every hook payload fits the frame cap  pass
[07/24] modal-signature an untrusted start shows a compiled modal literal  pass
...
[10/24] confirm-window the typed prompt reaches UserPromptSubmit within the window  pass
[11/24] question-answer a question answered through PreToolUse takes effect  pass
...
[14/24] dialog-concurrency two parallel questions each raise a dialog  pass
[15/24] long-paste-wrapper a long paste unwraps to the text as pasted  pass
[16/24] tag-escaping tag-like text un-escapes to the text as pasted  pass
[17/24] local-command-clear /clear starts a new session and submits no prompt  pass
[18/24] paste-newline an LF inside a paste stays inside the one prompt submitted  pass
[19/24] statusline-override a --settings statusLine runs in the status line's place  pass
[20/24] statusline-shell a statusline command runs through /bin/sh  pass
[21/24] statusline-rate-limits the statusline payload carries two whole-number rate_limits windows  pass
[22/24] resume-session --resume <id> reopens the session under that id  pass
[23/24] agents-join claude agents --json names the live session by pid and session id  pass
[24/24] local-command-compact /compact keeps the session id and submits no prompt  pass
stamped 2.1.287  24 pass  0 fail                           <- last stdout line; `fail` is never coloured

$ viola verify
...
stamped 2.1.287  22 pass  2 fail                           <- a failing row: exit 1, the stamp still written

$ viola verify                                             (stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM before its rows are checked)
unable: verify was stopped before it finished              <- stderr; stdout empty, no step line, no summary
hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI             <- the last stderr line: exit 1, no stamp written
```

Usage: `viola verify [--record <DIR>] [-- <program> [args…]]` (program default `claude`). One stdout step line per relied ledger row, `[NN/MM] <row id> <row words>  pass|fail`, in ledger order (`shim-resolution` · `spine-hooks` · `session-start-fields` · `prompt-verbatim` · `stop-message` · `largest-hook-payload` · `modal-signature` · `input-box-signature` · `quiet-period` · `confirm-window` · `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency` · `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear` · `paste-newline` · `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits` · `resume-session` · `agents-join` · `local-command-compact`; `MM` is the relied count, `LedgerRow::relied()`'s length: 24 on Unix, 21 on Windows, where the relied set skips the three statusline rows because the status line is not wrapped there and ends at `local-command-compact`; it grows as owning chunks land their rows), then the `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail` summary as the last stdout line. Exit 0 when every relied row passes, 1 on a failing row, a refusal (the `unable:`/`hint:` pairs, Primary content block 2) or a stop: a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (Unix `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, Windows Ctrl-C / Ctrl-Break) before its rows are checked prints only that plain ASCII pair, with no name, path or pid, and writes no stamp (chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). `--record` adds no human line. Plain ASCII, no colour. Each step line is appended once, with no progress bar and no redraw. `viola verify --help` adds one static ASCII paragraph naming no path: run it from a folder you trust in Claude Code (the input-box probe runs in a subfolder there, which inherits that trust), and an unapproved external CLAUDE.md import blocks the probe (its dialog shows in the subfolder, and verify never answers it).

title: Output structure — `viola --help`

body:
```
$ viola --help
Usage: viola [--home <dir>] <verb> [args]

board:    list
traffic:  send, wait, last, answer
wheel:    pause, release
handoff:  link, unlink
setup:    run, revive, verify, plugin install
```

**As built** (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline): `viola --help` (and `viola help`) prints exactly `Usage: viola [--home <dir>] <verb> [args]`, a blank line, the five rows `board:    list` · `traffic:  send, wait, last, answer` · `wheel:    pause, release` · `handoff:  link, unlink` · `setup:    run, revive, verify, plugin install`, a blank line, `Options:` and clap's options (`--home <HOME>`, `-h, --help`, `-V, --version`); no about line and no clap `Commands:` list; plain ASCII, pinned by the `HELP` literal in `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`. Served verbs only: `help_lists_only_served_verbs` reads `plugin install` as one entry of the `setup:` row, a bare `plugin` unserved. The usage line is the override literal on every OS. `viola mcp` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) is a hidden verb (`#[command(hide = true)]`, no argument but the global `--home`), run only by the plugin (`plugin/.mcp.json` registers it with the absolute pinned path and `["mcp"]`), never by a person: it appears in no row, and the `HELP` literal is unchanged.

`viola <verb> --help` gives clap's per-verb usage, unchanged; its usage line names the program by its executable, `viola.exe` on Windows. Prompt text comes from stdin or `--file`, never from a leading-slash argument, and help says so on `send`.

title: Output structure — `viola run`

body:
```
$ viola run builder -- claude
(nothing: the terminal belongs to the wrapped claude TUI until it exits)

$ viola run builder -- claude
unable: builder is already live                           <- stderr, exit 1; no paths, no pids
hint: viola list                                          <- stderr, the last line
```

title: Output structure — `viola revive`

body:
```
$ viola revive builder
(nothing: the terminal belongs to the resumed claude TUI until it exits)

$ viola revive builder --list
2026-10-10T14:21:07.512Z  startup  3f2b8c1e-7a4d-4e9b-9c10-5d6e7f8a9b0c    <- stdout, one row per logged session
2026-10-10T14:35:40.118Z  resume  3f2b8c1e-7a4d-4e9b-9c10-5d6e7f8a9b0c

$ viola revive builder
unable: builder's recorded directory is missing           <- stderr, exit 1; no paths, no pids, no logged id
hint: resume it by hand from a directory you choose: viola run builder -- claude --resume <id>, ids from viola revive builder --list
```

Usage: `viola revive <name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [-- <child args>]`, or `viola revive <name> --list` (`--list` conflicts with `--id`, `--fork` and the trailing arguments), each with `[--json]`. A start that passes its preflight prints nothing of its own while the child holds the terminal, as `viola run`. `--list` prints one stdout row per logged session in log order, `<ts>  <cause>  <id>` with two spaces between fields, no header and no colour, plain ASCII, with an empty stderr; the cause is `startup`, `clear`, `resume` or `compact` as logged, and `unknown` otherwise. Each refusal is exit 1 with one `unable:` line and one `hint:` line last on stderr and an empty stdout:
- `unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only`
- `unable: <name> is already live` / `hint: viola list` (`run`'s collision pair, and its stale sibling, unchanged)
- `unable: <name> has no logged session to resume` / `hint: start one: viola run <name> -- claude`
- `unable: <name> has no logged session with that id` / `hint: viola revive <name> --list`

- `unable: <name>'s session is open in another claude` / `hint: close it there first, or start a copy: viola revive <name> --fork` (the founder's wording, his own answer to P4 fork 4 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`)
- `unable: <name>'s recorded directory is missing` / the hint shown above

The hints are distinct and none names `viola release`. `--list` has two of the refusals (state files, no logged session). After the state-files check and before its wrapper log opens, the start checks its home tree as `run`'s start does: a refused home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/` or pinned copy prints the home pair `unable: the viola home is not private to you` / `hint: the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions`, a refused instance the state-files pair, each exit 1 with no log opened and no child (under `--json` the `strict-modes-failed` document). The start reads its preflight in a fixed order, the holder, the logged session, `session-live` (one `claude agents --json` read: a row whose `sessionId` is the logged id refuses; skipped under `--fork`; a failed read passes and the start goes on), then the recorded directory. A malformed `--id` is clap's usage error, exit 2.

Under `--json` (both arms; chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract) each refusal above is one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}`, exit 1, empty stderr, `<code>` one of `strict-modes-failed`, `already-live` (a live holder or a fresh replayed beat), `stale-heartbeat` (a stale holder), `no-session` (both of its pairs), `session-live`, `cwd-missing`; `--list --json` prints the rows as one document in log order, fields as the human rows, or the `no-session` document with exit 1. Without `--json` the pairs and the rows stay byte-identical. Under `--json` a refusal of the start `revive` shares with `run`, after a passed preflight, prints one exit-1 document too, with stderr empty: `<code>` is `batch-script-child`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `squatted-name`, `socket-dir-refused` (without `--json` the socket-directory pair of Primary content block 2), or `internal-error` for a program not found and for an error of the start itself, whose chain the catch site still logs. A `pump_child` error prints no document, the child having held the terminal.

title: Output structure — `viola plugin install`

body:
```
$ viola plugin install
viola@viola  written  <home>/marketplace          <- stdout, one write
run these to add it to Claude Code:
  claude plugin marketplace add <home>/marketplace
  claude plugin install viola@viola

$ viola plugin install --json
{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}

$ viola plugin install
unable: the viola home is not private to you              <- stderr, exit 21; nothing created, no log opened
hint: the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions
```

Usage: `viola plugin install [--json]`; `viola plugin` alone is a clap usage error (exit 2), and clap serves its own `viola plugin help [install]`. The verb writes the marketplace tree, then prints its four lines in one plain-ASCII stdout write, no SGR, never redrawn: `<dir>` is the canonical home joined with `marketplace`, printed bare unless the host's shell would split it (Unix: single-quoted unless every character is an ASCII letter, a digit or one of `_ - . / :`; Windows: double-quoted when it holds a space). The lines are as built (chunk 2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install). Under `--json` it prints the `ok` document above, no path. A refused strict-modes check of the home or a `marketplace/` tree dir is exit 21 with the home pair on stderr and stdout empty, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` with stderr empty. A failed exe read, dir creation or file write is the `cli` catch site's `error: internal error`, exit 1, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout with stderr empty.

title: Component — Header / banner (the BAY context line)

data.head: ### Component — Header / banner (the BAY context line)

body: - **The only header on any verb** is the one static BAY line at the top of `viola list`.

- **Cell order:** `BAY`, `5H <n> %`, `7D <n> %` (each followed by `expired` when the window has passed), `read <age> ago`, `gate open` or `budget-paused`, `skipped a - b - c`. Cells are separated by the two-space gutter.
- **Typography:** Label words and Data figures, all in the default foreground. There is no bold, no colour, no box drawing and no rule line under it.

- **No banner anywhere:** no ASCII-art logo, no tagline and no version line on normal output. The version appears only in `--version` / `--help`. `viola run` prints nothing, and `viola hook` / `viola mcp` have no human surface.

title: Component — Primary navigation (verb structure)

body: - **Flat verbs:** one lower-case word each (`plugin install` is the one two-word verb). There is no nested noun hierarchy, no interactive prompt, no TUI mode and no pager.

- **Argument order mirrors the channel `params`:** `viola <verb> <target>` for one strip, `viola link|unlink <driver> <driven>` for a handoff, `viola answer <target> <dialog_id>`. `<target>` is always a `ViolaName`. Unwrapped names are never valid targets.
- **Board vs. strip:** `viola list` shows the whole bay. Every other verb acts on one strip.

- **Global flag `--home`:** the same on every verb. `--json` is the machine view of every data verb, `viola revive` included (both arms: its refusal document and `--list`'s `ok.sessions`; chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract).

- **Discoverability:** `--help` groups verbs as board / traffic / wheel / handoff / setup; as built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline) it prints all five groups over the served verbs, `handoff:` holding `link, unlink` and `setup:` holding `plugin install`. `hint:` lines point to the next verb by name (`viola wait builder`, `viola list`, `viola verify`). They are the CLI's breadcrumbs. No hint names `viola release`: the refusals that carry hints reach drivers, and a driver's `release` is refused (`-32602`, exit 20). `release` is a human verb reached through `--help`.

title: Component — Hero / signature output line (the `viola send` readback mirror)

data.head: ### Component — Hero / signature output line (the `viola send` readback mirror)

body: - **Layout:** a fixed first column holding the four-character box (`[RB]`, `[  ]`, `[/ ]`). Then one space, then the padded state word (`open` / `read back` / `unable` / `unconfirmable`). Then the two-space gutter, then NAME, then the outcome fields: time, `cursor`, `reason  detail`, or the unconfirmable note.

- **Issue left, readback right, spread over time:** the TTY issue line on stderr is the open box. The outcome line under it is the closed box. The two lines line up column for column, so the eye reads them as one strip entry.
- **Colour:** none, on purpose. The mirror is words and brackets only. `read back` is never green and `unable` is never red, because colour on the CLI is reserved for `DIALOG` and `stale`.
- **What never happens:** no `Sending…` spinner, no `✓`, no `done`. `turn-ended` is never reported as a send outcome. That is `viola wait`'s result.

- **Machine view:** `--json` prints only the typed document (`ok` with `submitted_at` + `cursor`, `ok` with `confirmed:false` + `unconfirmable`, or `refusal` + `detail`), with the typed exit code and no glyph and no hint.

title: Component — Primary content block 1: `viola list` strip rows

data.head: ### Component — Primary content block 1: `viola list` strip rows

body: - **Columns:** NAME · LIVE · STATUS · WHEEL · DIALOG · CLI. Each column is padded to its widest word (`stale`, `unknown`, `driver - budget-paused`, `DIALOG permission`, `2.1.281 unverified-cli`), with the two-space gutter between columns. There are no box-drawing borders.

- **Styling:**
  - NAME is bold (Callsign).
  - The `DIALOG` word takes `color-accent` and the kind word after it stays default. This is the CLI cocked strip.
  - A `stale` row is `color-text-muted` (dim) from end to end, and the word `stale` is always in LIVE.
  - Nothing else is styled.
- **Rack separator:** `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` on its own line before the unwrapped rows. The WRAPPED rack has no separator, because it is always first and the caption row heads it.
- **Truncation:** only unwrapped NAMEs, with `...`, and only where the terminal width is known. Wrapped names are never clipped. No line ever wraps.

- **Escaping:** every field that comes from `claude agents --json` has C0/C1 controls escaped as hex text, **including** `\n` and `\t` inside a row, so a row never splits and the columns stay fixed-width (T5 ratified; stricter than the security floor, which keeps `\n` / `\t` for `wait` / `last` text).
- **No link column:** the six shared columns stay fixed. Links are visible only as `link` / `unlink` verb output (`overseer -> builder`).

- **As built** (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; the rack, chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board): the wrapped rows, then the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` separator and the unwrapped rows when the agents read lists any; on a terminal that takes colour (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline) NAME bold, the `DIALOG` word amber with its kind word plain, a `stale` row dim end to end with only `DIALOG` amber and not dim, nothing else styled, and no SGR when colour is off; only an unwrapped NAME is cut, with `...`, and only on a terminal whose width is known and too narrow for it, never inside an escape; the row escape (`escape_row`) covers every control character, DEL and C1 included, and as built its upstream-derived cells are the recorded CLI version and each unwrapped NAME (a `claude agents --json` `sessionId`). The widths are under Output structure — `viola list` (piped).

title: Component — Primary content block 2: refusal lines and the `unable` column

data.head: ### Component — Primary content block 2: refusal lines and the `unable` column

body: - **Line form (stderr):** `unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>`, fields separated by two spaces. `viola send` pads `unable` into the mirror's word column after `[/ ]`. The fixed-message exceptions are the exit-1 start refusals of `viola run` (`unable: <name> is already live` and its sibling causes, listed in design-system cli pattern 2), the exit-1 refusals of `viola revive` (the same collision pair, and its own five pairs under Output structure — `viola revive`; under `--json` its `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document in place of the pair) and `viola verify`'s exit-1 refusals, each an `unable: <text>` line and its own `hint:` line with no name, path or pid: `the claude CLI was not found` / `install Claude Code or put it on PATH`; `the claude CLI is a .cmd or .bat script` / `pass the real executable, not a .cmd or .bat shim`; `the CLI version could not be read` / `run claude --version to check the install`; `a recorded fixture is not clean: <file> <code>` (a screen fixture: `<file> row <n>[ seam] <code>`; codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`; it names the fixture file and the check, never the content) / `record with a viola home under your user home`; `verify was stopped before it finished` / `run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` (a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM, stdout empty); `the viola home is not private to you` / `the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` (the home pair: its strict-modes check refuses the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/` before its log opens, or refuses the stamps write; stdout empty, no step line, no summary); plus run's pinned-copy refusal; and the home-tree refusal of the `viola run` and `viola revive` starts, checked before the wrapper log opens: the home pair for the home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/` or the pinned copy's folders and file, `revive`'s instance pair for the instance's state files, no log opened, no line, no child; and, on Unix, the socket-directory refusal of the `viola run` and `viola revive` starts, exit 1, made before any snapshot, child or bind, stdout empty and the directory left as found: `unable: the socket directory for <name> cannot be trusted` / `hint: viola's socket directory must be a directory you own, readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` (under `revive --json` its document, Output structure — `viola revive`); and `viola list`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal of the whole board (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list; the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer, the operator's answer superseded 2026-10-13), stdout empty: `unable: the viola home is not private to you` / `hint: the viola home must be readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` for the home or `instances/`, and `unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only` (`revive`'s pair) for one instance; and `viola plugin install`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal, stdout empty, the same home pair for the home or a `marketplace/` tree dir, nothing created and no log opened; and the exit-21 strict-modes refusal of the frame verbs `viola send` (after its text read), `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` (for these two `<name>` is the driven instance), made before any role file or log opens, stdout empty: `revive`'s instance pair (`unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` / `hint: viola will not read them; make the viola home and its files owner-only`), no line written to any log and the directory's mode left as found; under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` with stderr empty. A failed or panicked `cli` verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `verify`, `revive --list`, `plugin install`, `link`, `unlink`; a `revive` start stays outside it) prints exactly `error: internal error` once, from the one catch site, with no hint, and with `--json` among the arguments before a `--` prints `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout in its place with stderr empty (for `wait` / `last` exit 1 also covers a refusal reply, an unparseable reply or any other channel error; for `link` / `unlink` a refusal reply or an `ok` of another shape; for `list` an `instances/` that cannot be listed and a log start that fails, while a per-instance read error gives no row).

- **Refusals decided before any request:** `viola send` refuses two texts itself, before any frame: one that holds a refused character (`not-delivered  control-character`) and one whose typed text is empty once its trailing CR and LF characters are removed, the empty text included (`not-delivered  empty-text`). Each takes the same `[/ ] unable  <name>  not-delivered  <detail>` line on stderr with exit 13, and its hint as the last stderr line (for `empty-text`: `hint: the text is empty once its trailing newlines are removed; send a text with content`). Under `--json` it is one document on stdout with no stderr line. The wrapper makes the same two refusals for a frame sent straight to it.

- **Hint line:** directly under each refusal, `hint: <one plain instruction>`, keyed by reason (or by reason · detail). Exit 21 and exit 1 each have several causes, and every cause gets its own hint, so an agent can tell the causes apart from the last stderr line (design-system cli pattern 2). The exit-1 start refusal `unable: <name> is already live` takes `hint: viola list`. `wait`, `last`, `link` and `unlink`'s exit 21 `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` (for `link` / `unlink`, `<name>` is the driven instance) takes `hint: <name> is not running; viola list shows the live instances` when the instance is not running (`viola send`'s exit 21 keeps its `[/ ] unable` mirror with the same hint). A frame verb's exit 21 on a name with no directory at its instance path takes `hint: <name> is not a wrapped session; only sessions started with viola run take commands`, and with its wrapper lost while the call is open `hint: <name>'s wrapper went away during the call; viola list shows whether it is still running`, each the last stderr line in plain ASCII. On Linux, Windows and macOS (on macOS an euid mismatch alone, the pid and start-time comparison absent, the named carve-out, owned by no route entry) a frame verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`) whose server check finds that the process on the endpoint is not the recorded wrapper, or cannot make the check, writes no frame and exits 21 with the same `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line (`send` in its `[/ ] unable` mirror) and `hint: the process on <name>'s endpoint is not its recorded wrapper; it was not contacted` as the last stderr line; under `--json` it prints the exit-21 document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` with stderr empty. On Unix a frame verb meeting a refused socket directory writes no frame and exits 21 with the same `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line (`send` in its `[/ ] unable` mirror) and `hint: viola's socket directory must be a directory you own, readable only by you; viola does not change its permissions` as the last stderr line; under `--json` it prints the exit-21 document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` with stderr empty. There is no hint for the `unknown` refusal, whose detail is a code word or nothing, for `wrapper fault` or for `internal error`. A hint never quotes the sent text or any upstream text, and never names a path or a pid.

- **Exit codes as the typed tail:** 10 `human-typing`, 11 `budget-paused`, 12 `unverified-cli`, 13 `not-delivered`, 14 `unknown`, 20 wrapper fault (`error: wrapper fault  <code>`), 21 `unable  instance-unreachable` (for `viola list`, `viola plugin install` and the strict-modes refusal of `viola send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` the fixed state pair above instead). Under `--json` the same outcome is one document on stdout, with no stderr line and no hint text. The machine view of exit 21 carries the cause in its document's `detail`, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, `<cause>` one of `strict-modes-failed`, `instance-dead`, `unwrapped-name`, `endpoint-lost`, `server-verify-failed`, `socket-dir-refused`.
- **Streams:** results go to stdout. `waiting:`, the issue line, refusals, hints and errors go to stderr. The two are never mixed.

title: Component — Footer / terminator

body: - **No terminator word.** No `done.`, no `success`, no summary banner. The exit code is the terminator, and the last printed line always says what happened, to whom and where: `[RB] read back      builder  19:45:05.912Z  cursor 48213`, `answered  builder  dialog 7`, `link    overseer -> builder  since 19:43:58Z`.
- **On a refusal**, the `hint:` line is the last line on stderr.

- **On `verify`**, the summary `stamped <version>  <n> pass  <n> fail` closes a completed run; a run stopped before its rows are checked prints no summary, and its `hint:` line is the last line on stderr.
- **No persistent footer.** Terminal scrollback is the history. The tape lives in `events.ndjson`.

title: IA notes

body: - **Command model:** flat verbs plus a target. The board is `viola list` and the strip-level verbs act on one `ViolaName`. There are no subcommand trees beyond `plugin install`.
- **Deep links:** none, and the CLI has no URL coupling. The shared references are `ViolaName` (never case-transformed) and `cursor` (the byte offset `send` prints and `wait --after` consumes).

- **Output as a contract:** the human columns and words are stable, because LLM drivers may read them. New fields go into `--json` first. Adding a human column is a design change, not an implementation choice.

- **Shared vocabulary:**
  - The six captions, words and slot order are fixed, and a future page reuses them.
  - The readback vocabulary is `open`, `read back`, `unable`, `unconfirmable`. The CLI brackets the box.
  - ` - ` separates inside a CLI field, and an arrow is `->`. There is no CLI inbound `<-` form.
  - Amber means `DIALOG` and nothing else. `stale` is SGR dim in the terminal.
  - The CLI is where every action lives.

title: Decisions Log
body:
## Decisions Log

`2026-09-24`: Initial layout templates generated by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8.

**Surfaces covered:** web-spa (`viola ui`), cli (`viola` verbs).

**Key layout choices:**
- **web-spa:** one route and one bay, in four fixed regions (ATIS header, WRAPPED rack, UNWRAPPED · READ-ONLY rack, TAPE). There is no nav chrome, no hero and no page footer. Strips are fixed-field grid rows on `--strip-cols`, in stable name order, never a card grid.
- **web-spa:** the tape is the only bounded scroll region, filling the viewport below the racks with a ten-line floor. This keeps the racks, and any cocked strip, in view while history is read. The page scrolls only when the racks plus that floor exceed the viewport.
- **web-spa:** transfer markers are `--line-h` lines in the rack gap on `color-surface-base`, under the driver (outbound, with the box) and under the driven strip (inbound twin, no box). There is no graph.
- **web-spa:** state strips (first reading, empty, 503, tape stopped) occupy the rack or tape position they describe. They are words only, with no loaders.
- **cli:** `viola list` is the single board, with one static BAY header and six padded columns identical to the web strip. Every other verb prints one or two phraseology lines, and the exit code is the terminator.
- **cli:** `viola send` is the only verb carrying the bracketed readback mirror. Other verbs share only its `unable` word column.

**Cross-surface IA decisions:**
- One token vocabulary (`color-*`, `space-*`, `radius-*`, typography roles) is used on both surfaces. The web resolves it to the CSS aliases in `/assets/app.css`, and the cli to the SGR tokens, the terminal default foreground or "not used". Differences are platform mechanics only: ANSI depth, the two-space gutter, ASCII `->` / ` - `, and brackets for the ruled box.
- The same six fields, words and slot order apply on both surfaces. `ViolaName` and `cursor` are the only shared references. There is no URL coupling.
- The web shows state and history. The CLI is the only place actions happen. The web's only printed command is the empty-rack `viola run <name> -- claude`.

**Signature placement strategy:**
- **web-spa:** `<viola-readback>` at the far right of every tape `send` line (spanning the last two `--tape-cols` tracks) and of every outbound `<viola-transfer>` marker once a send on that link is seen (`unknown` before that). It is one element and one drawing in both places, and both flip in the same frame.
- **cli:** the `[  ]` issue line (stderr, TTY) plus the `[RB]` / `[/ ]` / `[  ] unconfirmable` outcome line of `viola send`, with the `unable` word column carried into every verb's refusal line.
- **Supporting element:** the cocked strip on `<viola-session-row>`, mirrored by the amber `DIALOG` word in `viola list` and by `document.title`.

**Motion trigger placement:**
- **The cock** (the only High-impact moment): `<viola-session-row>` in the WRAPPED rack, when its `dialog_pending` turns true. It plays `translateX(--cock-offset)` over `--cock-dur` once. The band turns `color-accent` and the DIALOG cell insets in the same frame. The return into line is instant. It never fires in the tape, on unwrapped strips or on the CLI.
- **Ambient fade:** tape lines and `<viola-transfer>` markers that arrive over SSE after first paint (`data-live`) fade in over `--fade-dur`. The first paint is instant.
- **Deliberately instant:** the readback fill and strike (tape and marker), `stale` dimming, `unlink` removal, the header gaining a line, the `N new lines below` count and the `read Nm ago` age.
- **Reduced motion:** both durations are zero, and the cock position and band persist.
- **cli:** no motion. Nothing redraws in place, and nothing uses a spinner or progress bar. `verify` appends step-counter lines.

**Responsive breakpoints (web only):**
- ≥1024: primary, with one-line strips on `--strip-cols`.
- 760–1023: two-line strips on `--strip-cols-wrapped` / `--strip-rows-wrapped` / `--strip-areas-wrapped`, a caption row on the same template, the ATIS header on three or more lines, and tape word/reason ending in an ellipsis with the full text in the expanded body.
- <760: reserved for the later phone view and not laid out in v1.
- Never horizontal scroll at any supported width. Racks keep `--cock-offset` end padding.

**Notable surface-specific deferrals:**
- The 401 access strip content and recovery copy, the `viola ui` launch line's credential content, and the v1.x brake controls (`I HAVE CONTROL`, `UNLINK`, Raised-3 confirmation). Their placement and copy are deferred to implementation with the security plan. No control slot is reserved in the v1 bay.
- The phone view layout below 760, deferred to the later authenticated remote view.
- The polite-announcement mechanics and semantic roles of racks, strips and the tape are owned by a11y. This document only names what is announced.
- The data plumbing that sets a strip's `dialog_pending` live, and the CL-1 events (`send-issued` with `cursor` and `from`, `send-refused`, and the `unconfirmable` outcome). Until CL-1 lands, the layout shows only `read` boxes and `unknown` in marker last-send cells.

**Notes:**
- Four copy lines are layout decisions that were not spelled out in the design system: `no unwrapped sessions` (empty unwrapped rack), the tape INSTANCE cell of a send line printing the sending instance (it depends on CL-1 carrying `from`), the `space-micro` inline padding of boxed ATIS words, and `color-text-primary` for rack separator labels.
- The design system's Component Patterns 1–6 (web) and 1–5 (cli) were the starting point. This document adds the region order, the tape's bounded scroll region, per-screen instances (`builder` / `overseer` / `scratch` / `c1f9e2a4…`) and the concrete trigger points. It changes no token, colour, font stack, expression level or signature drawing.

`2026-09-24`: Overseer fix pass 2026-09-24 (cross-plan findings, founder-delegated). Each item was checked against the cited upstream line first.
- **T3:** the Discoverability breadcrumb no longer suggests `viola release builder --budget`. Drivers receive these hints, and a driver's `release` is refused (security: driver-originated `release`, `-32602`, exit 20).
- **T4:**
  - The refusal-line component now carries one hint per exit-21 and exit-1 cause, pointing to design-system cli pattern 2. Tests' exit-cause matrix requires a cause-specific hint.
  - `--json` carries no hint text. A per-cause detail code there is pending an arch amendment, because arch fixes `"detail":null` for exit 21.
- **T5 (ratified):** `list` row escaping also escapes `\n` / `\t`. This is stricter than the security floor.
- **By:** manual edit, overseer fix pass 2026-09-24.

`2026-09-24`: overseer fix pass 2, 2026-09-24 (cross-plan findings "a11y P3.5", founder-delegated). Checked against the cited lines first.
- **Y4 (a11y-plan D-A11Y-19):** the focus ring is named `--focus-ring`, the design-system token, in the Focus rule and in Quality check 10. The `color-border-focus` alias row in the token map becomes a pointer to `--focus-ring`. It already resolved there, so this is a naming change only, with no visual change. The other `color-*` aliases in the map are unchanged, because they were not part of the finding.
- **By:** manual edit, overseer fix pass 2, 2026-09-24 (founder-delegated).

`2026-09-24`: overseer fix pass 3, 2026-09-24 (cross-plan findings "a11y vs upstreams", founder-delegated). Checked against the cited line first.
- **Z10 (a11y-plan D-A11Y-06):** the out-of-view announcement scope now matches the a11y plan and design-system: a strip turning cocked, a readback refusal and `TAPE stopped`, plus the 401 access strip (announced instead of `TAPE stopped` after a `viola ui` restart) and a 503 / 404 / 405 rack strip that appears after first render. Quality check 7 points to this list, so it follows unchanged.
- **By:** manual edit, overseer fix pass 3, 2026-09-24 (founder-delegated).
