title: 5-command implementation

body: **`boot`**: start the product for testing.

- Command body: `scripts/agent-run.sh boot [--session <id>] [--instance <name>[:<fake-agent-args>]]... [--unstamped] [--cli-version <ver>] [--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed] [--statusline-echo]`. With no `--instance` flag, the instances are `overseer` and `builder`, whatever other flags are given (for example Path 6's `--statusline-echo`). One or more `--instance` flags replace that default list. `--agents-mode` defaults to `recorded`. `--statusline-echo` (built at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs; clap `conflicts_with` `--unstamped`, the misuse usage `arguments`: the home exists only once step 4's `viola verify` made it) runs after step 4 and before step 5. It configures the user statusline command as `<bin dir>/viola-fake-agent[.exe] statusline-echo <home>/fake/statusline.marker`, both paths with forward slashes, in the settings source that `run` reads, redirected into the session home: it writes `<home>/statusline-source.json` (`viola_state::fs::replace_private`, 0600, the settings shape `{"statusLine":{"type":"command","command":…}}`), which viola only reads and which is the source whenever it exists, and makes `<home>/fake/` through `create_private_dir`. A bin dir or home holding a character outside ASCII letters, digits and `_ - . / :` fails boot `reason:"build-failed"`. It sets no env var and writes no `budget.json`. It is used by Path 6 (§6 Path 6 step 1, `crates/viola-e2e/tests/path6_budget_harness.rs`). A `reason:"statusline-source-unresolved"` refusal is dropped: its premise (an unnamed source) is gone, and no entry owes it. `--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed` (built at the same chunk; an unknown value is usage `arguments`) writes the fake agent's `agents-mode` file beside the session's `bin/claude[.exe]` copy, which the fake reads beside its exe; it sets no env var (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`). A stale file is removed before step 4 and the value written (`replace_private`, 0600) after step 4 and the statusline plant, before `supervise.json`: step 4's Run B reads `claude agents --json` through that same copy, so a mode written first failed the `agents-join` row (`verify-failed`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs under `malformed`). It is recorded as `agents_mode` (serde default) in `session.json` and `supervise.json`, so a spec can reproduce the E1 unwrapped row. Steps:
  1. `cargo build --workspace --features viola/fake-agent` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<workspace root>/target/harness`. It never builds into the `target/` that the shim's `cargo run` uses: on Windows a running `target/debug/viola-harness.exe` cannot be relinked, and a workspace-wide build re-fingerprints it (measured 2026-09-24: `os error 5`, `UnitDependencyInfoChanged`). On failure it reports `reason:"build-failed"`, and no timeout applies to this step.
  2. Choose the home under the workspace's `target/e2e-home/` (obs-plan §9: CI's zero-panic G2 gate, the G4 schema gate, the secret scan and the `diag-<os>` upload all read `target/e2e-home/**`). Create a unique parent with `tempfile::Builder::new().prefix("viola-session-").tempdir_in("<workspace root>/target/e2e-home")?.keep()` and pass `<parent>/home`, which does **not** exist yet, as `--home`. viola then creates the home itself: 0700 on Unix, and on Windows the explicit protected user + SYSTEM DACL that security requires for a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%` (a hosted runner's workspace is outside it). A home pre-created by the harness would inherit the workspace ACL and fail the Windows strict-modes check. The base `target/e2e-home` itself is prepared before the `tempdir_in` by `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/mod.rs`): a plain base (absent, or a directory) is created as a directory; on Unix a base that is a link must have an absolute target, which is made with mode 0700 when it is gone (one non-recursive create, never a chmod after, never a parent) and accepted only when one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refused when its filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`; the message and the floor: §3 Test data bootstrap); on Windows it is the plain create. A refused base reads `reason:"build-failed"`, the reason a failed create gave before; none was added. On the Linux dev host the base is an operator-set link to the owner-only tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>` (§5 Setup / teardown lifecycle); the path string is unchanged, and no CI runner has a link.
  3. Copy `<bin dir>/viola-fake-agent[.exe]` (see step 5) to `target/agent-run/<session>/bin/claude[.exe]`, and put that dir first on a harness-scoped `PATH`, passed per child via `Command::env` and never `set_var`. It serves both `viola verify` and the `claude agents --json` stub.
  4. Unless `--unstamped` is given, run `viola verify --home <home>` against the fake agent driven with `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root <workspace root> --dialogs --framing`, so its print probe and all five interactive runs (Run A, Run B with its five added compiled pastes — the long, the tag-like and the newline texts, then `/compact`, then `/clear` — the dialog Runs C and D, and Run E, the `--resume` start of Run B's first session) stamp every relied ledger row (`LedgerRow::relied()`: all twenty-four on Unix, elsewhere twenty-one, the first eighteen, `resume-session`, `agents-join` and `local-command-compact`), Run B also making its one `claude agents --json` read (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) and carrying on Unix its one probe `--settings` (`typed/statusline.json`), whose status line the hidden `hook statusline --capture` arm files (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, relayed verbatim by the operator). This requires exit 0 and a last stdout line matching `^stamped \S+  \d+ pass  0 fail$`. It is the only writer of `ledger/stamps.json`; see Decisions Log.
  5. Spawn the supervisor `viola-harness supervise --session <id>` as an ordinary child process (no detach flags; it outlives `boot` and stops only through `stop.request`). It owns one portable-pty (`=0.8.1`, via the `viola-pty` seam) outer PTY per instance — a master writer, the child and a drain thread — and runs `viola run <name> --home <home> -- <bin dir>/viola-fake-agent[.exe] --cli-version <ver> --fixtures <workspace root>/fixtures/claude --receipt <home>/fake/<name>.receipt.ndjson --control <home>/fake/<name>.control --screens --trusted-root <cwd> <fake-agent-args>`, so a booted wrapper shows the trusted ready screen, where `viola` is also taken from `<bin dir>`. `--fixtures` names the parent dir: the fake agent joins `<cli-version>` itself, so replay follows `--cli-version` even under `--report-version`. `--plugin-dir` is not passed by the harness: `viola run` passes it to the child (architecture §Occupied Resources, Claude Code integration names). It drains every master on its own thread. `<bin dir>` is the directory boot step 3 copies from: `target/harness/debug` (boot step 1's target dir) for the CLI, the test executable's own target dir for `harness_session`, and `target/perf/release` for `--perf`. The harness never reads `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`, because Cargo sets that only for the root package's own integration tests. `<workspace root>` is resolved from `cargo metadata` or `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../..` and passed as an absolute path, because nextest runs `viola-e2e` tests with `crates/viola-e2e` as the cwd. The control file is created empty before spawn. Both rstest `booted_wrapper` copies pass the same `--control` path.

- Readiness signal. `boot` polls with a bounded 100 ms interval against a deadline; this is a file-state probe, not a sleep-based synchronisation. Readiness is staged. First the instance's `diagnostics/run-<name>.ndjson` holds a `process-start` line for `subject:"self"` and one for `subject:"claude-child"`, and both pids are alive by pid + start time (missing: `<name>:run-process-start`, `<name>:child-process-start`); a `process-exit` for `subject:"self"` first is `run-exited`. Only then are the checks below read (missing: `<name>:snapshot`, `<name>:endpoint`, `<name>:heartbeat`), and once those hold, the start records (missing: `<name>:events`); each joins as its surface lands. Per instance, all of the following must hold:
  - `instances/<name>/snapshot.json` parses with `pid`, `started_at`, `child_pid` and `endpoint` in its `data` (no `endpoint`: `<name>:endpoint`)
  - `heartbeat` mtime is less than 5 s old
  - `events.ndjson` lines 1–3 are `kind:"wheel"` with `data.cause:"start"`, then `kind:"budget-gate"`, then `kind:"session-start"` with `source:"hook"` (the fake agent fires SessionStart since "Hooks to normalised events", and Path 1 asserts line 3; `boot` checks all three through `start_records`, its fourth readiness stage, because `supervise` hands every booted fake agent `--fixtures <root>/fixtures/claude`, the recorded set)

- Exit code: 0 on ready within the timeout. Otherwise it exits 1 with `{"v":1,"cmd":"boot","ok":false,"reason":"build-failed"|"verify-failed"|"run-exited"|"readiness-timeout", "instance":<name|null>, "exit_code":<int|null>, "missing":[<unmet readiness checks>]}`. When the reason is `run-exited`, `exit_code` is the wrapper's exit code verbatim (for example 1 for a `live` or `stale` name, or a tampered pinned copy).
- Timeout: 20 s per instance after the build.
**`run`**: invoke test suites.

- Command body: `scripts/agent-run.sh run [--unit|--integration|--e2e|--mutants|--coverage|--perf|--fuzz-replay|--all] [--filter <nextest-filterset>] [--file <path>]... [--package <member>] [--local-live]`. `--file` (repeatable) needs `--mutants` (clap `requires`): it scopes the mutation run to those sources, the inner fix-loop (step 4). `--package` also needs `--mutants`: it mutates one whole member, the boundary tier's form (step 4 Package). `--coverage`, `--fuzz-replay` and `--mutants` never join the default selection. With no selector and no `--local-live` the default is `--all`, which runs steps 1 and 2 in order (`--local-live` passed alone is a selection of its own and runs neither step); step 4 runs only under `--mutants`:
  1. Unit + integration: `cargo nextest run --workspace --features viola/fake-agent --profile ci -E '<layer filterset>'`, then `cargo test --workspace --doc`, both with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<workspace root>/target/harness` (boot step 1). JUnit is still read from `<workspace root>/target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`: nextest's store is workspace-root-relative whatever the target dir (measured 2026-09-24). The layer filtersets are:
     - unit: `kind(lib) | kind(bin)`
     - integration: `kind(test) & !binary(/^(path[0-9]*|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_/)`, the complement of step 2's layer, so a test binary reports in exactly one of the two. A `binary()` regex that matches no binary is a nextest filterset parse error, not an empty set (as measured on cargo-nextest 0.9.146 on the Linux dev host at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs: a scratch crate, exit 94 "operator didn't match any binary names"; first measured on 0.9.133, 2026-09-24); the regex matches the root `chaos_`, `contract_`, `cross_`, `tui_` and `path<N>_` binaries, so both layers parse in this workspace, and the harness's own throwaway-workspace cases plant one `path_` binary before an integration run.
  2. Fake-agent E2E: `cargo nextest run --workspace --features viola/fake-agent --profile ci -E 'binary(/^(path[0-9]*|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_/)'`, suite `nextest-e2e`, run third after step 1's two nextest runs (`run --e2e`; in the default and `--all`), through the same nextest shape and target dir, a `--filter` intersecting it. `[0-9]*` after `path` admits the numbered Path binaries (`path1_run_start`, `path6_budget_harness`), which the written `^(path|…)_` did not select (as measured at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs: 18 binaries, and `run --integration` ran `path1`). 20 binaries / 157 tests at that chunk's end. `run --e2e` alone runs no doctest (doctest stays with step 1 and `--coverage`); the run-archive list is unchanged (unit, integration and coverage JUnit). Every nextest test uses one boot model:
     - No test shells out to `agent-run` / `viola-harness`, so there is never a nested `cargo run` inside nextest.
     - Root `tests/` suites use the rstest chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper`.
     - `crates/viola-e2e` scenarios use one of two boot models, chosen by the scenario's §6 Cleanup line:
       - Cleanup "harness `cleanup`" (Paths 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, E3): `viola_e2e::harness::session::harness_session(test, label, opts) -> HarnessSession`, a plain function and drop guard (`viola-e2e` carries no `[dev-dependencies]`, so never an rstest fixture), landed at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs. It calls the same library code as the `boot` / `cleanup` commands (`viola_e2e::harness::{boot, cleanup}`) with `stamp: !opts.unstamped` (`SessionOptions::unstamped`, default false, so the default session is stamped — the in-test form of `boot --unstamped`, chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers, whose Path 7 MCP leg boots the default `overseer` + `builder` pair unstamped, `SessionOptions { unstamped: true, ..SessionOptions::default() }`), and the library `boot` spawns the `supervise` process from the given binary dir, so `cleanup`'s pid + start-time proof stays exact (fork 2 of that chunk, `inputs#I1`). `SessionOptions` defaults to `overseer` + `builder`, no `--statusline-echo`, `--agents-mode recorded`, stamped (`unstamped` false); the guard exposes `home()`, `instance_dir(name)`, `bin_dir()`, `session()`, `workspace()` and `cleanup(self)`, panics with the boot document unless ready, and never shells out to `agent-run`. Its `Drop` runs `cleanup` (the home kept) unless `cleanup(self)` ran, then removes the home's parent unless `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`, or `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` while the test is panicking. `harness_session` always skips boot step 1, so no `cargo build` runs inside nextest. It passes `viola_e2e::harness::boot` the binary dir found from the test executable's own target dir (the assert_cmd `cargo_bin` lookup), never a literal `target/<profile>`, and boot step 3 copies the fake agent from that same dir. This is the same binary-dir parameter `--perf` uses (§10). As a result, the scenarios spawn the instrumented `viola` / `viola-fake-agent` under `--coverage`, and the plain debug binaries otherwise.
       - Cleanup "TempDir drop" or a test-owned outer PTY (Paths 1, 5, E1, E2, E5): the chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper` from `viola_e2e::fixtures`. Root `tests/support/` cannot be imported by another package, and the root package must not dev-depend on the tokio-based `viola-e2e`, so the chain exists twice (the sync root copy and the `viola-e2e` copy) against one contract. In both copies `stamped_home` runs `viola verify` against the fake agent. Today only the sync root copy exists (`tests/support/home.rs`; homes under `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*`). The `viola_e2e::fixtures` copy lands with its first consumer among these scenarios; Path 1's flow is not one, landing on the root chain as `tests/path1_run_start.rs` (fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs, `inputs#I1`). The root `stamped_home` runs `viola --home <h> verify -- <fake agent> --cli-version 2.1.287 --fixtures <root>/fixtures/claude` (the committed recorded set; `2.1.287` is the root chain's one literal, `tests/support/fake.rs` `RECORDED_CLI_VERSION`), and `stamped` is true only on exit 0 and a last line `stamped 2.1.287  <n> pass  0 fail`; anything else panics with the exit and match codes. `StampedHome::unstamped(TestHome)` (`stamped:false`, writes nothing) serves the tests that assert the unverified path. `booted_wrapper` drives the wrapper through a test-owned outer PTY (`tests/support/outer_pty.rs`; `Wrapper::boot/send/stop` in `tests/support/home.rs`, and `tests/run_cli.rs::run_viola`) and waits for `process-start` lines for `self` and `claude-child` and a fake-agent `start` receipt, each newer than the boot (a `gone` name's files are reused) — the receipt means its terminal is raw, so no key sent after it is swallowed — then for the snapshot (`pid`, `started_at`, `child_pid`) and a heartbeat under 5 s, bounded at 7 s — `WITHIN` in `tests/support/watch.rs`, shared by the root waits on a child (`Instant::now() + WITHIN` reads 28 sites in 20 files under `tests/`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor's wrap on the Linux dev host's final tree (the two new sites in `tests/cli_budget.rs` and `tests/cli_revive.rs`); architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem states the count's rule) and strictly below the nextest `mutants` profile's 10 s kill, so a stuck wait fails the test itself. `Wrapper::boot` always passes `--cli-version 2.1.287` (`--fixtures` stays a per-test extra). `Wrapper::stop` / `stop_keep` wait for the wrapper's exit and then, when the snapshot recorded an `endpoint`, for that endpoint to be unconnectable (`wait_endpoint_gone`; `unconnectable` is the harness `endpoint_gone` rule — on Windows a client connect reads NotFound, on Unix a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent, what `holder_gone` reads there). The kill path (`Wrapper::kill`, used by `tests/chaos_revive.rs`) kills the wrapper the test booted, waits for its exit, then for the child it recorded to be gone by pid and start time, then on `holder_gone` in place of `wait_endpoint_gone`: on Unix a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent, on Windows the pipe is not found. A killed wrapper removes nothing, so on Unix its socket file stays (the next bind takes over a leftover socket file) and a wait on the file being absent never ends after a kill (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive; the kill-and-revive case green on the three CI runners). The stop path keeps the `unconnectable` rule. An exit code is not the endpoint gone: on Windows the stopped wrapper's own pipe took a hook's connect and write 25 ms after its `process-exit` line, as measured at ci#36532038635; why the pipe outlives the observed exit is recorded, not established. Each wait notes what it polls (codes, counts and booleans, read in the predicate's own short-circuit order) to `<temp dir>/viola-root-watch/<test>.<label>.report`, one line per change, kept on a failure or a runner kill and removed on a pass. The wait is exit-aware: when `child.try_wait()` reports that the wrapper exited first, it fails at once (`wrapper <name> exited before ready`) instead of waiting out the bound. The bound stays below cargo-mutants' 20 s auto-timeout floor, so a mutant that stops the wrapper from getting ready grades as caught, not Timeout. Harness `boot` keeps its 20 s per-instance bound.
     - In §6, a step written `agent-run boot --session <id> <flags>` means `harness_session` with those flags. A Cleanup written `agent-run cleanup --session <id>` means harness `cleanup` as defined below. The `<id>` there (`p2`, `p7`) is only a readable label. The real session id always follows the `<test name>-<label>-<pid>` rule below, so neither parallel tests nor two sessions opened by one test (Path 7) share a session.
     - "Harness `cleanup`" means the test calls `session.cleanup()` at the end and asserts the report: no field `false` (an interim `null` field is allowed), same shape as the `cleanup` command. `Drop` is only a best-effort fallback for panicking tests.
     - The session id is `<test name>-<label>-<pid>`, where `<label>` is the §6 `--session` label (`p2`, `p7`, `p7-stamped`) or `main` when the step gives none. Each session gets its own temp home and its own `target/agent-run/<session>/` dir, because a session record holds exactly one `home`. The endpoint hash includes the absolute home, so the default `overseer` / `builder` names never collide across parallel tests.
  3. None in 0.1.0: the browser step left with the browser leg, and the mutation step keeps its number 4.
  4. Mutation:
     - Base: the whole chunk, derived by the harness from the repository's own history, so every run of an operator pass, fix pushes included, mutates the whole chunk. `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE` (trimmed, non-empty) is an explicit override, kept for the harness's own tests; nothing in CI sets it. Otherwise the harness reads `.andromeda/master-route.md` from HEAD's tree, takes the marker of every `{marker} · pending · ` record, and bounds its search at the parent of the OLDEST commit in HEAD's history whose message carries `chore({marker}): operator pre-CI commit`, or at HEAD when there is none (no pending record, or a chunk not yet pushed). The base is the last commit at or before the bound that added or removed a `· complete ·` master line (`git log -1 -G ' · complete · ' <bound> -- .andromeda/master-route.md`), i.e. the last master flip. When that commit is HEAD itself and the working tree's `.andromeda/master-route.md` holds no pending record HEAD's copy lacks (the wrap push, whose own commit is the flip), the base is `HEAD^`, so that push reads its own delta, never an empty diff. When that commit is HEAD but the working tree holds such a record, a promoted chunk is still uncommitted on top of the flip (/implement and the pre-commit operator pass, right after every wrap): the flip itself is the base, the base CI derives once the pre-CI commit lands (as measured at chunk 2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate: the old rule derived acd08c7 there while CI derived a69c5ef; `chunk_base_of_an_uncommitted_promotion_is_the_flip_at_head`). With no flip in history the base falls back to `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` (which never resolves on this project's single build branch). The bound exists because an unbounded pickaxe moves mid-pass: a fix commit that edits a `complete` record matches `-G` too (measured at chunk 2026-09-26-ci-chunk-base-and-union-verdict: a scratch-repo pass and `chunk_base_holds_the_flip_across_a_pass`). The chosen revision is resolved to its full sha (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet <rev>^{commit}`); when none resolves, `run --mutants` exits 1 with `reason:"base-missing"`. It never writes an empty `chunk.diff`, which cargo-mutants would report as zero mutants, i.e. a false `"mutants":{"tested":0}` pass.
     - Diff: the working tree plus every untracked, non-ignored file, against `merge-base(<base>, HEAD)`, written to `target/agent-run/chunk.diff` (any stale diff is deleted first). Both `git diff` argvs (the merge-base diff and each untracked file's `--no-index` diff) pin `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/`: a host's global `diff.mnemonicprefix=true` or `diff.noprefix=true` would otherwise write `c/ w/` or bare headers the Classification below cannot read (as measured at chunk 2026-10-03-mutation-scoring-completion, `chunk_diff_pins_its_prefixes_under_a_hostile_config`). /implement never commits, so the committed-only `git diff <base>...HEAD` would mutate nothing; on a committed tree with an ancestor base the two are equal.
     - Command: first `cargo build --package viola --features fake-agent` (the root package only: the harness tests spawn the root's `viola` and `viola-fake-agent`, cargo-mutants builds only the packages the diff touches, and a root-only build never relinks the running `viola-harness`; a failure is `reason:"build-failed"`), then `NEXTEST_PROFILE=mutants cargo mutants --workspace --features fake-agent --in-diff target/agent-run/chunk.diff --test-tool=nextest --copy-target=true --caught --unviable --build-timeout=400`, so the scratch copy carries those bins. Both builds use the mutation run's own cargo target dir, `MUTANTS_TARGET` = `target/mutants`: the root pre-build runs with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<repo>/target/mutants` and `cargo mutants` with the relative `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/mutants` (it was removed from the environment before), so each copied tree builds every test binary inside its own copy. A copied default `target/` keeps the original tree's `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*` paths, so root integration tests drove the unmutated binary (as measured at chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events `evidence/red-mutants-stale-test-binary.md`: a hand-applied mutant failed 4 tests in the repository and passed in the scratch). The command runs with `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=0` and `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=0`, overriding `ci.yml`'s workflow-wide `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`: a mutation run keeps no test home (the kept-home gates belong to the test job), since every home carries a pinned copy of the viola binary. cargo-mutants' stdout goes live to the harness's stderr instead of being captured, and `--caught --unviable` prints every outcome line (repo-relative name plus build and test seconds). A stalled or cancelled `run --mutants` therefore names the mutant it stopped at in its own stderr. `--build-timeout=400` (the shared `MUTANTS_PROGRESS`) bounds each mutant's build, which cargo-mutants leaves unbounded by default, with a fixed floor of 5 × the largest measured 78 s baseline; it replaced `--build-timeout-multiplier=5`, which cargo-mutants makes conflict with it and which derives a sub-second bound from a sub-second baseline (chunk 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id, Red B). As measured on CI run 36046091888 (windows, 2026-09-24): with the output captured, a stalled run printed nothing for 2 h 45 m. Without them a diff touching only `viola-e2e` fails its baseline (exit 4; measured 2026-09-24 on the dev host with a diff touching only `crates/viola-e2e`). `--copy-target` costs one copy of the target dir per run (2.9 GB of `target/` on the dev host, 2026-09-24). `--file <path>` (each one given) is passed beside `--in-diff`. On a Windows host (`HOST_SCRATCH`) the run first resolves the host mutation scratch `<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch` from the repository's absolute path and refuses unless its final component is exactly `viola-mutants-scratch` and the repository is neither it nor inside it (`reason:"scratch-refused"`, exit 1, never a fallback to `%TEMP%` or the repository). It then measures the scratch's bytes and removes and recreates it (`reason:"scratch-wipe-failed"` when the removal fails, a leaked process holding a file), the re-creation through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir`: the scratch takes the protected user + SYSTEM DACL, so every temp copy and test home laid inside it inherits owner-only, as one under `%TEMP%` does (a plain re-create on the runner's workspace drive inherited BUILTIN\Users write, and the root package's baseline failed the instance check there, run 38215104120). The decided keys are `unix`, `windows`, `target_family`, `target_os` and `target_arch`; any other key is unknown, and `not` / `all` / `any` are three-valued. The host's facts are compile-time constants, never a child process or an environment read. Then require `missed − host-excluded == 0 && timeout == 0 && unviable <= caught`. cargo-mutants' own summary and outcome lines still say MISSED for a left-out mutant, so the harness document judges the run, never those lines. A run with more unviable than caught mutants tested almost nothing, because its mutant builds failed. It is red with the `failures[]` code `unviable-exceeds-caught`, and `failed` = survivors + 1. With `--file` the object is `{"tested":N,"verdict":"scoped","base":"<sha>","files":[<the given paths>]}`: survivors stay red as in a counted run. A counted, scoped or package object also carries `"host_excluded"` when at least one mutant was left out (step 4, Verdict): an array of `{"name","cfg"}`, the name cargo-mutants' own and the predicate as written in source, repo-relative and never an absolute path. The field is absent when nothing was left out.

An absent source is skipped and named on stderr (`run-archive: skipped {name} (absent)`).

- Command body: `scripts/agent-run.sh status [--session <id>]`. It runs:
  - `<bin dir>/viola --home <home> list --json`, the bin dir and the session `bin/` read from `supervise.json` (`session.json` records neither), with `PATH` the session path so the fake agent answers `claude agents --json`, and `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` / `VIOLA_BIN` removed so the read files no role line under a host bridge's name; stdout read through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and parsed as one JSON object; with no `supervise.json` it spawns nothing (Status endpoint shape: `down`, `list-exit-none`)

- Polled fields:
  - per item: `name`, `wrapped`, `liveness`, `status`, `wheel`, `budget_paused`, `dialog_pending`, `cli_verified`
  - envelope: `skipped.{unknown_kinds,unknown_fields,torn_lines}` and `budget`

- Exit code:
  - 0 when `ok:true` (`state:"ready"`).
  - 1 for `degraded` or `down`. The full Status endpoint shape document is still printed, so an agent waiting for a `stale` transition reads exit 1 as a state, not a harness fault.
  - 2 on a usage error, or when no `session.json` exists for the id: `{"v":1,"cmd":"status","ok":false,"reason":"unknown-session"}`.
**`cleanup`**: tear down.

- Command body: `scripts/agent-run.sh cleanup [--session <id>|--all]`. Steps:
  1. Create `target/agent-run/<session>/stop.request`. The supervisor writes `\x03` into each outer PTY and presses it again every 500 ms until the child exits, because a Ctrl-C written into a child that has not set raw mode yet is swallowed: the fake agent exits on Ctrl-C.
  2. The supervisor calls `child.wait()` on every process handle with a 10 s deadline, then `Child::kill()` on survivors. It writes `supervisor-exit.json` with each exit status and a `killed` flag.
  3. Cleanup confirms the supervisor pid is gone via sysinfo (pid + start time) and reads that report.
  4. For each instance, `viola last <name> --json --home <home>` must exit 21. The endpoint recorded in the snapshot must be gone: on Windows a `viola-channel` client connect fails with NotFound, and on Unix a connect to the `<per-user 0700 dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` path is refused or the path is absent (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` on Linux, `$TMPDIR/viola/` on macOS, `/tmp/viola-<uid>/` as the fallback; security IPC access control). After a force-killed wrapper on Unix the leftover socket file stays until a next bind of that name takes it over: cleanup removes nothing of it, and its document reads `endpoint_gone` true and `ok:true` (`cleanup_after_a_force_killed_wrapper_reads_the_endpoint_gone`, `unconnectable_reads_a_leftover_socket_file_no_one_listens_on`).
  5. It removes the home dir with its `target/e2e-home/viola-session-*` parent and `session.json`. On the Linux dev host, where `target/e2e-home` is a link (`boot` step 2), that removal goes through the link and deletes outside the working directory; it takes only the `viola-session-*` dir the harness itself created (a boundary widening, ratified by the founder, live, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer). **In CI the home is kept:** `ci.yml` sets `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` workflow-wide (the `run --mutants` command alone overrides it to `0`), so step 6 removes only `session.json`, and the home stays under `target/e2e-home/` until obs-plan's gate steps have run (G2, G4, the secret scan and the scan-gated uploads, obs-plan §9 step order). The ephemeral runner then discards it with the job. `home_removed` reports `"kept"` in that mode, which is not a failure.
- Idempotency: cleanup MUST be idempotent. With no `session.json` it prints `{"v":1,"cmd":"cleanup","ok":true,"cleaned":[]}` and exits 0.

- Verification: reported in `{"cleaned":[…],"processes_gone":true,"endpoint_gone":true,"home_removed":true,"killed":[<names force-killed>]}`. `processes_gone` covers the supervisor, every wrapper and every child, by pid + start time; survivors are force-killed first. `endpoint_gone` is reported from the wrapper channel on. Any `false` field means exit 1. A force-kill is reported but does not by itself fail cleanup.
**`logs`**: fetch product logs.

- Command body: `scripts/agent-run.sh logs [--session <id>] [--instance <name>] [--kind <event-kind>] [--process run|hook|mcp|cli] [--after <byte offset>]`. It streams, as ndjson on stdout:
  - every `instances/<name>/events.ndjson` line, wrapped as `{"src":"events","instance":<name>,"offset":<byte offset>,"record":<line>}`
  - every per-process log line from `<home>/diagnostics/*.ndjson`, wrapped as `{"src":"diag","file":<basename>,"record":<line>}`
  - every content-bearing detail line from `<home>/instances/*/diagnostics/detail-*.ndjson` (obs-plan D-08), wrapped as `{"src":"diag","file":<basename>,"instance":<name>,"record":<line>}`. The added `instance` disambiguates, because every instance has its own `detail-<process>.ndjson` with the same basename. A panic line appears both in a role file and in its detail file, so panic counts use the role files only (`.file|startswith("detail-")|not`).

  Torn or unparseable lines are emitted as `{"src":…,"torn":true,"offset":n}` and never dropped. Assertions pipe into `jq -e` (jq 1.8.2) or jaq 3.1.1, for example `agent-run logs --instance builder --kind send-issued | jq -e '.record.data.cursor'`.
- Format: see Log format below.

- Retention window: the whole lifetime of the session home. Events are never truncated, and `cleanup` deletes the home, except in CI, where `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` keeps it until obs-plan's gate steps have run (`cleanup` step 5). On CI failure the home's `diagnostics/` and `events.ndjson` are uploaded as an artifact, after the secret-scan test has passed on them. Every harness and rstest home lives under `target/e2e-home/` (boot step 2), which is the root obs-plan's CI gates and upload read. On the Linux dev host that root is a link to a tmpfs directory, so a home kept there (`AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`) lives in memory: it does not survive a reboot, and `/tmp` ages out what is untouched for ten days. In CI nothing changes.
**Internal harness subcommands** (implemented in `viola-harness`, forwarded unchanged by the shims, not part of the agent's 5-command surface):

- **`supervise --session <id>`**:
  - Spawned only by `boot` step 5 (the CLI or the library call) as an ordinary child process that outlives `boot`, never by an agent or directly by a test. `boot` hands it `target/agent-run/<session>/supervise.json` (`home`, instances with fake-agent args).
  - It owns the outer PTYs from boot step 5 and drains each master on its own thread, keeping each master writer until its child exits. It watches for `stop.request` with the same bounded 100 ms file-state probe as boot readiness, then runs cleanup steps 1–2.
  - It writes `supervisor-exit.json` as `{"v":1,"cmd":"supervise","ok":<bool>,"exits":[{"name":<instance>,"exit_code":<int|null>,"killed":<bool>}]}`. Its stdout is discarded; the JSON document is the file.
  - Exit 0 when no child needed `kill()`, 1 otherwise, 2 on usage error.

- **`schema-check`** (the §6 Schema conformance check body behind obs-plan gate G4; CI step `id: schema-conformance`):
  - Walks `target/e2e-home/**`. A `*.ndjson` directly inside a `diagnostics/` dir is validated with jsonschema 0.57.0: home-level role files against `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `detail-*` files against `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`.
  - A non-JSON line is counted as `torn`. A directory at such a path, which some tests create to force an I/O error, is counted as `skipped_non_file` and never read.
  - It prints `{"v":1,"cmd":"schema-check","ok":<bool>,"files":N,"lines":N,"torn":N,"skipped_non_file":N,"failures":[{"file","line","keyword"}]}`. `file` is relative to `target/e2e-home`, and no line content is ever printed.
  - Reasons: `empty-scope` (no diagnostics file) and `schema-unreadable`. Exit 0, 1, or 2 on usage error.

- **`gate --require <suite>[,<suite>…] [--artifacts <dir>]`** (default dir `target/agent-run/artifacts/`):
  - `--require` takes only the eight closed `suite` values other than `local-live` (`gate::SUITES`: `nextest-unit · nextest-integration · doctest · nextest-e2e · mutants · coverage · perf · fuzz-replay`); an empty list or any other value (`a11y` included) is usage `unknown-suite`.
  - Inputs:
    - `junit-<suite>.xml`. `run` copies the invocation's `nextest/ci/junit.xml` here right after each nextest invocation, because nextest overwrites that path on every invocation. For unit, integration, e2e and coverage the source is `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`: nextest's store stays workspace-root-relative under `cargo llvm-cov nextest` too, and `target/llvm-cov-target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` never exists (as measured at chunk 2026-09-24-quality-gates, research.md M6: llvm-cov 0.9.1, nextest 0.9.133). `run` deletes the source before each invocation. If the file is missing afterwards, that is an `artifact-missing` breach, never a copy of an earlier run's file.
    - `run-summary.json`. Every `run` also writes its stdout document here, merged by `suite` across invocations.
    - the `mutants` suite in `run-summary.json` (its `survived` = missed − host-excluded + timeout from the run's own `mutants.out/outcomes.json`, under the host scratch on a Windows host)
    - `llvm-cov-summary.json`, from `cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only`
    - `perf-<hook>.json`, from hyperfine `--export-json`
  - A breach is any of:
    - a `--require`d suite is absent from `run-summary.json`, has `failed > 0`, or has `skipped > 0`
    - coverage below §10, each floor its own breach
    - the `mutants` suite's `survived > 0`.
    - a required perf JSON that is missing, unreadable or whose `.results[0].max` is at or over its §10 gate. The five rows `perf-session-start.json`, `perf-user-prompt-submit.json`, `perf-stop.json`, `perf-session-end.json` and `perf-pre-tool-use.json` (the one const `perf::ROWS`, re-exported as `run::PERF_ROWS`) are required by name, each absent one its own `artifact-missing` breach naming that file; every present `perf-*.json` is judged `.results[0].max <` `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` (1.0 s), the product constant `gate.rs` `perf()` imports; the breach text is `{file} max {max} >= {bound}`. A missing artifact is a breach, never a pass.
  - Output: `{"v":1,"cmd":"gate","ok":<bool>,"breaches":[{"gate":"suite-missing"|"suite-failed"|"suite-skipped"|"coverage"|"mutants"|"perf"|"artifact-missing","suite":<name|null>,"detail":<string>}]}`. `detail` is a fixed code or a count, never file content: `absent`, `no-run-summary`, `failed N`, `skipped N`, `survived N`, `lines 84.99 < 85`, `<metric> unreadable`, `junit-<suite>.xml`, `llvm-cov-summary.json`, `perf-<hook>.json` (the absent row's file) or `<file> max X >= 1`.
  - Exit 0 with no breaches, 1 on any breach, 2 on usage error.
  - CI runs `gate` as the last step of every test-running job, with `--require` set to exactly the suites that job ran (`coverage,doctest` in the per-OS `test` job). No CI job gates `mutants`. The per-job lists live in `ci.yml`. In the per-OS `test` job, `target/agent-run/` (including `artifacts/`, minus `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`) leaves CI only in obs-plan §9's scan-gated `harness-${{ matrix.os }}` artifact (`path` `target/agent-run/` plus `!target/agent-run/chunk.diff`; `if: failure() && steps.secret-scan.outcome == 'success'`). There is no unscanned `agent-run-<os>` upload.

- **`pre-push`** (the operator pass's local Linux gate; Linux host only, forwarded by both shims, not an agent command — the 5-command surface is unchanged):
  - When: the operator pass runs it on the uncommitted tree before the pre-CI commit, and a red stage stops the pass.
  - Runs natively on the Linux host, in the working tree itself (no clone, no sync), every child `/usr/bin/env -i HOME=<home> PATH=<home>/.cargo/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin <argv>` from the repository root (every PATH component a constant under the home or a system dir, carrying no host value; no inherited environment, so no `CLAUDE*` value crosses). `<home>` is the passwd entry's field 6, read by two probes that carry only `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` (`id -u`, then `getent passwd <uid>`); the harness's own `$HOME` is never read for it.
  - Stages, fail-fast in order, the document naming the one it reached: `host` (off Linux → exit 2 `pre-push-linux-only`) · `tools` (the passwd home, `cc`, `rustc` / cargo-nextest / cargo-mutants / cargo-llvm-cov at the pins read from `rust-toolchain.toml` and the §9 `test`-job `tool:` line) · `linux-tests` (`run --coverage`, then `gate --require coverage,doctest`), the last stage: `ok:true` when it is green. No stage runs mutation (retired 2026-09-28); `tools` keeps the cargo-mutants pin because `run --coverage` runs the real-cargo-mutants harness tests. The other OSes are CI's alone.
  - It prints `{"v":1,"cmd":"pre-push","ok":<bool>,"reason"?,"detail"?,"stage",linux{run,gate}}` — codes, counts and repo-relative names only, never a home or repository path. Exit 0 when every stage is green, 1 on a red stage or a stop reason, 2 on `pre-push-linux-only` or usage.

- **Closed enums:**
  - `run` `suite`: the nine values in `run` Output format (`local-live` only under `--local-live`, by the verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness chunk). `gate` `--require` takes the other eight. `local-live` failure codes: `build`, `verify-exit-<n>`, `verify-exit-none`, `row-missing`.
  - `boot` readiness missing codes: `<name>:run-process-start`, `<name>:child-process-start`, `<name>:snapshot`, `<name>:endpoint`, `<name>:heartbeat`, `<name>:events` (the start records, by the verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness chunk).
  - `status.last_error`: `null`, `list-exit-<code>`, `list-exit-none` (no exit code, no spawn or no `supervise.json`; by chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs).
  - `run --mutants` `mutants.verdict`: `counted`, `scoped` (`--file`), `no-rust-delta`, `test-only-rust-delta`, `package` (`--package`, by the mutation-scoring-completion chunk).
  - `run` `reason` added by the quality-gates chunk: `fuzz-linux-only` (exit 2), `tool-missing`, `corpus-empty`; by the Epoch 2 cleanup chunk: `scratch-refused`, `scratch-wipe-failed` (the Windows-host mutation scratch); by the verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness chunk: `live-in-ci` (exit 2); by the mutation-scoring-completion chunk: `package-refused` (exit 2). Usage `detail`: `unknown-suite`.
  - `schema-check` `reason`: `empty-scope`, `schema-unreadable`. `secret-scan` `reason`: `empty-scope`. `secret-scan` hit `class`: `claude-stripped`, `cookie`, `content-canary`, `mode`, `unreadable`.
  - `pre-push`: `cmd` `pre-push`. `reason`: `pre-push-linux-only` (exit 2), `tool-missing` (reused), `tool-pin-mismatch`, `linux-document-unreadable`. `detail`: `passwd-home` (`tool-missing`), `cc`, `rustc`, `cargo-nextest`, `cargo-mutants`, `cargo-llvm-cov`, `pins-unreadable`, and `run` / `gate` (the harness command whose document was unreadable). `stage`: `host`, `tools`, `linux-tests`. Retired with the WSL gate by the mutation-scoring-completion chunk: `pre-push-windows-only`, `sync-failed`, `sync-mismatch`, the details `wsl-distro-ubuntu`, `source-path`, `patch`, `clone`, `fetch`, `reset`, `clean`, `apply`, `cache`, and the stages `sync`, `cache`, `vm-release`, `windows-tests`.
  - A new value needs a Decisions Log entry.

title: Status endpoint shape
Status endpoint shape

body: This is the `agent-run status` document. Its nested `list` member is the verbatim `viola list --json` document (see Section 1, Status endpoint shape).

```json
{
  "v": 1, "cmd": "status", "ok": true,
  "state": "ready | degraded | down",
  "pid": null,
  "uptime_ms": null,
  "last_error": "null | <harness code: list-exit-<code> (e.g. list-exit-21) | list-exit-none>",
  "list": "<viola list --json document>",
  "instances": [{ "name": "<ViolaName>", "wrapper_pid": "<pid>", "alive": "<pid + start-time liveness>" }]
}
```

`status` runs `viola list` since chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs (5-command `status`). `state` is `ready` when `list` exits 0 and every booted instance is an item `wrapped:true, liveness:"live"` (an unwrapped item is ignored; a session that booted none reads `ready`). It is `degraded` when a booted instance is `stale` or absent (a gone instance is omitted from `list`), or the document holds no `items`. It is `down` when `list` exits non-zero (`last_error` `list-exit-<code>`), gives no exit code, cannot be spawned or has no `supervise.json` to run from (`list-exit-none`), or exits 0 with no JSON object on stdout (`list-exit-0`, `list:null`). `list` is the parsed document, the exit-21 error document included; `pid` and `uptime_ms` stay `null`; `instances` keeps the pid + start-time `alive`. `ok` is true only for `ready`; the exit is 0 for `ready`, 1 otherwise, 2 for an unknown session. The agent polls this document through the `status` command to verify state transitions during E2E scenarios.

title: Log format

body:
- **Format:** JSON-per-line. There are two streams:
  - **Event stream:** product events in `instances/<name>/events.ndjson`, exactly the arch Event line `{"v":1,"ts","instance","kind","source":"hook|wrapper|cli","data"}`.
  - **Process logs:** emitted by tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 `fmt().json().flatten_event(true).with_current_span(false)`, writing codes-only lines to `<home>/diagnostics/{run-<name>,hook-<name>,mcp,cli-<name>}.ndjson`. Content-bearing detail (chains, drift reports, panic payload and backtrace) goes only to `<home>/instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-<process>.ndjson` (obs-plan D-08). Files are 0600, dirs 0700, with one `write` per line.

- **Required fields:**
  - For process logs: `timestamp` (RFC 3339 UTC with ms and `Z`), `level` (`DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR`), `target`, and `fields.message` (or the flattened `message`).
  - `event`, a closed kebab-case enum. A new value needs a Decisions Log entry, like the §3 closed enums. Each value fixes what its `corr` holds:
    - `channel-request`, `channel-response`: `corr` = the JSON-RPC request `id`; null for an id-less `hook.event` notification and on a response to a frame that yielded no id (`error_code` -32700 or -32600)
    - `dialog-raised`, `dialog-answered`: `corr` = `dialog_id`
    - `hook-invoked`, `hook-decision`: `corr` = `dialog_id` for dialog hooks, otherwise null. A dialog `hook-invoked` may still be null (fail-open before `dialog_id` is known, obs-plan D-07), and so may a `hook-decision` that carries `detail`
    - `send-issued`, `send-confirmed`, `send-refused`: `corr` = the send `cursor`. A send refused before `send-issued` (`human-typing`, `budget-paused`, `input-not-ready`, `turn-running`) has no arch cursor, so its wrapper-side `send-refused` carries `corr` = the target's `events.ndjson` end offset at the moment of refusal, a log join key only, never returned to the caller (obs-plan D-28). Wrapper-side `send-*` lines also carry `conn` and `rpc_id`, the originating `send` request's connection and JSON-RPC `id`, so `(conn, rpc_id)` joins them to that call's `channel-*` lines (obs-plan D-30). The client-side `send-refused{side:"client"}` has `corr` null.
    - `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` requires `corr` exactly where the rules above always define it: `dialog-raised`, `dialog-answered`, `release-from-driver`; `channel-request` unless `method` is `hook.event`; `channel-response` unless `error_code` ∈ {-32700, -32600}; `send-*` when `side` is `wrapper`; `hook-decision` when `hook_event` ∈ {`pre-tool-use`, `permission-request`} and no `detail`. `hook-invoked` never requires it.
    - `release-from-driver`: `corr` = the JSON-RPC request `id` (obs-plan D-01; the wrapper's `-32602` refusal of a `release` that carries a string `from`; a `from` of another type is a plain `-32602` with no `release-from-driver` line)
    - `process-start`, `process-exit`, `panic`: `corr` = null
    - `state-recovered`, `parse-rejected`: `corr` = null (obs-plan D-03, D-05)
  - `process` (`run|hook|mcp|cli`; `cli` is a short-lived verb with a resolved instance, writing `cli-<name>.ndjson`, obs-plan D-06) and `instance` (a `ViolaName` or null).
  - `corr` is copied unchanged as a JSON number or string. It is never renamed (for example to `correlation_id`).
  - **Null encoding:** a null `corr` or `instance` is written as key **absence** (tracing has no null field value; obs-plan D-12). The harness and every `jq` / jaq assertion treat an absent key and `null` as the same value (`.corr == null` holds for both), and obs-plan's `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` rejects a literal `null`.

  obs-plan may add fields but must not rename or remove these. The harness greps on them.

- **Constraints:**
  - The hook trace is the `hook-<name>.ndjson` file. A failed write there is swallowed, so the hook still exits 0 and never writes to stderr.
  - No line may contain a `Cookie` header or any stripped `CLAUDE*` value. This is enforced by the secret-scan test in §6.

- **Agent parsing:** lines parseable with `jq -c 'select(.event=="dialog-raised")'` or equivalent; NEVER multi-line stack traces. A panic in a hook is caught and logged as one `level:"ERROR", event:"panic"` line.

title: PID file
PID file

body: - **Location:** N/A as a product pid file, per test-scope Sec 3. Product pids are in `<home>/instances/<name>/snapshot.json` (`pid`, `started_at`, `child_pid`) with liveness in `<home>/instances/<name>/heartbeat`. The harness's own process record is `target/agent-run/<session>/session.json` (`supervisor_pid`, `wrapper_pid`).

- **Lifecycle:**
  - `session.json` is written by `boot` once readiness passes.
  - It is read by `status`, `logs` and `cleanup`.
  - Kill targets are always verified by pid + start time via sysinfo 0.39.6 before signalling, so a reused pid is never killed.
  - `session.json` is removed by `cleanup`.

title: Test data bootstrap

body: - **Strategy:** self-bootstrapping (no developer-seeded data)

- **Mechanism:**
  - a tempfile 3.27.0 home per test or session
  - rstest 0.27.0 `#[fixture]` chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper`
  - fake-agent replay of `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/`
  - `viola verify --home <home>` against the fake agent for stamps
  - generated statusline stdin piped into `viola hook statusline` for `budget.json`
  - proptest 1.11.0 strategies with committed `proptest-regressions/` seeds for randomized inputs
  - Windows x64, root tests only: `tests/support/home.rs` `seed_conpty(home)` places the two ConPTY companions under `<home>/bin/<key>/conpty/` from the per-run `target/conpty-seed/<key>/` copy before the test's `viola run` (the §5 carve-out), making the home and the seed dir through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` first; the companions are hard links to one shared seed file, so an inheritable grant on a seeded home or its `bin/` reaches the shared companion and every seeded home, and a test that widens a home tree above `bin/<key>/conpty/` starts that home unseeded; the harness `boot`, `run_viola_unseeded` starts and `tests/conpty_sideload.rs` never seed
  - `tests/support/home.rs` `TestHome::outside_scan()`: a home under the system temp dir (`viola-chaos-*`), used only by `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` (the §5 second carve-out, the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer)
  - `tests/support/home.rs` `prepare_home_base(base)`, called from `TestHome::new`, prepares the root chain's base `target/e2e-home` before the `tempdir_in`, under the contract of the harness keeper `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` (`boot` step 2): a plain base is created as a directory; on Unix a linked base needs an absolute target, which is made with mode 0700 when it is gone and accepted only when one `lstat` reads a real, owner-only directory; on Windows it is the plain create. A refusal panics with a fixed message that names the failed check and no path. A linked base whose filesystem reads less than `HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB` (9 GiB) free by `statvfs` (`f_bavail × f_frsize`) is refused too, its fixed message `e2e-home backing: {free} MiB free, below the {floor} MiB floor` holding the two counts and no path; the decision is the plain function `headroom_refusal(free, floor_mib)`, unit-tested on every OS, and the floor one compiled constant equal to the harness keeper's, set by no variable, flag or config key, its basis the tmpfs's EDQUOT reading of about 8 GiB free plus 1 GiB (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup/evidence/headroom.md`). A plain base reads no headroom. On the Linux dev host the base is an operator-set link to `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>` (0700, tmpfs), an environment fact outside harness code; the path string is unchanged, and `viola` is given a `--home` under the link and resolves nothing

- **Per-test isolation:**
  - Every test gets a fresh home, so no endpoint, log or `budget.json` is shared: the FNV-1a endpoint hash includes the absolute home path.

- **Cleanup:** a root `TestHome` removes its home on drop through `tests/support/home.rs` `remove_owned`, which deletes the `owner.json` record last: std's `remove_dir_all` stops at the first entry it cannot delete, in listing order, so a removal that stops part-way (a file another process still holds) keeps the record, and a later sweep can still take the dir. A test the runner kills (nextest's slow-timeout kill, or a mutant that kills the test process; the `mutants` profile's `terminate = "wait"` lets every other running test finish) never drops its home, so every root `TestHome` records `owner.json` `{pid, started_at}` beside it, and a new `TestHome`, when no `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_*` is set, first removes, through the same `remove_owned`, only the dirs whose recorded owner process is gone (pid dead, or alive with another start time) — never by age or name, never a dir without a record; a kept home drops its record. Ownerless remnants still appear on runs that fail at the D: dev volume's deadlines, as measured at chunk 2026-10-02-epoch-2b-cleanup `evidence/leaks.md` (0–3 per run, none on a C: copy); their mechanism is recorded, not established (M2, open). Harness sessions are cleared by `cleanup`. A failing root test keeps its home only when `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`, so that `logs` can inspect the home. viola-e2e's booted lifecycle tests (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs`) hold a `Booted` guard instead: on drop, even after a failed assertion, it runs `cleanup(.., keep_homes = true)` (every recorded process stopped, the home kept; the tests' own cleanup calls assert `home_removed:"kept"`) and then removes the home unless `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1` and the thread is panicking — `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` is not read there, so a passing test's home is always removed. In CI, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` (set by `ci.yml`, overridden to `0` under `run --mutants`) keeps every rstest home, passing or failing, and makes harness `cleanup` keep its home (§3 `cleanup` step 5). The homes then stay under `target/e2e-home/` until obs-plan's G2, G4, secret scan and scan-gated uploads have run; the one `outside_scan()` chaos home is outside those scans by design. On the Linux dev host, through the `target/e2e-home` link, a `TestHome`'s drop and the owner sweep delete outside the working directory, in `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, still only dirs the test side itself created (by `owner.json` record, by its own `TempDir`); the widening is ratified by the founder (live, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer). A home kept there (`AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`) is on tmpfs: it does not survive a reboot, and `/tmp` ages out what is untouched for ten days, so `logs` can inspect it only until then. After a reboot the link's target is gone and the next start makes it again (the keepers). After `cargo clean` the link is gone and the next start puts a plain directory on the shared volume with no signal: `test -L target/e2e-home && findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T target/e2e-home/` reads it, and one `ln -s` restores it.

title: Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project)

body:
The downstream skills derive the following bootstrap phases from
the contract above. Listed for explicitness. route may reorder or
combine them, and setup-project may add stack-specific intermediate steps.

- **test-runner-install:**
  - Install cargo-nextest 0.9.146 via taiki-e/install-action (SHA-pinned) in CI, or `cargo install --locked` locally.
  - Add `.config/nextest.toml` with:
    - `[profile.ci]`: `junit.path = "junit.xml"`, `retries = 0`, `slow-timeout = { period = "30s", terminate-after = 4 }`, `fail-fast = false`, plus two `[[profile.ci.overrides]]`, the first matching winning: `filter = 'test(/verify_window_/)'` at `slow-timeout = { period = "20s", terminate-after = 3 }` (a 60 s kill; the class holds three cases: the no-screen case waits out the gate's 8.5 s maximum four times by design, 34.3 s on the dev host and up to 35.3 s on the CI legs as measured at chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint, and `verify_window_paste_hint_past_the_gate_maximum_still_stamps` holds a cleared screen for 9 s after a long paste's Stop, 13.1 s to 13.7 s on the CI legs at that chunk, and since chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup the harness test `verify_window_boot_with_an_unknown_cli_version_is_verify_failed` (`crates/viola-e2e`), whose verify makes four interactive runs against a CLI version with no fixture set, each waiting out the gate maximum: 8577, 8561, 8563 and 8562 ms, the test passing in 34.482 s under profile `ci`, as measured on the dev host at that chunk; by its name it takes this 60 s kill, where it took the profile's 120 s), then the twenty-six verify-driven binaries (the `binary(…)` names on that filter line: `channel_endpoint channel_error_bodies channel_links chaos_forward_compat chaos_torn_append cli_answer cli_budget cli_error_bodies cli_fake_agent cli_instance_state cli_links cli_list cli_send cli_verify cli_version_gate cli_wheel conpty_sideload contract_fake_agent_drift contract_ledger_probes cross_exit_causes cross_list_rows hook_statusline mcp_tools path1_run_start security_negatives_socket_dir tui_wheel`, as `.config/nextest.toml` reads; `channel_links` (`tests/channel_links.rs`) joined there, each of its cases booting a wrapper (`booted_wrapper`); `mcp_tools` (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs`) joined at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers, its cases starting from a stamped harness session and reading 0.01–5.9 s, while `path6_budget_harness`, also a stamped harness session, is not on the line; `path1_run_start` joined at chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs, its one case starting from `stamped_home`, and `cross_list_rows`, on the line before that chunk, was missing from this list; `hook_statusline` joined at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through, because five of its cases start from a stamped home, `cli_budget` at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor, every one of whose cases starts from one, and `cli_links` at chunk 2026-10-10-session-links, each of whose five cases starts from one; `cli_list` at chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list, every case but the two `cfg(unix)` refusals and the absent-home case starting from one, and with it `chaos_forward_compat` and `chaos_torn_append`, which start from one since that chunk's CI fix; `channel_error_bodies` and `cli_error_bodies` on it because each one's witness starts from `stamped_home`) at `{ period = "10s", terminate-after = 2 }` (a 20 s kill). This is the `verify_window_` class grown to every verify-driven test (the overseer's founder-delegated decision, 2026-10-05): a test that drives `viola verify` (`support::verify::verify`, and through it `stamped_home` / `dialogless_home`) has no test-side bound on that call, and the per-test kill is its bound, sized from the measured floor (verify's four interactive runs, seven 300 ms settles when it was sized: about 1.0 s → 2.1 s median on the ubuntu coverage leg) plus a 3x runner tail. Since chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows Run B's three added turns make it ten 300 ms waits; the longest verify-driven test under the 20 s kill read 9.98 s on that leg in ci#37534758441 (`fake_agent_dialog_replay_matches_every_recorded_dialog_set`, one verify per recorded set), and no bound moved. Since chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row Run B makes four added turns (the newline paste joined); that chunk's integration entry read 34.69 s against 35.4 s at its plan review, and no kill line moved. Since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows verify makes a fifth interactive run, Run E (one start and one settle after its SessionStart); in the no-screen `verify_window_` case Run E's settle waits out the gate maximum once more by design, 34.42 s → 42.98 s on the dev host at that chunk, against the class's 60 s kill (the `mutants` profile's too), and no kill line moved; with no fixture set Run E has no Run B SessionStart to resume and spawns nothing, so the unknown-CLI-version harness case still makes four interactive runs.   - ripgrep 15.2.0 (PCRE2), the G1/G3 gate tool, comes from `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh` in the `lint` job. The script downloads the official release asset, checks it against the sha256 its release publishes, installs it idempotently into `target/tools/ripgrep/bin`, and prints `tool-missing: <tool>` when a tool it needs is absent. taiki-e/install-action `7623a79…` has no ripgrep manifest.

- **quality-gate-config-emit:** emit `.github/workflows/ci.yml` enforcing:

  - `retries = 0`
  - hyperfine `max` gates

  - `viola-harness gate --require <that job's suites>` as the last step of every job that runs a harness suite (§3 Internal harness subcommands); `lint`, `supply-chain` and `release` are plain exit-code jobs with no gate step

route uses this list to plan phase ordering (typically:
test-runner-install → 5-command-discipline-wire → status-endpoint-implement
→ log-format-bind-with-obs → pid-file-commitment-wire →
test-data-bootstrap-wire → coverage-tooling-install → ci-tool-install →
quality-gate-config-emit). setup-project uses this list to materialize
each phase's bootstrap script + dependency list + verification
command. Ownership:
- This plan is the binding source for the harness-grepped log fields and the `agent-run status` shape.

## 2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton — mutation gate prebuilds the root bins (post-commit CI fix)
**Section:** §3 `run` step 4 (Command)
**Change:** `run --mutants` first runs `cargo build --package viola --features fake-agent`, which fails with `reason:"build-failed"`, and then passes `--copy-target=true` to cargo-mutants, so the scratch tree carries the root `viola` / `viola-fake-agent` bins that the harness tests spawn.

The operator chose prebuild + copy-target (founder-delegated). Cost: one `target/` copy per run, 2.9 GB on the dev host.

## 2026-09-24-fake-agent-and-test-data-fixtures — mutation verdict for Rust-free diffs
**Section:** §3 `run` step 4 (Classification bullet added; Verdict scoped to the `counted` arm) · §3 `run` Output format (`mutants` object) · §3 Closed enums (`mutants.verdict`) · §10 Mutation gate · §12 Decisions Log (new entry)
**Change:**

## 2026-10-04-windows-boundary-mutation-workflow — the mutants profile waits for running tests
**Section:** §3 → Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project) · §3 → Test data bootstrap (Cleanup)

The 38 are 17 kill-path leftovers by design and 21 half-removed fixture git repos (a `terminate`-independent class). A full Linux viola-e2e run takes 78 m against 23 m, counts identical.
- Cleanup: the killed-test example was "nextest `terminate = \"immediate\"`"; it now names the slow-timeout kill or a mutant-made kill, with `wait` letting every other running test finish.

## 2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume — the home base's keepers and the dev host's tmpfs backing
**Section:** §3 → 5-command implementation (`boot` step 2, `run --local-live`, `cleanup` step 6, `logs` Retention window) · §3 → Test data bootstrap (Mechanism, Cleanup) · §5 Integration Test Strategy → Setup / teardown lifecycle
**Change:**
- `boot` step 2: the base `target/e2e-home` is prepared before the `tempdir_in` by `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home`. A plain base is created as a directory; on Unix a linked base needs an absolute target, made 0700 when gone (one non-recursive create) and accepted only when one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit; Windows is the plain create. A refused base reads `reason:"build-failed"`; no reason added.
- `run --local-live`: the keeper runs after the build and before the verify. `verify-exit-none` was "no exit code"; now "no exit code, or a base the keeper refused, the verify not started". The four failure codes are unchanged.
- `cleanup` step 6: on the Linux dev host the `viola-session-*` removal goes through the link and deletes outside the working directory, only the dir the harness created.
- `logs` Retention window and Test data bootstrap Cleanup: on the dev host a kept home (`AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`) is on tmpfs: gone at a reboot, aged out of `/tmp` after ten untouched days. Cleanup also: a `TestHome`'s drop and the owner sweep delete through the link; after a reboot the next start re-makes the target; after `cargo clean` the link is gone and `test -L target/e2e-home && findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T target/e2e-home/` reads it.
- Test data bootstrap Mechanism: `prepare_home_base`, called from `TestHome::new`, holds the same contract and panics with a fixed message naming the failed check and no path.
- §5: the `tempdir_in("<workspace root>/target/e2e-home")` statement holds by path; on the dev host the path is an operator-set link to `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`. Not a third carve-out: these homes stay inside G2, G4 and the secret scan. No CI runner has a link; the pinned copy's `sync_all()` is unchanged.
**Why:** a start's pinned copy stalled behind other builders' writes; the backing was proved in one natural window at this chunk. The removals outside the working directory are a boundary widening, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, live, relayed by the overseer. Standing rule: a stalled-start red is a finding about the backing, stopped on and reported, never re-run for green; no kill, `WITHIN` or retry moved.
**Kept:** the two existing carve-outs and every CI statement about kept homes stand as written; the `--local-live` bullet's row list was not touched.

## 2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade — `run --mutants` leaves host-excluded missed mutants out and names them in `host_excluded`
**Section:** §3 → 5-command implementation (`run` step 4 Verdict · Exit code semantics · Output format · `gate`) · §3 → Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project) · §2 Test Strategy (Mutation row) · §10 Build failure conditions · §11 Test Anti-Patterns → Quality
**Change:**
- Verdict: the run's own `outcomes.json` is read by record first. A record whose summary is `MissedMutant` and whose whole span sits under a `cfg` predicate proved false for the host the harness was built for (on a node covering the span, or on the `mod` declaration that brings the file in) is host-excluded: it leaves the missed count, `survived` and `failures`; `tested` still counts it. Decided keys: `unix`, `windows`, `target_family`, `target_os`, `target_arch`; any other key is unknown; `not` / `all` / `any` are three-valued. The host's facts are compile-time constants. A caught, unviable or timed-out record is never left out, and anything the reader cannot read keeps the mutant counted. The requirement is `missed − host-excluded == 0 && timeout == 0 && unviable <= caught` (was `missed == 0 && …`).
- `survived` = missed − host-excluded + timeout (was missed + timeout), in Output format and in `gate`'s `run-summary.json` line.
- Output format: a counted, scoped or package `mutants` object carries `"host_excluded"`, an array of `{"name","cfg"}`, repo-relative and never an absolute path, only when at least one mutant was left out.
- Exit code semantics, §2's Mutation row, §10's failure condition and §11's ban each read "missed" as missed beyond the host-excluded ones. §11 also bans trusting cargo-mutants' summary line, which still counts a left-out mutant as missed.
- Bootstrap phases: `viola-e2e`'s dependency line gains syn `=2.0.119` and proc-macro2 `=1.0.107`.
**Why:** the chunk moved the classification of mutants a host never compiles from a hand record into the harness, so that zero missed reads over the measurable set without an argued list. The harness document, not cargo-mutants' own lines, is the verdict.
**Kept:** `unviable <= caught` and `unviable-exceeds-caught` are judged as before. No `verdict`, `reason`, `suite` or `event` value is added, and `suites[]` keeps its field names. Founder Direction 1's words ("surviving mutants are red") stand; they read true under the new `survived`.

**Section:** §3 → Test data bootstrap (test-data-bootstrap.md: Mechanism, the Windows x64 seed) · §5 Integration Test Strategy (test-plan.md and integration-test-strategy.md: Setup / teardown lifecycle, the seed carve-out) · §7 Test Data & Fixtures (test-data-fixtures.md: On-disk product state; a new row, A widened seeded home (Windows x64))

- `seed_conpty` makes the home and the seed dir `target/conpty-seed/<key>/` through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` (owner-only modes and DACL) before `bin/<key>/conpty/`, so a seeded home passes `check_instance` and, on windows-2025, the three `hook_statusline` cases pass. Was "a home that seed made is not one viola created … `hook statusline`'s instance check refuses it", per "2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through — the fake agent's statusline options, the reader's property and seeds, the stamped-home rule on Windows, three counts", and "a seeded home skips [viola's own home DACL], so that entry owns making the seed let viola create the home first (route CARRY)", per "2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty — the Windows x64 seeded-home carve-out"; that CARRY is gone from the body.
- The companions are hard links to one shared seed file: an inheritable `icacls` grant (`(OI)(CI)`) on a seeded home or its `bin/` reaches the shared `target/conpty-seed/<key>/` companion and widens every seeded home until removed, so a test that widens a home tree above `bin/<key>/conpty/` starts that home unseeded (`run_refuses_a_widened_home_tree_before_its_log`), as measured on windows-2025. The new §7 row holds it, per-test; the §5 master carve-out reads "into a home `seed_conpty` makes private" with the unseeded rule.
**Why:** the chunk's `seed_conpty` makes the home and the seed dir with `create_private_dir`, and the seeded homes passed on the green Windows leg; the two red Windows runs measured the grant reaching every seeded home through the hard links, and the fix commit started that test's home unseeded.

## 2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity — the start's and verify's home-tree checks before any log
**Section:** §1 Test Scope Summary (test-plan.md: Critical paths, Path 1; test-scope-summary.md: Path `run` start sequence and its signals) · §6 E2E Test Strategy (e2e-test-strategy.md: Path 1; the Exit-cause matrix, exit 1 for `run` and for `revive`; test-plan.md: Exit-cause matrix) · §5 Integration Test Strategy (integration-test-strategy.md: On-disk, a new item)
**Change:**
- Path 1: the start runs `check_home_tree` before the wrapper log opens: the home (read rule), `check_instance`'s set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, then `bin/<key>/`, the pinned copy, `plugin/<key>/`, its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists. A refused tree exits 1 with the home pair, or the instance pair when the refusal is at instance level, opens no log, writes no line and starts no child. Was a sequence opening at the collision check, its exit-1 list ending at a tampered pinned exe; now a refused home tree joins it.
- `tests/run_cli.rs` `run_refuses_a_widened_home_tree_before_its_log`: after one clean start, a 0770 home or a widened `instances/<name>`, `bin/` or pinned copy refuses the next `viola run` before its log, the widening as found. `tests/cli_verify.rs` `verify_refuses_a_widened_ledger_before_any_step`: a widened `ledger/` on a stamped home refuses `viola verify` with the home pair, no step line or summary, `stamps.json` byte for byte.
- Exit 1, `run`: "the `--home` fails strict-modes at `run`" now names the home-tree check, a read-granted pre-existing home included on every OS, and beside it `viola verify` over a refused home tree (the home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`); the master's matrix names `tests/run_cli.rs` and `tests/cli_verify.rs` for these exit-1 refusals.
- Exit 1, `revive`: its strict-modes cause also covers the home, the instance directory or its `diagnostics/` read by another user (`cfg(unix)`), and the start arm runs `run`'s home-tree check before the wrapper log (under `--json` the `strict-modes-failed` document).
**Why:** the chunk's `run` and `revive`'s start check the tree before `open_wrapper_log`, and `verify` checks the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its log; the report reads the criterion met on the entry's binaries and the unit tier.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-26T21-34-52-wrap/

**Section:** §4 Unit Test Strategy (unit-test-strategy.md: viola-state, the Snapshot envelope and server check items, a new replayed-readers item; test-plan.md: viola-state, root bin) · §6 E2E Test Strategy (e2e-test-strategy.md: Path 6, step 6) · §1 Test Scope Summary (test-scope-summary.md: Path `run` start sequence, the collision check; Path budget governor, the statusline signal)

**Why:** the founder's own answer to the chunk's P4 fork Q1 (inputs#I3, live by dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer) moved the readers now, his boundary-widening ratification; the wrap's halt confirmed these items on the overseer's founder-delegated answer (inputs#I6, PROVISIONAL), the ratification staying his inputs#I3.

**Section:** §6 E2E Test Strategy (test-plan.md: Scenario E5, Verification signal and As landed; Chaos suite; e2e-test-strategy.md: the E5 procedure; Chaos suite) · §1 Test Scope Summary (test-scope-summary.md: the chaos trigger, snapshot corruption) · §2 Test Strategy (test-strategy.md: the trigger map's Filesystem (V7) row, E5)
**Change:**
- As landed: was "in part", steps 1–3 unbuilt while the collision check called `read_snapshot`, the readers' move a CARRY owed to the route entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity", per "2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame — E5 steps 1–3 and the three other snapshot readers, held on "Home and code-bearing file integrity""; now "built": steps 1–3 run as `tests/chaos_snapshot_replay.rs` (`a_start_over_an_unreadable_snapshot_replays_the_log`, `a_start_over_a_replayed_snapshot_and_a_fresh_beat_refuses_already_live`). The replay's product readers were two and are six (`viola revive`, `viola list`'s `board::read`, hook `connect`, statusline `serve`, `run`'s collision check, `liveness::live_endpoint`), each after its strict-modes check; `read_snapshot` has no product caller under `src/`; the CARRY is gone.

The master's set-against note ("two of the signals above are set against what landed, for the entry that builds it to restate") is removed; the procedure's two signals read as built.
- Chaos suite: a start over a truncated or `v:99` snapshot replays the log, and a fresh beat over it refuses `already-live` (`chaos_snapshot_replay.rs`); the snapshot-corruption item and the V7 row name the file for steps 1–3.

## 2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity — a home a test makes before viola: `create_private_dir`, the plain home refused, the per-OS oracle
**Section:** §5 Integration Test Strategy (integration-test-strategy.md: Setup / teardown lifecycle; CLI, `cli_verify`) · §7 Test Data & Fixtures (test-plan.md: On-disk product state; test-data-fixtures.md: On-disk product state, a new seed-strategy item) · §1 Test Scope Summary (test-scope-summary.md: Test data strategy, a new constraint)
**Change:**
- A test that makes a home before viola makes it through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir`, never `create_dir_all`, as `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`, `tests/cli_machine_contract.rs` and `tests/tui_env_strip.rs` do: a `create_dir_all` home is refused, on Unix (0755) by the read rule, on windows-2025 `Writable`, the refused entry an inherited `S-1-5-32-545` (Users) write ACE (`strict_instance_refuses_a_plain_home_made_before_viola_and_names_the_entry`); that home's canonical SDDL is not recorded. Was "the refused home's DACL was not read, and that reading is owed to the working-route entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity"", per "2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through — the fake agent's statusline options, the reader's property and seeds, the stamped-home rule on Windows, three counts".
- A catch-site case holds a viola-made home with a regular file where the checked entry goes (`tests/cli_wait_last.rs`, `diagnostics/`; `tests/cli_verify.rs`, `ledger/`). A home planted under a regular file takes a per-OS oracle: on Unix a strict-modes refusal, exit 1 with the home pair; on Windows the path stats `NotFound`, the check skips it as absent and the catch-site line stands (`verify_under_a_regular_file_refuses_the_home`); `verify_under_a_regular_file_prints_only_the_internal_error_line` forces the catch-site line on every OS.
**Why:** the read rule now refuses a 0755 home; the Windows reading was measured on windows-2025, disproving the "not read" claim; the plain home's SDDL could not be recorded from a passing run, so the case asserts the refused ACE instead; the Windows `NotFound` stat came from the first red Windows run.

## 2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary — the `viola mcp` stdin line cap's tests
**Section:** §6 E2E Test Strategy (e2e-test-strategy.md: the ipc-internal (MCP stdio) row, the Security sweep) · §1 Test Scope Summary (test-scope-summary.md: the MCP surface's as-landed entries; test-plan.md: the security-vector-coverage (MCP) trigger) · §4 Unit Test Strategy (unit-test-strategy.md: a new viola-mcp group; test-plan.md: the viola-mcp bullet)
**Change:**
- §1: `viola mcp` reads stdin through `CappedLines` capped at `MAX_FRAME`; a line past the cap passes no byte, is never truncated or skipped, and ends the session as a stdin close does, with one `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin", detail:"oversize", count:1}` WARN line holding no byte of it; on an initialized session the earlier lines are answered, exit 0, stderr empty, stdout only the earlier frames. The MCP trigger's required tests add this negative.
- §6: `mcp_tools_a_line_past_max_frame_ends_the_session_with_one_line` (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs`) spawns and owns a `viola mcp` child from a fresh home, writes raw lines from its own writer thread (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, one line past `MAX_FRAME`, stdin left open), drains stdout and stderr on their own threads, awaits exit under an 8 s kill deadline: exit 0, stderr empty, stdout only the `initialize` response, exactly one such line in `mcp.ndjson`, valid against `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, the line's canary in no file under the home.
- §4, a new viola-mcp group: `stdin::tests` hold a line of exactly the cap whole, its `\n` counted, and one byte more releasing no byte, setting the cut flag and reading as end of stream, at the literal `16 * 1024 * 1024` too; the count restarts after each newline; a split over-long line is cut, a split fitting one joined (the six `capped_lines_*` cases); the `serve` child cases, each killed at 5 s: `serve_ends_the_session_at_a_line_past_max_frame`, `serve_on_a_closed_stdin_is_the_initialize_error`.
**Why:** rmcp 3.4.1's stdio transport reads each line unbounded, so the bound belongs to the reader viola hands it. A line is refused whole: a truncated one could dispatch a padded request, a skipped one leaves a request unanswered. Green on the three CI OSes (ci#40458923095).
